question: プレゼントはきれいな紙で ＿包んで＿ あった。
explanation:
包んで is read つつんで because 包む means "to wrap", fitting the description of a gift wrapped in pretty paper.
包む (つつむ) = to wrap, to envelop. Its て-form is 包 (つつ) んで. The sentence says 「プレゼントはきれいな紙 (かみ) で包 (つつ) んであった」 — "The present was wrapped in pretty paper." 包む describes surrounding something with paper, cloth, or any wrapping material. The kanji 包 contains 巳 (snake/coiled shape) inside 勹 (a wrapping figure) — the image of something coiled inside a wrapper.
✗ つづんで is not a real Japanese word. The correct て-form of 包む is つつんで (with unvoiced つ, not voiced づ). Voicing つ to づ is the main trap here.
✗ つうつんで inserts an extra long vowel う after the first つ. 包む reads つつむ — two short つ sounds, not つう. つうつんで is not a real word.
✗ つうづんで combines the long vowel insertion error (つう) and the voicing error (づ). Both parts are wrong.
例: 誕生日 (たんじょうび) のケーキをリボンで包 (つつ) んで渡 (わた) した。 — I wrapped the birthday cake with a ribbon and gave it as a gift.

question: 彼はダンスが ＿得意＿ だ。
explanation:
得意 is read とくい because both kanji take their on-yomi, forming the standard compound meaning "being good at / confident in."
得意 (とくい) is a na-adjective meaning "good at something" or "one's strong point." It carries a nuance of confidence and ease — you do this thing well and feel comfortable doing it. The compound uses the on-yomi of both kanji: 得 (とく) and 意 (い). 得 (とく) means "to gain" or "to be able to" and appears in words like 得点 (とくてん, score) and 納得 (なっとく, understanding). 意 (い) means "intention" or "feeling" and appears in 意見 (いけん, opinion) and 注意 (ちゅうい, attention). Together, 得意 (とくい) conveys the idea of "what one has naturally gained a feel for." The sentence says: "He is good at dance." The pattern X が得意 (とくい) だ = "X is one's strong point" is a fixed expression at N4–N3 level. The long vowel distinction is key: とく (two beats, と + く) not とう or どく. Beginners sometimes mistakenly add a long vowel, producing とうくい or どくい, neither of which is a real word.
✗ どおくい gives 得 a voiced reading どお that does not exist. 得 reads とく in this compound, not voiced どく and certainly not the elongated どお.
✗ とおくい inserts a long vowel after と, producing とお instead of とく. Long vowels matter in Japanese — とおい (遠い) means "far," a completely different word. 得 reads とく, a short syllable.
✗ どくい voices the first syllable as ど and shortens 得 incorrectly. The on-yomi of 得 is とく (unvoiced), not どく. どく has its own kanji (毒, poison), creating a very different meaning.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) は料理 (りょうり) が得意 (とくい) で、友達 (ともだち) によく作 (つく) ってあげる。 — She is good at cooking and often makes food for her friends.

question: 新しい星が ＿発見＿ された。
explanation:
発見 is read はっけん — 発 reads はっ (geminate) and 見 reads けん, meaning "discovery".
発見 (はっけん) = discovery — finding something new. 発 (はっ) = to emit/launch/discover, 見 (けん) = to see/observe. Together: seeing/finding for the first time. The sentence says 「新 (あたら) しい星 (ほし) が発見 (はっけん) された」 — "A new star was discovered." Note the geminate: 発 (はつ) + 見 (けん) → はっけん (the つ compresses before the k). 見 reads けん (on-yomi) in this compound, not the common kun-yomi み.
✗ はけん: drops the geminate — shortens はっ to は. 発 in 発見 reads はっ (with the double consonant), not は alone.
✗ はつけん: fails to geminate — keeps はつ fully. The compound 発 + 見 produces the geminate はっけん, not はつけん.
✗ ばつけん: voices 発 to ばつ. 発 reads はっ (unvoiced h/p), not ばつ (voiced b). ばつ belongs to 罰 (ばつ, penalty) or ×印 (ばつ, an X mark).
例: その科学者 (かがくしゃ) は新 (あたら) しい元素 (げんそ) を発見 (はっけん) した。 — The scientist discovered a new element.

question: このグラフは人口の変化を ＿表して＿ います。
explanation:
表して is read あらわして and means "represents / shows" — a graph showing population changes.
表す (あらわす) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to express", "to show", or "to represent". The te-form 表して (あらわして) here connects with います to form the continuous "is representing". The sentence 「このグラフは人口の変化を表しています」 means "This graph represents changes in population." The kanji 表 has two kun-yomi that learners sometimes confuse: あらわす (to express/show — transitive, used here) and おもて (the front/outside surface). The on-yomi ヒョウ appears in: 表現 (ひょうげん, expression), 表面 (ひょうめん, surface), 発表 (はっぴょう, presentation). When 表 appears as a verb, the reading is always あらわ.
✗ しめして is the te-form of 示す (しめす), meaning "to indicate / to point to". 示 and 表 overlap in meaning — both can describe showing information — but the kanji 表 reads あらわ, not しめ. 示す tends to be used for pointing something out directly.
✗ ふやして is the te-form of 増やす (ふやす), meaning "to increase". Increasing and representing are opposite concepts here — a graph does not increase population, it represents changes.
✗ うごかして is the te-form of 動かす (うごかす), meaning "to move / to operate". Moving and representing are unrelated in this context; 表 does not read うごか.
例: このグラフは過去 (かこ) 10年間 (じゅうねんかん) の気温 (きおん) の変化 (へんか) を表 (あらわ) している。 — This graph shows the changes in temperature over the past ten years.

question: 山田さんから、来週の会議の ＿件＿ で電話がありました。
explanation:
件 is read けん, a formal counter/noun for matters or cases — here meaning the matter of next week's meeting.
件 (けん) is a noun meaning "matter," "case," or "item" — used for something that needs attention or discussion, often in a formal or business context. It uses the on-yomi けん. The sentence says: "There was a phone call from Yamada-san about the matter 件 (けん) of next week's meeting." 来週の会議の件 (らいしゅうのかいぎのけん) = "regarding the matter of next week's meeting" is a standard formal expression used in business Japanese. 件 also appears in 事件 (じけん, incident/case), 条件 (じょうけん, condition/terms), and 件数 (けんすう, number of cases). The four distractors — あん (案, plan/proposal), ほう (法/方, law/method), and よう (用/様, need/manner) — are all common single-kanji options that can appear in similar business contexts, but each carries a different nuance. けん specifically refers to a matter/case being discussed; it does not mean a plan (案), a method (ほう), or a need (よう).
✗ あん is the reading of 案 (あん), meaning "plan," "proposal," or "idea." A plan and a case/matter are different: 案 is about something proposed, while 件 is about a matter that needs handling. The sentence says a phone call came about the meeting — it is a matter (件), not a plan (案).
✗ ほう could be the reading of 方 (ほう, direction/way) or 法 (ほう, law). Neither fits here — the sentence is about a specific meeting matter, not a method or law.
✗ よう could be the reading of 用 (よう, use/need/errand) or 様 (よう, manner/appearance). 用がある means "to have something to attend to / to have business." While close in feel, 件 (けん) specifically refers to a case or matter, while 用 (よう) refers to an errand or need. The sentence says the call was regarding a specific matter (件), not about having a general need.
例: 先ほどのご連絡 (ごれんらく) の件 (けん) について、確認 (かくにん) させてください。 — Regarding the matter of your earlier message, please allow me to confirm.

question: ＿通勤＿ にとても時間がかかります。
explanation:
通勤 is read つうきん and means "commuting to work".
通勤 (つうきん) is an on-yomi compound: 通 (ツウ, pass through / communicate) + 勤 (キン, work / attend). Together the word means "going to and from work" — the daily commute. The sentence 「通勤にとても時間がかかります」 means "Commuting takes a very long time." Both kanji use their on-yomi. 通 (ツウ) appears in many passage-related words: 通路 (つうろ, passageway), 交通 (こうつう, traffic), 通訳 (つうやく, interpretation). 勤 (キン) appears in work-related words: 勤務 (きんむ, duty/service), 出勤 (しゅっきん, going to work). This compound is a classic N3 vocabulary item because it tests whether learners distinguish ツウキン from the similarly-spelled distractors.
✗ つうがく (通学) means "commuting to school". It uses the same 通 (ツウ) but pairs it with 学 (ガク, study/school), not 勤 (キン, work). The second kanji is entirely different.
✗ つうやく (通訳) means "interpretation / translating speech". 訳 (やく) means "translation". This word belongs to the communication domain, not the commuting domain.
✗ つうしん (通信) means "communication / correspondence". 信 (シン) means "message / trust". 通信 describes the transmission of information, not traveling to work.
例: 通勤 (つうきん) ラッシュの時間 (じかん) は電車 (でんしゃ) がとても混 (こ) んでいる。 — During rush hour, the trains are extremely crowded.

question: この海岸は ＿岩＿ が多い。
explanation:
岩 is read いわ, meaning "rock" or "boulder" — the sentence says this coastline has many large rocks.
岩 (いわ) means "rock" or "boulder" — a large, solid stone formation. It is typically found in nature: coastlines, mountains, rivers. The kanji uses the kun-yomi いわ when standing alone as a noun. Its on-yomi がん appears in compound words like 岩石 (がんせき, rock/stone material) and 岩盤 (がんばん, bedrock). The sentence says: "This coastline 海岸 (かいがん) has many rocks 岩 (いわ)." A rocky coastline is a concrete natural image, making いわ the natural fit. The distractors are all words that describe features you might find at a coast: かい (shell), すな (sand), なみ (wave). These test whether the student reads the specific kanji 岩 rather than guessing based on the coastal context. 岩 is composed of the radical 山 (mountain) over 石 (stone), visually encoding "a stone on/from a mountain" — a boulder.
✗ かい is the reading of 貝 (かい), meaning "shellfish" or "shell." Shells and rocks are both found on beaches, but 岩 does not read かい. 岩 and 貝 are completely different kanji.
✗ すな is the reading of 砂 (すな), meaning "sand." Sand and rocks are both coastal features, but 岩 (rock/boulder) is a much larger, harder formation than 砂 (fine-grained sand).
✗ なみ is the reading of 波 (なみ), meaning "wave." Waves are dynamic water features, completely different from 岩 (solid rock). 岩 does not read なみ.
例: 海辺 (うみべ) の大 (おお) きな岩 (いわ) の上 (うえ) に座 (すわ) って海 (うみ) を眺 (なが) めた。 — I sat on a large rock by the sea and looked out at the water.

question: ＿努力＿ することは大切だと思います。
explanation:
努力 is read どりょく — 努 reads ど (voiced) and 力 reads りょく, meaning "effort / hard work".
努力 (どりょく) = effort, hard work. 努 (ど) = to strive, 力 (りょく) = strength/power. The sentence says 「努力 (どりょく) することは大切 (たいせつ) だと思 (おも) います」 — "I think making effort is important." 努 reads voiced ど (not unvoiced と), and 力 reads りょく (with long ょ), not りよく (without long vowel). This question uses the correctly spelled りょく in the options, making it cleaner than the other 努力 entry.
✗ どうりょく: elongates 努 to どう. 努 reads ど (one mora), not どう. どうりょく could suggest 動力 (どうりょく, motive power) — a different word.
✗ とうりょく: unvoiced とう for 努. 努 reads voiced ど, not unvoiced と or とう.
✗ とりょく: unvoiced と for 努. 努 reads voiced ど. The voiced/unvoiced distinction between ど and と is exactly what this question tests.
例: 夢 (ゆめ) を実現 (じつげん) するためには努力 (どりょく) が欠 (か) かせない。 — Effort is essential for realizing one's dreams.

question: 日本の ＿首都＿ はどこですか。
explanation:
首都 is read しゅと — 首 reads しゅ and 都 reads と, meaning "capital city".
首都 (しゅと) = capital city. 首 (しゅ) = head/chief, 都 (と) = metropolis/city. Together: the chief city of a nation — the capital. The sentence says 「日本 (にほん) の首都 (しゅと) はどこですか」 — "Where is the capital of Japan?" Both kanji read with short on-yomi: しゅ (one mora) and と (one mora). The trap is elongating either to しゅとう or しゅうと.
✗ しゅとう: elongates 都 to とう. 都 reads と (one mora) in 首都. とう would be the reading for 都 in other contexts (e.g., 都合, つごう), but in 首都 it is a short と.
✗ しゅうと: elongates 首 to しゅう. 首 reads しゅ (one mora) in this compound. しゅう belongs to kanji like 週 (しゅう, week) or 州 (しゅう, state). Note: しゅうと means "father-in-law" (舅) — a completely different word.
✗ しゅうとう: elongates both kanji — wrong on both counts. 首 reads しゅ, 都 reads と. Neither has a long vowel in this compound.
例: 首都 (しゅと) 圏 (けん) には多 (おお) くの人 (ひと) が集 (あつ) まって住 (す) んでいる。 — Many people gather and live in the capital region.

question: ＿地球＿ は太陽のまわりを回っている。
explanation:
地球 is read ちきゅう and means "Earth" (the planet).
地球 (ちきゅう) is an on-yomi compound: 地 (チ, ground/earth) + 球 (キュウ, ball/sphere). Together the word literally means "the earth sphere" — the planet Earth. The sentence 「地球は太陽のまわりを回っている」 means "The Earth revolves around the Sun." The reading challenge is キュウ for 球 — a long vowel (two morae). Distractors ちきゅ and じきゅ test the vowel length and the voicing of 地. 地 reads チ (unvoiced) in 地球, not ジ (voiced). ジ is used in 地面 (じめん, ground surface) and 地震 (じしん, earthquake), where 地 has the voiced reading. The unvoiced チ is standard in most formal compounds like 地球 and 地図 (ちず, map).
✗ じきゅう voices the first kanji to ジ. In 地球, 地 reads the unvoiced チ. While 地 does have a voiced reading ジ in some compounds (地面 じめん, 地震 じしん), 地球 uses the unvoiced チ.
✗ じきゅ is the same first-kanji error (voiced ジ) plus dropping the long vowel from キュウ to きゅ. Both readings are wrong.
✗ ちきゅ correctly unvoices チ but drops the long vowel from 球 (キュウ → きゅ). The on-yomi of 球 is キュウ (two morae). Shortening it loses one mora.
例: 地球温暖化 (ちきゅうおんだんか) の問題 (もんだい) は、一国 (いっこく) だけでは解決 (かいけつ) できない。 — The problem of global warming cannot be solved by any one country alone.

question: あの時計は ＿遅れて＿ いる。
explanation:
遅れて is read おくれて and means "running late / behind time" — that clock is running slow.
遅れる (おくれる) is a kun-yomi intransitive verb meaning "to be late" or "to fall behind". The te-form 遅れて (おくれて) here connects with いる to express the ongoing state: 「あの時計は遅れている」 — "That clock is running slow (behind time)." The kanji 遅 contains the 辶 (movement) radical — something that moves but arrives late. The on-yomi チ appears in: 遅延 (ちえん, delay), 遅刻 (ちこく, being late). The kun-yomi おくれる is used for the verb; the adjective form is 遅い (おそい, slow/late). Note that 遅い has two kun-yomi: おそい (slow in general) and おくれる specifically for "running behind".
✗ こわれて is the te-form of 壊れる (こわれる), meaning "to break / to stop working". A broken clock and a slow clock are different states — こわれて means it stopped entirely, while おくれて means it is still running but showing the wrong time.
✗ たおれて is the te-form of 倒れる (たおれる), meaning "to fall over / to collapse". A clock that has fallen over and one that is running slow are different situations; 遅 does not read たお.
✗ よごれて is the te-form of 汚れる (よごれる), meaning "to get dirty". A dirty clock and a slow clock are different problems; 遅 does not read よご.
例: 電車 (でんしゃ) が30分 (さんじゅっぷん) 遅 (おく) れているので、会議 (かいぎ) に間 (ま) に合 (あ) わないかもしれない。 — The train is running 30 minutes late, so I may not make it to the meeting on time.

question: 二人で ＿協力＿ すれば、仕事も早く終わるだろう。
explanation:
協力 is read きょうりょく because 協 takes on-yomi きょう and 力 takes on-yomi りょく, giving the standard reading for "cooperation."
協力 (きょうりょく) means "cooperation" or "working together." It is a Sino-Japanese compound using the on-yomi of both kanji: 協 (きょう) means "together, in harmony" and 力 (りょく) means "strength, effort." Together they convey the idea of combining efforts toward a shared goal. The sentence says: "If the two of them cooperate 協力 (きょうりょく), the work will probably finish quickly." The long vowel in きょう is essential — the vowel after き is elongated (きょ + う), not shortened to きょ alone. This long vowel きょう comes from the on-yomi of 協, which appears in other words like 協会 (きょうかい, association) and 協定 (きょうてい, agreement). The second kanji 力 reads りょく in compounds (体力 たいりょく, physical strength; 努力 どりょく, effort) and ちから as kun-yomi (力 ちから, strength). The distractor どりょく is the real word 努力 (どりょく, effort/hard work), but it uses 努 (ど) not 協 (きょう).
✗ きょりょく drops the long vowel from きょう, shortening it to きょ. This does not correspond to any real word. The on-yomi of 協 is always the long きょう, not the short きょ.
✗ どりょく is the reading of 努力 (どりょく), meaning "effort" or "working hard on one's own." It uses the kanji 努 (ど, to strive). 努力 and 協力 are both N3 vocabulary, but 努 reads ど, not きょう.
✗ どうりょく is the reading of 動力 (どうりょく), meaning "motive power" or "driving force," or 同僚 (どうりょう, colleague). Neither matches 協力. The kanji 協 does not have the reading どう.
例: みんなで協力 (きょうりょく) すれば、どんな問題 (もんだい) でも解決 (かいけつ) できる。 — If everyone cooperates, any problem can be solved.

question: 大学の奨学金(しょうがくきん)に ＿応募＿ した。
explanation:
応募 is read おうぼ and means "to apply (for a scholarship, contest, etc.)".
応募 (おうぼ) is an on-yomi compound: 応 (オウ, respond/apply) + 募 (ボ, recruit/solicit). Together the word means "to respond to a recruitment" — to apply or enter (a contest, scholarship, job offer, etc.). The sentence 「大学の奨学金に応募した」 means "I applied for the university scholarship." The reading おうぼ uses the on-yomi of both: オウ + ボ. The confusion zone is おうぼ vs おうも vs おうぼう — distractors replace ボ with モ (a wrong on-yomi) or add an extra long vowel (おうぼう). 募 (ボ) appears in: 公募 (こうぼ, public recruitment), 募集 (ぼしゅう, recruitment drive), 募る (つのる, to solicit/grow stronger).
✗ おうも misreads 募 as モ instead of ボ. 募 reads ボ, not モ. The voiced b-sound (ボ) is essential — mo is a completely different syllable.
✗ おうぼう adds a long vowel to 募, making it ボウ. The on-yomi of 募 is a short ボ (one mora), not the long ボウ (two morae). おうぼう is not a reading of 応募.
✗ おうもう combines both errors — the wrong vowel モ and the extra length ウ. Neither the Mo reading nor the extended vowel are correct for 募.
例: コンテストに応募 (おうぼ) したら、二次審査 (にじしんさ) に進 (すす) めた。 — After applying to the contest, I was able to advance to the second round.

question: 子どもの ＿疑問＿ に答えた。
explanation:
疑問 is read ぎもん and means "a question" or "a doubt".
疑問 (ぎもん) is an on-yomi compound: 疑 (ギ, doubt/suspect) + 問 (モン, question/ask). Together the word means "a point of doubt" — a question that arises from uncertainty about something. The sentence 「子どもの疑問に答えた」 means "I answered the child's question." The reading ぎもん uses on-yomi for both: ギ + モン. The key issue is the voiced ギ for 疑 — the same kanji that reads うたがう as a verb uses ギ in compounds. Distractors manipulate the voicing of the initial sound: くもん (unvoiced k-), きもん (softened ki-), ぐもん (voiced g- but different vowel). Only ぎもん has both the correct voicing (voiced g-) and the correct vowel (i) for 疑.
✗ くもん does not match 疑 — 疑 reads ギ (voiced), not ク (unvoiced). くもん could suggest 苦悶 (くもん, agony) — a completely different word.
✗ きもん unvoices the initial consonant — ギ (voiced) becomes き (unvoiced). 疑 always reads ギ (voiced g-sound) in compounds, not the unvoiced き.
✗ ぐもん shifts the vowel of the initial syllable — ぎ (gi) becomes ぐ (gu). 疑 reads ギ (with an i-vowel), not グ (with a u-vowel). ぐもん is not a reading of 疑問.
例: 授業 (じゅぎょう) 中 (ちゅう) に疑問 (ぎもん) が生 (しょう) じたら、遠慮 (えんりょ) なく質問 (しつもん) してください。 — If you have a question during class, please do not hesitate to ask.

question: 試験の成績(せいせき)が ＿発表＿ された。
explanation:
発表 is read はっぴょう because 発 undergoes a sokuon contraction to はっ and 表 takes the on-yomi ひょう, voiced to ぴょう after the small っ.
発表 (はっぴょう) means "announcement" or "presentation." The reading requires understanding two phonological rules at once. First, 発 (はつ/ほつ) has an on-yomi はつ, but when it precedes a syllable beginning with ひ/は, the つ contracts into a sokuon っ: はつ + ひょう → はっひょう → はっぴょう. Second, after the glottal stop っ, the following consonant voices: ひょう becomes ぴょう. So the full chain is: は + っ + ぴょう = はっぴょう. This sokuon voicing pattern also appears in other words like 発表 (はっぴょう), 発見 (はっけん, discovery), and 発音 (はつおん, pronunciation — here no contraction because 音 begins with お). The character 表 (ひょう/おもて) means "to show" or "surface/table." It appears in 時刻表 (じこくひょう, timetable) and 代表 (だいひょう, representative). The sentence says: "The exam results 成績 (せいせき) were announced 発表 (はっぴょう)." 発表する is the standard verb for announcing or presenting information formally.
✗ はっひょう keeps the initial ひ unvoiced after the sokuon っ. In Japanese phonology, a voiceless consonant following っ typically voices to its pair: ひ → ぴ, は → ぱ, etc. はっひょう is phonologically non-standard and does not reflect the actual pronunciation.
✗ はっひょ drops the long vowel う from ひょう. The on-yomi of 表 is ひょう (a two-mora syllable ひょ + う). Shortening it to はっひょ removes the final mora and produces a non-existent reading.
✗ はっぴょ applies the correct voicing (ひ → ぴ) but drops the trailing long vowel う from ぴょう. The full on-yomi is ぴょう (three morae: ぴ + ょ + う), not the two-mora ぴょ.
例: 来週、プロジェクトの結果 (けっか) を発表 (はっぴょう) する予定 (よてい) です。 — We plan to announce the project results next week.

question: ＿単語＿ のリストはとなりのページにあります。
explanation:
単語 is read たんご because 単 takes on-yomi たん and 語 takes on-yomi ご, forming the standard compound for "vocabulary word."
単語 (たんご) means "a word" or "a vocabulary item" — a single unit of language. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 単 (たん) = single/alone, and 語 (ご) = word/language. Together they describe a single language unit — a word. The sentence says: "The list of vocabulary words 単語 (たんご) is on the next page." 単語リスト = vocabulary list is a standard classroom expression. The reading challenge involves distinguishing たん vs だん (voiced vs unvoiced) for 単, and ご (single mora) vs ごう (long vowel) for 語. The correct reading たんご is short: たん (two morae: た + ん) + ご (one mora). The distractors introduce: げいご (using an unrelated読み), けいご (敬語 けいご = honorific language — a real word but different kanji), and だんご (団語 — not real; but 団子 だんご means dumplings — different word). The key trap is けいご (敬語), which is a real JLPT word, but 敬 ≠ 単.
✗ げいご assigns the reading げい to 単. 単 does not read げい. げい is the reading of 芸 (art/skill — 芸術 げいじゅつ) or 鯨 (げい, whale). Neither applies here.
✗ けいご is the reading of 敬語 (けいご), meaning "honorific language" — a real and important Japanese word. However, 敬語 uses the kanji 敬 (けい, respect) and 語 (ご, language), not 単 (たん). 単語 (vocabulary word) and 敬語 (honorific language) are entirely different compounds.
✗ だんご voices 単 to だん. The on-yomi of 単 is たん (unvoiced), not voiced だん. だんご is the reading of 団子 (だんご), meaning dumplings — a very different word using different kanji.
例: 試験 (しけん) に備 (そな) えて、毎日新 (まいにちあたら) しい単語 (たんご) を10個 (じっこ) 覚 (おぼ) えている。 — To prepare for the exam, I memorize 10 new vocabulary words every day.

question: 1 今年の夏は、 ＿過去＿ 十年間で一番の暑さだったそうだ。
explanation:
過去 is read かこ because 過 takes on-yomi か and 去 takes on-yomi こ, forming the short compound meaning "the past."
過去 (かこ) means "the past" — time that has already elapsed. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 過 (か) = to pass, and 去 (こ) = to go away/leave. Together they describe time that has passed and gone. The sentence says: "This summer, the heat is apparently the worst in the past ten years." 過去十年間で一番の暑さ = "the hottest in the past ten years." This uses 過去 (かこ) in the common expression 過去○年間 (かこ○ねんかん, over the past ○ years). This is a second question testing the same reading かこ — see also entry hash 6b7589ae01efd5f7, which used a different sentence context (remembering things from the past). The core reading remains かこ: both morae are short, with no long vowels. The reading trap of adding long vowels (かきょ, かこう, かきょう) is the same. Here, the sentence context (hottest in ten years) reinforces the temporal past-reference use of 過去.
✗ かきょ uses the alternative on-yomi きょ for 去. In 過去, 去 reads こ (short), not きょ (used in 去年 きょねん, last year). The reading split of 去 is こ (in 過去) vs きょ (in 去年).
✗ かこう adds a long vowel to 去, producing こう instead of こ. 去 reads the single mora こ in 過去 — no long vowel is added.
✗ かきょう combines both the きょ reading of 去 and an added long vowel う. Both changes are wrong: 去 reads こ in 過去, and there is no long vowel.
例: 過去 (かこ) の失敗 (しっぱい) を教訓 (きょうくん) にして、今後 (こんご) に活 (い) かしたい。 — I want to learn from past failures and use them going forward.

question: 2 あと５分で東京駅に ＿到着＿ します
explanation:
到着 is read とうちゃく — 到 reads とう and 着 reads ちゃく, meaning "arrival".
到着 (とうちゃく) = arrival. 「あと5分 (ふん) で東京駅 (とうきょうえき) に到着 (とうちゃく) します」 — "We will arrive at Tokyo Station in 5 minutes." 到 reads unvoiced とう (not voiced どう).
✗ とうつく: correct とう for 到 but kun-yomi つく for 着. In 到着, 着 takes on-yomi ちゃく.
✗ どうつく: voices 到 to どう (wrong) and uses kun-yomi つく for 着 (wrong).
✗ どうちゃく: correct ちゃく for 着 but voices 到 to どう (wrong).
例: 飛行機 (ひこうき) は30分 (さんじゅっぷん) 遅 (おく) れて到着 (とうちゃく) した。 — The airplane arrived 30 minutes late.

question: 3 公園の木の枝を ＿折って＿ はいけません。
explanation:
折って is read おって, meaning "break off / snap" — breaking branches in a park is prohibited.
折る (おる) means "to break off," "to snap," or "to fold." Its te-form 折って (おって) is used in compound instructions or descriptions. The sentence says: "You must not break 折って (おって) the branches of park trees." 公園の木の枝を折ってはいけません = "Do not snap branches off park trees" is a public rules sign. The kanji 折 uses the kun-yomi お in the transitive verb form: 折る (おる, you snap something). The intransitive counterpart is 折れる (おれる, it snaps by itself). Its on-yomi せつ appears in 骨折 (こっせつ, bone fracture) and 折衷 (せっちゅう, compromise). The four distractors — うって (売る, to sell/hit), おって (correct), わって (割る, to break/split), and きって (切る, to cut) — all describe destructive or ending actions on objects. The crucial distinction: 折る (fold/snap at a joint), 割る (crack/split into pieces), and 切る (cut with a blade). Tree branches are snapped (折る), not cut (切る) or split (割る).
✗ うって is the te-form of either 売る (うる, to sell) or 打つ (うつ, to hit/strike). Selling or hitting tree branches are different actions. 折 does not read うって.
✗ わって is the te-form of 割る (わる), meaning "to split" or "to crack." Breaking a branch means snapping it (折る), not splitting it into pieces (割る). 折 does not read わって.
✗ きって is the te-form of 切る (きる), meaning "to cut." Cutting uses a sharp instrument; snapping a branch uses force at a joint. These are different actions. 折 does not read きって.
例: 祖母 (そぼ) が庭 (にわ) の花 (はな) を折 (お) って花瓶 (かびん) に飾 (かざ) ってくれた。 — My grandmother snapped off some flowers from the garden and arranged them in a vase.

question: 4 インターネットで最新の ＿情報＿ をチェックした。
explanation:
情報 is read じょうほう — 情 reads じょう and 報 reads ほう, meaning "information".
情報 (じょうほう) = information/data. 情 (じょう) = feelings/circumstances, 報 (ほう) = to report. 「インターネットで最新 (さいしん) の情報 (じょうほう) をチェックした」 — "I checked the latest information on the internet."
✗ じゅうほう: じゅう for 情 is wrong. 情 reads じょう. じゅう belongs to 十 (ten) or 重 (heavy).
✗ じょうほ: shortens ほう to ほ. 報 reads ほう (long vowel), not ほ.
✗ じゅうほ: wrong じゅう for 情 and wrong ほ for 報.
例: 最新 (さいしん) の情報 (じょうほう) はウェブサイトで確認 (かくにん) できます。 — You can check the latest information on the website.

question: 5 最近、野菜の ＿値段＿ が高くなっています。
explanation:
値段 is read ねだん and means "price".
値段 (ねだん) means "price" or "cost". The compound uses a mix of readings: 値 (ね, value/price — kun-yomi) + 段 (だん, step/grade — here the on-yomi DAN softens to だん). The sentence 「最近、野菜の値段が高くなっています」 means "The prices of vegetables have been rising recently." The reading challenge is ね for 値 — the on-yomi of 値 is チ (e.g., 価値 かち, value/worth), but in 値段 the kun-yomi ね is used. The voiced だん for 段 (normally タン in formal compounds like 段階 だんかい) here uses a lighter, kun-like reading common in everyday compounds. Distractors かかく (価格, formal price) and かがく (科学, science) share similar sounds but are different words.
✗ かかく (価格) means "price" in a more formal/economic register. 価格 uses entirely different kanji — 価 (カ, value) + 格 (カク, standard/grade). It is a real synonym of 値段 but is not a reading of 値段.
✗ かがく (科学) means "science" or (化学, chemistry). It is phonetically close to かかく but refers to a completely different domain — not price at all.
✗ ねたん is a near-miss that misreads 段 as タン instead of the correct voiced だん. In 値段, 段 takes the voiced reading だん, not the unvoiced タン.
例: 旬 (しゅん) の時期 (じき) は野菜 (やさい) の値段 (ねだん) が下 (さ) がるので、たくさん買 (か) っておく。 — When vegetables are in season, their prices drop, so I buy a lot.

question: 6 彼はあの国の文化に ＿深い＿ 関心を持っている。
explanation:
深い is read ふかい and means "deep" — describing a deep interest in that country's culture.
深 (ふか) い is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "deep". The sentence 「彼はあの国の文化に深い関心を持っている」 means "He has a deep interest in that country's culture." In Japanese, 深い (ふかい) extends beyond physical depth — it also describes intensity of feeling, interest, or understanding, much like English "deep". The kun-yomi ふか is the only reading used when 深 appears alone as an adjective. The on-yomi シン appears in compounds: 深夜 (しんや, late night), 深刻 (しんこく, serious/grave), 深海 (しんかい, deep sea). The 氵 (water) radical visually signals something related to depth.
✗ つよい is the reading of 強い, meaning "strong". A strong interest and a deep interest are related but 強 and 深 are different kanji; 深 does not read つよ.
✗ ひろい is the reading of 広い, meaning "wide / broad". A broad interest and a deep interest overlap in meaning, but 広 (ひろい, wide) and 深 (ふかい, deep) are distinct adjectives with different kanji.
✗ おもい is the reading of 重い, meaning "heavy" or "serious". While 重い can sometimes describe a serious matter, it does not pair with 関心 (かんしん, interest) in this way; 深い is the standard collocate for 関心.
例: この問題 (もんだい) については、深 (ふか) く考 (かんが) える必要 (ひつよう) がある。 — We need to think deeply about this issue.

question: 7 昨日、友達に本を ＿返しました＿ 。
explanation:
返しました is read かえしました and means "returned" — the speaker returned a book to a friend.
返す (かえす) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to return (something) to its owner". The polite past form 返しました (かえしました) expresses the completed act of giving something back. The sentence 「昨日、友達に本を返しました」 means "Yesterday, I returned a book to my friend." The kanji 返 contains the 辶 (movement) radical and the component 反 (reverse/against), visually suggesting movement back to the origin. Its on-yomi ヘン appears in: 返答 (へんとう, reply), 返金 (へんきん, refund), 返済 (へんさい, repayment). The verb 返す is transitive — the speaker returns something — as opposed to 帰る (かえる, to go back), which is intransitive.
✗ かしました is the polite past form of 貸す (かす), meaning "to lend". Lending a book and returning a book are opposite actions — lending is giving someone else temporary use; returning is giving it back.
✗ もどしました is the polite past form of 戻す (もどす), meaning "to put back / to restore". While 戻す and 返す both relate to putting things back, 返す specifically means returning something to its owner, while 戻す means restoring to a previous state or location.
✗ わたしました is the polite past form of 渡す (わたす), meaning "to hand over / to pass". Handing something over and returning it to an owner are different — 渡す is a general transfer while 返す specifically completes a loan.
例: 借 (か) りた傘 (かさ) を返 (かえ) さないままにしていて、相手 (あいて) に申 (もう) し訳 (わけ) なかった。 — I felt bad for not returning the umbrella I had borrowed.

question: 8 月の ＿表面＿ はでこぼこしている。
explanation:
表面 is read ひょうめん — 表 reads ひょう and 面 reads めん, meaning "surface".
表面 (ひょうめん) = surface — the outer face or exterior of something. 表 (ひょう) = outer surface/to show, 面 (めん) = face/surface. The sentence says 「月 (つき) の表面 (ひょうめん) はでこぼこしている」 — "The surface of the moon is bumpy." Both kanji have long vowels in their on-yomi: 表 is ひょう (three morae) and 面 is めん (two morae). The trap is shortening either to しょ or ひょ.
✗ しょめん: wrong しょ for 表. 表 reads ひょう, not しょ. しょ could fit kanji like 書 (しょ, writing) or 所 (しょ, place).
✗ ひょめん: shortens 表 to ひょ, dropping the final う. 表 reads ひょう (three morae, long vowel), not ひょ alone.
✗ しょうめん: wrong しょう for 表, though this reading looks like 正面 (しょうめん, front face) — a real word but not what is written here. 表 reads ひょう, not しょう.
例: この金属 (きんぞく) は表面 (ひょうめん) がなめらかで美 (うつく) しい。 — This metal has a smooth and beautiful surface.

question: １ スポーツで ＿汗＿ をかいたので、シャワーをあびた。
explanation:
汗 is read あせ and means "sweat" — worked up a sweat playing sports, then took a shower.
汗 (あせ) means "sweat" or "perspiration". The sentence 「スポーツで汗をかいたので、シャワーをあびた」 means "Because I sweated doing sports, I took a shower." 汗をかく (あせをかく) is the set phrase meaning "to sweat", where かく means "to produce/exude". The kanji 汗 contains the 氵 (water) radical, consistent with its meaning of a liquid produced by the body. The on-yomi カン appears in compounds like 発汗 (はっかん, perspiration/sweating). When 汗 stands alone as a noun, it always reads あせ. The four options test whether learners distinguish body fluids and substances: sweat (あせ), garbage (ごみ), dirt (よごれ), tears (なみだ).
✗ ごみ means "garbage" or "trash" — a non-liquid substance. Garbage and sweat are entirely different things. ごみ is typically written in hiragana or with the kanji 塵 or 芥, not 汗.
✗ よごれ means "dirt" or "a stain" — what is left on something after it gets soiled. Dirt and sweat are related (sweating can cause dirt) but are distinct; 汗 does not read よごれ.
✗ なみだ is the reading of 涙 (tears). Tears and sweat are both bodily liquids from the 氵 radical family, but they come from different body parts and different stimuli. 汗 does not read なみだ.
例: 夏 (なつ) に走 (はし) ると大 (おお) 量 (りょう) の汗 (あせ) をかくので、水分 (すいぶん) を十分 (じゅうぶん) に補給 (ほきゅう) する必要 (ひつよう) がある。 — Running in summer makes you sweat a lot, so you need to stay well hydrated.

question: ２ このお知らせをみんなに ＿配って＿ ください。
explanation:
配って is read くばって, meaning "distribute / hand out" — the instruction is to distribute a notice to everyone.
配る (くばる) means "to distribute," "to hand out," or "to deliver" — giving something to multiple people one by one. Its te-form 配って (くばって) appears in instructions. The sentence says: "Please distribute 配って (くばって) this notice お知らせ to everyone." みんなに配る = "to hand out to everyone" is a typical classroom or meeting instruction. The kanji 配 uses the kun-yomi くば in verb form. Its on-yomi はい appears in compounds like 配達 (はいたつ, delivery), 配布 (はいふ, distribution/circulation), and 心配 (しんぱい, worry/concern). Note 心配 (しんぱい, worry) — 配 in this compound means distributing one's heart/mind (a figurative use). The distractors — だまって (keeping silent), もらって (receiving), and はらって (paying) — are all te-form verbs that could naturally appear in social or transactional contexts, but none means distributing.
✗ だまって is the te-form of 黙る (だまる), meaning "to keep silent" or "to be quiet." Distributing a notice requires action; keeping silent is the opposite of actively handing things out. 配 does not read だまって.
✗ もらって is the te-form of もらう, meaning "to receive" (as a favor from someone). Receiving is the opposite direction from distributing. 配 does not read もらって.
✗ はらって is the te-form of 払う (はらう), meaning "to pay." Paying for something and distributing something are different transactions. 配 does not read はらって.
例: 会議 (かいぎ) の前 (まえ) に資料 (しりょう) を参加者 (さんかしゃ) に配 (くば) っておいた。 — Before the meeting, I distributed the materials to the participants.

question: ３ 新しい道路がもうすぐ ＿完成＿ するそうだ。
explanation:
完成 is read かんせい and means "completion" — a new road will be finished soon.
完成 (かんせい) is an on-yomi compound: 完 (カン, complete/whole) + 成 (セイ, accomplish/become). Together the word means "full accomplishment" — reaching a completed state. The sentence 「新しい道路がもうすぐ完成するそうだ」 means "I heard that the new road will be completed soon." The reading challenge is distinguishing かんせい (完成, completion) from other similarly-sounding compounds: けんせつ (建設, construction), かんぜん (完全, perfect), けんちく (建築, architecture). All four relate to buildings and construction, making them contextually plausible but semantically distinct. 完 appears in: 完了 (かんりょう, completion/finishing), 完全 (かんぜん, perfection).
✗ けんせつ (建設) means "construction" — the process of building. 建 (ケン, build) + 設 (セツ, establish). A road under construction would use 建設中, while 完成 describes the finished result.
✗ かんぜん (完全) means "perfect" or "complete (without flaws)". 完 (カン) + 全 (ゼン, all/complete). 完全 describes a state of perfection; 完成 describes the act of finishing/completing a project.
✗ けんちく (建築) means "architecture" or "the act of constructing a building". 建 (ケン) + 築 (チク, build/construct). Architecture and completion are related but different stages — 建築 is the activity, 完成 is the outcome.
例: 3年 (さんねん) かけて書 (か) いた小説 (しょうせつ) がついに完成 (かんせい) した。 — The novel I spent three years writing was finally completed.

question: ４ ここから ＿島＿ がたくさん見えますよ。
explanation:
島 is read しま, meaning "island" — from here, many islands are visible.
島 (しま) means "island" — a landmass surrounded by water. The sentence says: "From here, you can see many islands 島 (しま)!" ここから島がたくさん見える is a natural sight-seeing expression, especially in Japan with its many island chains. The kanji 島 uses the kun-yomi しま when standing alone as a noun. Its on-yomi とう appears in compounds like 半島 (はんとう, peninsula), 島国 (しまぐに, island nation), and 列島 (れっとう, archipelago). Japan itself is often called 島国 (しまぐに) because it is an island nation. The four distractors — ほし (star), とり (bird), しま (correct), and うま (horse) — are four common noun readings that share no visual connection to the kanji 島. This tests direct kanji-reading recognition, as the distractors describe entirely different things (celestial body, animal, island, animal).
✗ ほし is the reading of 星 (ほし), meaning "star." Stars and islands are both scattered across vast spaces (sky/sea), but 島 does not read ほし. The kanji 星 and 島 look completely different.
✗ とり is the reading of 鳥 (とり), meaning "bird." The kanji 島 does contain a bird-like component (鳥 is embedded visually), but 島 itself reads しま (island), not とり (bird). The radical origin does not change the reading.
✗ うま is the reading of 馬 (うま), meaning "horse." Horse and island have nothing in common. 島 does not read うま.
例: この地域 (ちいき) には大 (おお) きな島 (しま) が一つと、小 (ちい) さな島 (しま) がいくつかある。 — This area has one large island and several smaller islands.

question: ５ 田中さんはちょっと ＿困って＿ いるみたいです。
explanation:
困って is read こまって and means "in trouble / struggling" — Tanaka seems to be having difficulty.
困る (こまる) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to be in trouble", "to be troubled", or "to struggle with something". The te-form 困って (こまって) connects with いる to express the ongoing state: 「田中さんはちょっと困っているみたいです」 — "It seems Tanaka is having a bit of trouble." The kanji 困 contains the 囗 (enclosure) radical around the 木 (tree) component — visually, a tree stuck inside a box, unable to grow. This is a perfect visual mnemonic for being stuck or in a difficult situation. The on-yomi コン appears in: 困難 (こんなん, difficulty/hardship), 困惑 (こんわく, confusion/perplexity).
✗ まよって is the te-form of 迷う (まよう), meaning "to get lost / to be indecisive". Being uncertain what to do and being in trouble are related feelings, but 困 does not read まよ.
✗ おこって is the te-form of 怒る (おこる), meaning "to get angry". Being angry and being troubled are different emotional states; 困 does not read おこ.
✗ うたがって is the te-form of 疑う (うたがう), meaning "to doubt / to suspect". Suspecting someone and being in trouble are different; 困 does not read うたが.
例: 道 (みち) に迷 (まよ) って困 (こま) っていたら、親切 (しんせつ) な人 (ひと) が案内 (あんない) してくれた。 — When I was lost and in trouble, a kind person showed me the way.

question: ６ ＿平日＿ は午後8 時まで開いています。
explanation:
平日 is read へいじつ and means "a weekday" (as opposed to a weekend or holiday).
平日 (へいじつ) is an on-yomi compound: 平 (ヘイ, ordinary/level) + 日 (ジツ, day). Together the word means "an ordinary day" — i.e., Monday through Friday, as opposed to 休日 (きゅうじつ, day off) or 休みの日. The sentence 「平日は午後8時まで開いています」 means "On weekdays, (we) are open until 8 p.m." The phonological trap is the same as in 休日 — 日 reads ジツ (not にち) when it is the second element in certain time compounds. The distractor へいにち would be a mistake of reading 日 as にち in this compound context. The first kanji 平 reads ヘイ here, not ほん (which belongs to 本).
✗ ほんにち (本日) — wait, this option is ほんにち, which would come from 本日 (ほんじつ, today — formal). But here the first kanji is 平 (ヘイ, ordinary), not 本 (ほん/ホン). So ほんにち misidentifies both the first kanji reading and the second kanji reading.
✗ へいにち misreads 日 as にち. In the compound 平日, 日 uses the on-yomi ジツ, not にち. へいにち is not a standard reading of this compound.
✗ ほんじつ (本日) is a real word meaning "today" (formal), but it is a different word. Its first kanji is 本 (ほん, this/book), not 平 (へい, ordinary). The compound in the question is 平日, not 本日.
例: この図書館 (としょかん) は平日 (へいじつ) のみ開 (あ) いていて、土日 (どにち) は休 (やす) みです。 — This library is open only on weekdays and is closed on Saturdays and Sundays.

question: ７ わたしは3年前に大学を ＿卒業＿ しました。
explanation:
卒業 is read そつぎょう because 卒 takes on-yomi そつ and 業 takes on-yomi ぎょう, forming the standard word for "graduation."
卒業 (そつぎょう) means "graduation" — completing a course of study at a school. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 卒 (そつ) = to finish/graduate, and 業 (ぎょう) = undertaking/work/studies. Together 卒業 describes completing (卒) one's educational undertaking (業). The sentence says: "I graduated 卒業 (そつぎょう) from university three years ago." 大学を卒業する = "to graduate from university" is the standard phrase. The reading challenge: 卒 must be そつ (unvoiced, two morae), not the voiced さつ or the short forms そつぎょ. 業 must be ぎょう (voiced, long vowel), not the unvoiced きょう or the shortened ぎょ. The four options systematically cover: そつぎょう (correct), さつぎょう (voiced beginning), そつぎょ (missing long vowel), and さつぎょ (both wrong). 卒 also appears in 卒業式 (そつぎょうしき, graduation ceremony) and 卒業生 (そつぎょうせい, graduate). 業 also appears in 授業 (じゅぎょう, class), 就業 (しゅうぎょう, employment), and 残業 (ざんぎょう, overtime).
✗ さつぎょう voices 卒 to さつ. 卒 reads そつ (unvoiced), not さつ (voiced). さつ is the reading of 殺 (kill) or 冊 (volume) — not 卒.
✗ さつぎょ voices 卒 and drops the long vowel from 業. Both changes are wrong: 卒 = そつ (unvoiced), 業 = ぎょう (long vowel). さつぎょ is a double error.
✗ そつぎょ reads 卒 correctly as そつ but drops the trailing long vowel from 業. 業 reads ぎょう (three morae: ぎ + ょ + う), not the shorter ぎょ (two morae). The long vowel is essential.
例: 彼 (かれ) は今年 (ことし) 大学院 (だいがくいん) を卒業 (そつぎょう) して、外資系企業 (がいしけいきぎょう) に就職 (しゅうしょく) した。 — He graduated from graduate school this year and got a job at a foreign-affiliated company.

question: ８ びんのふたは ＿固く＿ しめておいてください。
explanation:
固く is read かたく because 固 takes the kun-yomi かた, meaning "firmly / tightly," which matches tightening a bottle lid.
固い (かたい) is an i-adjective meaning "hard, firm, or tight." Its adverbial form 固く (かたく) means "firmly" or "tightly." The kanji 固 carries the idea of something set, hardened, or not easily moved. The sentence says: "Please close the bottle lid firmly." 固く (かたく) fits perfectly here because it describes the manner of tightening — not lightly, not loosely, but with a firm grip. The kun-yomi かた is the reading used when 固 stands alone as a verb or adjective stem: 固い (かたい, hard/firm), 固める (かためる, to harden/solidify). The on-yomi こ appears in compounds like 固定 (こてい, fixation) and 固体 (こたい, solid substance). In adjective-adverb use like this sentence, kun-yomi かた is always correct. The adverbial suffix く attached to かたい produces かたく, changing the i-adjective to an adverb modifying the verb しめる (to close/tighten).
✗ かるく is the adverbial form of 軽い (かるい), meaning "lightly." Closing a lid lightly would be the opposite of what the sentence instructs.
✗ ゆるく is the adverbial form of 緩い (ゆるい), meaning "loosely." A loosely closed lid defeats the purpose of the instruction — contents could spill or air could get in.
✗ きつく is the adverbial form of きつい, meaning "tight" or "strict." While close in nuance to かたく, the underlined kanji is 固く, not きつく. きつい is typically written in kana and does not use the kanji 固. The question tests the reading of 固, not a vocabulary substitution.
例: この機械 (きかい) のネジは固 (かた) く締 (し) めてある。 — The screw on this machine is fastened firmly.

question: このひもは ＿短すぎて＿ 使いにくい。
explanation:
短すぎて is read みじかすぎて and means "too short" — the cord is too short to use.
短い (みじかい) is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "short (in length)". The form みじかすぎて combines 短い (short) + すぎる (too much) + て, meaning "being too short and (therefore)...". The sentence 「このひもは短すぎて使いにくい」 means "This cord is too short and hard to use." The kun-yomi みじか is the only reading for 短 when it functions as an independent adjective. The on-yomi タン appears in compounds like 短所 (たんしょ, shortcoming), 短編 (たんぺん, short story), 短距離 (たんきょり, short distance). The antonym 長い (ながい, long) is also kun-yomi.
✗ よわすぎて would come from 弱すぎる (よわすぎる), meaning "too weak". Weakness and shortness of length are different properties; 短 does not read よわ.
✗ ほそすぎて would come from 細すぎる (ほそすぎる), meaning "too thin / too slender". Thinness and shortness are different dimensions; 短 does not read ほそ.
✗ かたすぎて would come from 硬すぎる (かたすぎる), meaning "too hard / too stiff". Hardness and length are unrelated properties; 短 does not read かた.
例: 冬 (ふゆ) は日 (ひ) が短 (みじか) くて、夕方 (ゆうがた) 5時 (ごじ) にはもう暗 (くら) くなる。 — In winter the days are short, and it gets dark as early as 5 in the evening.

question: あの人は ＿他人＿ の意見を全然聞かない。
explanation:
他人 is read たにん and means "other people / someone else".
他人 (たにん) is an on-yomi compound: 他 (タ, other) + 人 (ニン, person). Together the word means "another person" — someone outside one's own circle, a stranger or third party. The sentence 「あの人は他人の意見を全然聞かない」 means "That person does not listen to other people's opinions at all." The reading たにん uses on-yomi for both: タ + ニン. Key distinction: 人 reads ジン in formal abstract compounds (個人 こじん, 成人 せいじん), and reads ニン in occupational or count compounds (職人 しょくにん, 三人 さんにん). In 他人, the ニン reading applies. Distractors confuse タ with チ (a wrong on-yomi) and ニン with ジン.
✗ ちにん misreads 他 as チ. 他 reads タ, not チ. チ belongs to other kanji (知 = knowledge, 地 = ground), not 他 (other).
✗ たじん uses ジン instead of ニン for 人. While ジン is a common on-yomi for 人, in the compound 他人 the reading is ニン. This ジン/ニン distinction is a known N3 trap.
✗ ちじん misreads both kanji — 他 as チ and 人 as ジン. Neither adjustment is correct. ちじん does not correspond to the compound 他人.
例: 他人 (たにん) のことを批判 (ひはん) する前 (まえ) に、自分 (じぶん) の行動 (こうどう) を振 (ふ) り返 (かえ) るべきだ。 — Before criticizing others, you should reflect on your own actions.

question: 人口の変化をグラフで ＿示した＿ 。
explanation:
示した is read しめした because 示す means "to show / to indicate", fitting the act of showing data on a graph.
示す (しめす) = to show, to indicate, to point out. Its past tense 示 (しめ) した. The sentence says 「人口 (じんこう) の変化 (へんか) をグラフで示 (しめ) した」 — "The change in population was shown on a graph." 示す is used for displaying data, indicating a direction, or pointing to evidence. The kanji 示 contains 二 at the top and 小 below — resembling an altar or something presented for display.
✗ うつした: past tense of 写す (うつす, to copy/photograph) or 映す (うつす, to project/reflect). Neither means "to show data on a graph". Copying or projecting is different from indicating/displaying.
✗ さした: past tense of 差す (さす, to point/to stick) or 指す (さす, to point at). While 指す (さす) can mean to point at something, it differs from 示す (しめす, to show/indicate data). The kanji on the page is 示, not 指 or 差.
✗ あらわした: past tense of 表す/現す (あらわす, to express/to represent). 表す means to express or represent something symbolically. While close in meaning, the kanji shown is 示 (しめす), not 表 or 現 (あらわす).
例: 研究結果 (けんきゅうけっか) をグラフで示 (しめ) してください。 — Please show the research results on a graph.

question: 田中さんは ＿外科＿ のお医者さんです。
explanation:
外科 is read げか and means "surgery" (a medical department).
外科 (げか) is a two-kanji compound: 外 (ゲ/そと, outside) + 科 (カ, department/subject). Together the word refers to the surgical department of a hospital — "external medicine", i.e., treatment that operates on the body from the outside. The sentence 「田中さんは外科のお医者さんです」 means "Dr. Tanaka is a surgery doctor." The reading challenge is the irregular on-yomi of 外: in most compounds 外 reads ガイ (外国 がいこく, foreign country), but in 外科 it reads ゲ — a less common on-yomi of the same kanji. This ゲ reading appears in: 外科 (げか, surgery), 外皮 (がいひ — standard), but 外科 specifically uses ゲ by convention.
✗ がいか applies the standard on-yomi ガイ to 外. While ガイ is the dominant on-yomi of 外 (as in 外国 がいこく), the fixed medical compound 外科 specifically uses the alternative on-yomi ゲ. がいか is not the standard reading of 外科.
✗ げいか adds a long vowel to ゲ, making it げい. The on-yomi of 外 in this compound is a short ゲ (one mora), not the long げい (two morae). げいか is not a reading of 外科.
✗ がか applies neither the standard on-yomi ガイ nor the compound-specific ゲ — it creates a vowel-shortened form that matches no reading of 外. がか is not a word related to surgery.
例: 骨 (ほね) が折 (お) れたので、病院 (びょういん) の外科 (げか) に行 (い) って手術 (しゅじゅつ) を受 (う) けた。 — I broke a bone, so I went to the surgery department of the hospital and had an operation.

question: 佐藤さんほ ＿笑顔＿ がとてもすてきです。
explanation:
笑顔 is read えがお — it means "smiling face", and the reading is an irregular compound of two kun-yomi.
笑顔 (えがお) = a smiling face. This is an irregular compound: 笑 (え) is an unusual abbreviated reading of 笑い (わらい, laughter), and 顔 (かお) = face. The combination えがお is a set expression meaning a cheerful, smiling face — not just any expression but specifically a warm, welcoming smile. The sentence says 「佐藤 (さとう) さんの笑顔 (えがお) がとてもすてきです」 — "Sato-san's smile is very lovely." Note that 笑 normally reads わらう (to laugh) or わらい, but in the compound 笑顔, it takes the shortened reading え.
✗ えかお: uses か instead of が. In Japanese compound nouns, the second element often voices (連濁, れんだく). Here 顔 (かお) voices to がお — えがお, not えかお.
✗ わらがお: reads 笑 as わら (the standard kun-yomi prefix). However, the compound 笑顔 is a fixed expression read えがお — the わら reading is not used in this specific compound.
✗ わらかお: same problem as わらがお — uses わら for 笑 and then fails to voice 顔 to がお. Both parts of this option are wrong for the compound 笑顔.
例: 彼 (かれ) はいつも笑顔 (えがお) で人 (ひと) に接 (せっ) する。 — He always interacts with people with a smile.

question: 5時 ＿以降＿ にもう一度お電話ください。 -
explanation:
以降 is read いこう and means "on and after / from (a time) onwards".
以降 (いこう) is an on-yomi compound: 以 (イ, from/since) + 降 (コウ, descend/from a point down). Together the word means "from a certain point onwards" — used with a time reference to mean "after X" or "from X on". The sentence 「5時以降にもう一度お電話ください」 means "Please call again after 5 o'clock." The compound 以降 is part of a set of directional time markers: 以前 (いぜん, before/previously), 以後 (いご, after/from now on), 以降 (いこう, from that point onwards). The distinction between 以後 (いご) and 以降 (いこう) is subtle: 以後 is often used for personal declarations (「以後、気をつけます」 I will be careful from now on), while 以降 more naturally marks a specific point in a schedule or timeline.
✗ いこ drops the long vowel from コウ. The on-yomi of 降 in this compound is コウ (long, two morae), not コ (short, one mora). いこ is not a reading of 以降.
✗ いごう adds an extra vowel, producing いごう instead of いこう. No standard compound following 以 reads いごう with a reversed vowel order.
✗ いご (以後) is a real word meaning "from now on / henceforth", but it is a different word from 以降 (いこう). 以後 uses 後 (ご, after/following), while 以降 uses 降 (こう, descend/from a point down). They are close in meaning but distinct.
例: 申し込み (もうしこみ) は今月 (こんげつ) 末 (すえ) 以降 (いこう) は受け付 (つ) けません。 — Applications will not be accepted after the end of this month.

question: 道路を ＿横断＿ するときは、車に十分注意してください。
explanation:
横断 is read おうだん — both on-yomi; traffic-safety context.
横断 (おうだん) = crossing a road. 「道路 (どうろ) を横断 (おうだん) するときは車 (くるま) に十分 (じゅうぶん) 注意 (ちゅうい) してください」 — "Please take full care regarding cars when crossing the road."
✗ よこだん: kun-yomi よこ for 横. In 横断, 横 takes on-yomi おう.
✗ おうたん: correct おう for 横 but unvoiced たん for 断. 断 reads voiced だん.
✗ よこたん: both wrong.
例: 赤信号 (あかしんごう) での横断 (おうだん) は危険 (きけん) です。 — Crossing on a red light is dangerous.

question: わたしが ＿合図＿ をしたら、始めてください。
explanation:
合図 is read あいず and means "a signal" — the speaker will give a signal to start.
合図 (あいず) means "a signal" or "a cue" — a prearranged sign that tells someone to begin or act. The sentence 「わたしが合図をしたら、始めてください」 means "When I give the signal, please begin." The reading あいず is a kun-yomi compound: 合 (あい, mutual/fit) + 図 (ず, diagram/plan — here extended to mean a sign or figure). The voiced ず for 図 comes from the regular on-yomi ズ when 図 is the second element of a compound. The 合 here uses the kun-yomi reading あい rather than the on-yomi ゴウ or ガッ. Distractors test whether learners confuse the on-yomi ゴウ with the kun-yomi あい, and ズ with ト (the kun-yomi of 図).
✗ ごうと applies the on-yomi ゴウ for 合 and reads 図 as ト (a kun-yomi, as in 図る はかる, to plan). Neither combination matches the fixed reading あいず.
✗ あいと reads 合 correctly as あい (kun-yomi) but misreads 図 as ト instead of ズ. In 合図, 図 is voiced to ズ, not read as ト.
✗ ごうず applies the on-yomi ゴウ for 合 while reading 図 as ず. Only the kun-yomi あい is used for 合 in this compound. ごうず is not a reading of 合図.
例: 監督 (かんとく) の合図 (あいず) で選手 (せんしゅ) たちがグラウンドに出 (で) てきた。 — At the coach's signal, the players came out onto the field.

question: ＿苦しい＿ ときは、この歌を聞きます。
explanation:
苦しい is read くるしい — it means "painful / suffering".
苦しい (くるしい) = physically or emotionally painful. The sentence says 「苦 (くる) しいときは、この歌 (うた) を聞 (き) きます」 — "When times are painful, I listen to this song."
✗ かなしい = reading for 悲しい (sad). 悲 ≠ 苦.
✗ くやしい = reading for 悔しい (frustrated/regretful). Different kanji.
✗ さびしい = reading for 寂しい (lonely). Different kanji.
例: 練習 (れんしゅう) が苦 (くる) しくてもあきらめないでほしい。 — Even when practice is painful, I hope you will not give up.

question: 来月、日本に ＿出張＿ する予定です。
explanation:
出張 is read しゅっちょう and means "a business trip".
出張 (しゅっちょう) is an on-yomi compound: 出 (シュツ→しゅっ, go out) + 張 (チョウ, extend/spread). Together the word means "going out for official business" — a business trip. The sentence 「来月、日本に出張する予定です」 means "Next month, I am scheduled to go on a business trip to Japan." The phonological challenge is the gemination (double consonant): シュツ + チョウ → しゅっちょう. When the on-yomi ends in ツ (like シュツ) and the next element starts with a consonant (チ), the ツ collapses into a っ (geminate), giving しゅっ + ちょう. This is a regular sound change (促音 そくおん). Distractors test whether learners apply it correctly.
✗ しゅちゅう misses the gemination — it reads the first element as しゅ (not しゅっ) and also shortens the second to ちゅう instead of ちょう. The geminate っ and the long vowel ちょう are both essential.
✗ しゅちょう applies the correct ちょう for 張 but still misses the geminate っ before it. The correct reading has しゅっ (not しゅ), because シュツ + チョウ → しゅっちょう.
✗ しゅっちゅう applies the geminate っ correctly but shortens 張 from チョウ to ちゅう, losing the long vowel. The correct second element is ちょう (long vowel), not ちゅう.
例: 今月 (こんげつ) は出張 (しゅっちょう) が多 (おお) くて、自宅 (じたく) にほとんど戻 (もど) れなかった。 — I had so many business trips this month that I could barely return home.

question: 一つだけ ＿席＿ があいていました。
explanation:
席 is read せき, meaning "seat" — only one seat was available.
席 (せき) means "seat" or "place" — a spot to sit at a table, theater, train, or gathering. The kanji uses the on-yomi せき when it stands alone as a noun meaning a seating spot. Its on-yomi せき also appears in compounds like 席順 (せきじゅん, seating order), 席次 (せきじ, seating rank), and 出席 (しゅっせき, attendance). The kun-yomi is not commonly used for standalone reading. The sentence says: "There was only one seat 席 (せき) available." あいている = "was open/available." One seat being open in a restaurant, train car, or event is a common situational description. The distractors test four very different noun readings — かぎ (lock/key), あな (hole), and ふた (lid/cover) — none of which makes sense in the context of available seating. The key is to read 席 specifically as the seating-related term せき.
✗ かぎ is the reading of 鍵 (かぎ), meaning "key" or "lock." A key being available makes no sense in the context of a venue. 席 does not read かぎ.
✗ あな is the reading of 穴 (あな), meaning "hole." One hole being open is not a natural interpretation. 席 does not read あな.
✗ ふた is the reading of 蓋 or 二, meaning "lid" or "two." Neither fits the context of available seating. 席 does not read ふた.
例: 人気 (にんき) のレストランは週末 (しゅうまつ) になると、席 (せき) が全部 (ぜんぶ) 埋 (う) まってしまう。 — The popular restaurant fills up all its seats on weekends.

question: その木の ＿根＿ は薬にもなるそうです。
explanation:
根 is read ね and means "root" — the root of that tree can be used as medicine.
根 (ね) means "root" — the underground part of a plant that absorbs water and anchors it to the soil. The sentence 「その木の根は薬にもなるそうです」 means "I heard that the root of that tree can also be used as medicine." The kun-yomi ね is the standard reading when 根 stands alone as a noun. The on-yomi コン appears in compounds: 根本 (こんぽん, the root/foundation of something), 根拠 (こんきょ, basis/grounds for a claim), 根性 (こんじょう, grit/perseverance). Visually, 根 contains the 木 (tree/wood) radical, linking it naturally to the roots of a tree.
✗ は is the reading of 葉 (leaf) or 歯 (tooth). The root of a tree and a leaf of a tree are different parts; 根 does not read は. は/葉 is above ground; 根/ね is underground.
✗ かわ is the reading of 皮 or 川 — meaning "skin/bark" or "river". The bark of a tree and the root of a tree are different parts; 根 does not read かわ. Bark (皮, かわ) covers the outside; root (根, ね) is underground.
✗ め is the reading of 芽 (bud/sprout) or 目 (eye). A bud sprouts upward from the plant; a root grows downward. 根 does not read め.
例: 問題 (もんだい) の根本 (こんぽん) を解決 (かいけつ) しなければ、同 (おな) じことがまた起 (お) こる。 — Unless you solve the root of the problem, the same thing will happen again.

question: すみませんが、 ＿事情＿ があっで、今日は行けません。
explanation:
事情 is read じじょう and means "circumstances / reasons behind a situation".
事情 (じじょう) is an on-yomi compound: 事 (ジ, matter/thing) + 情 (ジョウ, feeling/condition). Together the word means "circumstances" — the background conditions or reasons behind a situation, especially when those reasons are personal or sensitive. The sentence 「すみませんが、事情があって、今日は行けません」 means "I am sorry, but there are circumstances, so I cannot come today." The speaker implies a personal reason without stating it directly — this is a natural use of 事情. The reading challenge is ジジョウ: both kanji use their on-yomi, and the ジョウ for 情 (long vowel) must be fully pronounced. Distractors test whether learners confuse 事 (ジ) with じこ (事故, accident) or add extra syllables.
✗ じこ (事故) means "an accident". 事 (ジ) + 故 (コ, cause/reason). An accident and personal circumstances are different — 事故 is something that happened unexpectedly, while 事情 describes the underlying state of affairs.
✗ じこう could correspond to 事項 (じこう, items/matters) or 時効 (じこう, statute of limitations). Neither is the word for personal circumstances, and 情 does not read こう.
✗ じじょ shortens 情 from ジョウ (two morae) to じょ (one mora), dropping the long vowel. 情 reads ジョウ, not じょ. じじょ is not a standard reading of 事情.
例: 先生 (せんせい) に事情 (じじょう) を話 (はな) したところ、締め切 (しめき) りを延 (の) ばしてもらえた。 — When I explained the circumstances to my teacher, they extended the deadline for me.

question: 面接の結果は、1週間以内に ＿通知＿ します。
explanation:
通知 is read つうち — 通 reads つう and 知 reads ち, meaning "notification / notice".
通知 (つうち) = notification, notice, or announcement. 通 (つう) = to pass through/communicate, 知 (ち) = to know/inform. Together: communicating information to make someone know — a notification. The sentence says 「面接 (めんせつ) の結果 (けっか) は、1週間 (しゅうかん) 以内 (いない) に通知 (つうち) します」 — "We will notify you of the interview results within one week." 通 reads つう (long vowel), not とお.
✗ とおち: reads 通 as とお. 通 reads つう (on-yomi) in this compound. とお is a kun-yomi reading of 通 used in 十 (とお, ten) or 通り (とおり, street). On-yomi compounds use つう.
✗ つうし: correct つう for 通 but wrong し for 知. 知 reads ち (unvoiced), not し. し belongs to 示 (し, to show) or 誌 (し, journal).
✗ とおし: wrong とお for 通 and wrong し for 知. Both readings are incorrect for this compound.
例: 試験 (しけん) の合否 (ごうひ) は後日 (ごじつ) 郵送 (ゆうそう) で通知 (つうち) します。 — We will notify you of the pass/fail results by mail at a later date.

question: あの人はプロのサッカー ＿選手＿ です。
explanation:
選手 is read せんしゅ because 選 takes on-yomi せん and 手 takes on-yomi しゅ, forming the standard compound for "athlete" or "player."
選手 (せんしゅ) means "athlete," "player," or "competitor" — a person selected to participate in a sport or competition. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 選 (せん) = to choose/select, and 手 (しゅ) = hand/person (used as a person suffix in compounds). Together they describe a person (手) who has been selected (選) to compete. The sentence says: "That person is a professional soccer player 選手 (せんしゅ)." プロのサッカー選手 is natural. The reading challenge: 選 reads せん (unvoiced, long vowel) — not the voiced ぜん. And 手 reads しゅ (one mora) — not the elongated しゅう. The four options test voiced vs unvoiced for 選 (せん vs ぜん) and short vs long vowel for 手 (しゅ vs しゅう). Correct: せん + しゅ = せんしゅ. 手 (しゅ) as a person suffix also appears in 投手 (とうしゅ, pitcher), 助手 (じょしゅ, assistant), and 歌手 (かしゅ, singer).
✗ ぜんしゅ voices 選 to ぜん. The on-yomi of 選 is せん (unvoiced). ぜん is the reading of 前 (before/front), 全 (all/complete), or 然 (natural state) — not 選.
✗ せんしゅう adds a long vowel to 手, extending しゅ to しゅう. 手 reads しゅ (single mora) as on-yomi in this compound. しゅう is the reading of 週 (week) or 集 (gather) — not 手 in 選手.
✗ ぜんしゅう combines both errors: voices 選 to ぜん and adds a long vowel to 手 (しゅう). Both changes are wrong. ぜんしゅう could suggest 全週 (all weeks) or similar compounds, but not 選手.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) は若 (わか) い頃 (ころ) からテニスを続 (つづ) け、今 (いま) ではプロの選手 (せんしゅ) として活躍 (かつやく) している。 — She has been playing tennis since she was young and is now active as a professional player.

question: 試合に出られなかったのは、 ＿実力＿ が足りなかったからだ。
explanation:
実力 is read じつりょく and means "real ability / true competence".
実力 (じつりょく) is an on-yomi compound: 実 (ジツ, real/actual) + 力 (リョク, power/ability). Together the word means "one's genuine ability" — what someone can actually do, as opposed to luck or appearance. The sentence 「試合に出られなかったのは、実力が足りなかったからだ」 means "The reason I could not enter the match was that my real ability was not enough." The key phonological trap is ジツ vs しつ: 実 reads ジツ (voiced, with a clear d-sound), not しつ. Learners sometimes confuse ジツ with similar-sounding syllables. The kun-yomi of 実 is み (e.g., 木の実 きのみ, fruit of a tree) or じつ, but in this compound on-yomi ジツ applies.
✗ しつりょく replaces the voiced ジツ with the unvoiced しつ. 実 reads ジツ (voiced), not しつ. There is no standard word しつりょく meaning real ability.
✗ どりょく (努力) means "effort / hard work". 努 (ど) means "to make an effort". 努力 is about trying hard, not about one's existing ability. 実力 and 努力 are complementary but distinct: 実力 is what you have; 努力 is what you do.
✗ とりょく is not a standard Japanese word. It seems to conflate 努力 (どりょく) with a different initial consonant. 努 reads ど (voiced), not と (unvoiced).
例: どんなに緊張 (きんちょう) しても、本番 (ほんばん) では実力 (じつりょく) を発揮 (はっき) できるように練習 (れんしゅう) している。 — I practice so that I can demonstrate my true ability during the real thing, no matter how nervous I am.

question: 庭に ＿生えた＿ 草にきれいな花が咲いていた。
explanation:
生えた is read はえた — 生える means "to grow / sprout naturally".
生える (はえる) = to grow/sprout naturally. Past: 生 (は) えた. 「庭 (にわ) に生 (は) えた草 (くさ) にきれいな花 (はな) が咲 (さ) いていた」 — "Beautiful flowers bloomed on the naturally grown grass."
✗ せいえた: not a real word.
✗ しょうえた: not a real word.
✗ うえた: past of 植える (to plant — transitive, intentional). This sentence describes natural growth.
例: 春 (はる) になると庭 (にわ) に雑草 (ざっそう) が生 (は) えてくる。 — When spring comes, weeds sprout in the garden.

question: 今週は ＿各地＿ でいろいろなお祭りがあります。
explanation:
各地 is read かくち because 各 takes on-yomi かく and 地 takes on-yomi ち, forming the compound meaning "various places" or "each region."
各地 (かくち) means "various places," "each region," or "across the country." Both kanji take their on-yomi: 各 (かく) = each/every, and 地 (ち) = place/land/ground. Together they describe every individual place — used when talking about events or phenomena spread across many locations. The sentence says: "This week there are various festivals 各地 (かくち) in various places." 全国各地 (ぜんこくかくち, throughout the entire country) is a common set phrase. The reading challenge is that 各 uses the on-yomi かく (two morae: か + く), not the contracted forms かっ or the voiced がく. And 地 reads ち (one mora), not じ. The options systematically test: voiced vs unvoiced (かく vs かっ) and whether you use the geminate form かっ or the straightforward かく. 各 also appears in 各自 (かくじ, each person individually) and 各種 (かくしゅ, various kinds).
✗ かっじ contracts 各 to a sokuon かっ (non-standard for this kanji) and voices 地 to じ. 各 reads かく (two morae, no contraction), and 地 reads ち (unvoiced). Neither change is supported.
✗ かっち contracts 各 to かっ and keeps 地 as ち (unvoiced, correct for 地). However, 各 does not undergo sokuon contraction in this compound — it reads kaく, not かっ. The contraction pattern is not triggered here.
✗ かくじ voices 地 to じ. 地 reads ち (unvoiced) in 各地 — じ is the reading of 字 (character) or 自 (self), not 地. The voiced じ does not apply to 地 in this compound.
例: 台風 (たいふう) の影響 (えいきょう) で、各地 (かくち) でイベントが中止 (ちゅうし) になった。 — Due to the typhoon, events were cancelled in various places across the country.

question: ＿貯金＿ がどのくらいかわかりません。
explanation:
貯金 is read ちょきん because 貯 takes on-yomi ちょ (to save/store) and 金 takes on-yomi きん (money).
貯金 (ちょきん) means "savings" or "money saved up." The compound uses the on-yomi of both characters: 貯 (ちょ) means "to accumulate" or "to store," and 金 (きん) means "money" or "gold." Together they describe money that has been stored away — savings. The sentence says: "I don't know how much savings I have." This is a common life situation, and 貯金 (ちょきん) is the standard everyday word for personal savings in Japanese. The key reading challenge is 貯 (ちょ): its on-yomi ちょ is short — one beat, not two. Learners sometimes insert a long vowel and guess ちょう, but the correct on-yomi has no long vowel. 貯 also appears in 貯蔵 (ちょぞう, storage) and 貯水 (ちょすい, water storage). The character 金 reads きん as on-yomi in compounds (現金 げんきん, 金属 きんぞく) and かね/かな as kun-yomi (お金 おかね, money).
✗ だいきん is the reading of 代金 (だいきん), meaning "the price / payment for something." It is a real word, but it uses the kanji 代, not 貯. 貯 has no reading that starts with だ.
✗ げんきん is the reading of 現金 (げんきん), meaning "cash." Cash and savings are related concepts but different words with different kanji. 貯 does not read げん.
✗ ぜいきん is the reading of 税金 (ぜいきん), meaning "tax." This is a common word students learn at N3, but 税 (ぜい) is a completely different kanji from 貯 (ちょ). Taxes and savings are opposite concepts.
例: 毎月少しずつ貯金 (ちょきん) するようにしている。 — I try to save a little money each month.

question: 隣のお宅は ＿留守＿ のようです。
explanation:
留守 is read るす — an irregular fixed compound meaning "no one is home / being away".
留守 (るす) = no one at home / being away. The sentence says 「隣 (となり) のお宅 (たく) は留守 (るす) のようです」 — "The neighboring house seems to have no one home." The reading るす is a fixed irregular compound: 留 shortens to る, 守 simplifies to す. Must be memorized as a unit. Related: 留守番電話 (るすばんでんわ, answering machine).
✗ りゅうす: on-yomi りゅう for 留 (as in 留学, りゅうがく). In 留守, the reading shortens irregularly to る.
✗ るしゅ: applies on-yomi しゅ to 守. 留守 is read as the fixed unit るす, not りゅうしゅ or るしゅ.
✗ りゅうしゅ: on-yomi for both kanji. 留守 is a fixed irregular reading るす — not derived from standard on-yomi combinations.
例: 留守 (るす) にしている間 (あいだ) はペットを友達 (ともだち) に預 (あず) けた。 — While I was away, I left my pet with a friend.

question: もう少し ＿浅い＿ 皿はありませんか。
explanation:
浅い is read あさい and means "shallow" — the speaker wants a shallower dish.
浅 (あさ) い is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "shallow". The い-adjective pair 浅い (あさい) / 深い (ふかい) maps directly onto the English shallow/deep contrast. In the sentence 「もう少し浅い皿はありませんか」, the speaker is asking a shop assistant whether they have a dish (皿, さら) that is a bit more shallow. The kun-yomi あさ is the only reading used when 浅 stands alone as an adjective; the on-yomi セン appears in compounds such as 浅瀬 (あさせ, shallow water area) or 浅学 (せんがく, shallow learning). When learners see 浅 on its own before the い ending, the reading is always あさい — the い is the adjective inflection, not part of the stem.
✗ ふかい is the reading of 深い, meaning "deep" — the exact opposite of 浅い (あさい, shallow). Choosing ふかい would reverse the meaning the speaker intends.
✗ あつい is the reading of either 厚い (thick / substantial) or 熱い (hot). Neither meaning fits 浅 (shallow), and 浅 does not carry the readings あつ- at all.
✗ うすい is the reading of 薄い, meaning "thin" or "light (color)". A thin plate and a shallow plate are different concepts; 薄 and 浅 are separate kanji with different meanings.
例: この川は浅 (あさ) いので、子どもでも安全 (あんぜん) に渡 (わた) れます。 — This river is shallow, so even children can cross it safely.

question: この ＿文章＿ は長くてわかりにくい。
explanation:
文章 is read ぶんしょう and means "a written passage" or "text".
文章 (ぶんしょう) is an on-yomi compound: 文 (ブン, sentence/text) + 章 (ショウ, section/chapter). Together the word refers to a piece of writing — a paragraph, passage, or text. The sentence 「この文章は長くてわかりにくい」 means "This passage is long and hard to understand." The phonological challenge here is the ショウ reading of 章. Learners may be tempted by ぶんしょ (dropping the long vowel) or ぶんそう (confusing ショウ with ソウ). The long vowel in ショウ is essential — it distinguishes 文章 (ぶんしょう, text) from a non-word. The kanji 章 appears in 文章 as well as in 楽章 (がくしょう, movement in music) and 序章 (じょしょう, preface/prologue).
✗ ぶんそ drops the vowel length from both components and does not correspond to any real reading of 文章.
✗ ぶんしょ shortens ショウ to しょ, losing the long vowel. There is no standard compound read ぶんしょ meaning a passage or text.
✗ ぶんそう misreads 章 as ソウ. ソウ belongs to different kanji — for example 争 (ソウ, to compete) or 想 (ソウ, to think). 章 reads ショウ, not ソウ.
例: わかりやすい文章 (ぶんしょう) を書 (か) くには、一文 (いちぶん) を短 (みじか) くすることが大切 (たいせつ) です。 — To write clear text, it is important to keep each sentence short.

question: ＿改札＿ の前で待っています。
explanation:
改札 is read かいさつ and means "ticket gate" at a train station.
改札 (かいさつ) is an on-yomi compound: 改 (カイ, check/revise) + 札 (サツ, ticket/plate). Historically the word described the act of inspecting (改める, あらためる) paper tickets (切符, きっぷ); today 改札 refers to the automated ticket barrier at the entrance to a train platform. The sentence 「改札の前で待っています」 means "I am waiting in front of the ticket gate." The reading かいさつ uses the on-yomi of both characters: カイ + サツ. Common confusion arises because 察 (サツ, observe/investigate) looks similar to 札 (サツ, tag/ticket) and shares the same on-yomi reading — this is why けいさつ (警察, police) appears as a distractor.
✗ かいじょう would correspond to 会場 (event venue) or 解錠 (unlocking). Neither meaning fits a train station gate, and 改札 does not read かいじょう.
✗ けいさつ is the reading of 警察 (police). The kanji 察 (サツ) appears in both 警察 and looks superficially similar to 札, but 改札 uses 札 (ticket tag), not 察 (investigate).
✗ けいじょう would correspond to a word built from 警 and 状 or similar — it is not a standard reading of 改札. The first kanji 改 reads カイ, not ケイ.
例: 改札 (かいさつ) を出 (で) たところで、友達 (ともだち) が待 (ま) っていた。 — My friend was waiting just outside the ticket gate.

question: その話をしたら、彼女は ＿笑って＿ いました。
explanation:
笑って is read わらって because 笑う means "to laugh / to smile", fitting the description of her laughing after hearing the story.
笑う (わらう) = to laugh or to smile. Its て-form is 笑 (わら) って. The sentence says 「その話 (はなし) をしたら、彼女 (かのじょ) は笑 (わら) っていました」 — "When I told that story, she was laughing." 笑う is the kun-yomi used for the natural action of laughing. The on-yomi しょう appears in compounds like 苦笑 (くしょう, wry smile) or 失笑 (しっしょう, involuntary laugh).
✗ こまって: て-form of 困る (こまる, to be troubled/at a loss). Being troubled is not the same as laughing. 困 and 笑 are different kanji with opposite emotional tones.
✗ おこって: て-form of 怒る (おこる/おこる, to get angry). Getting angry is the opposite of laughing. 怒 and 笑 are different kanji.
✗ うたがって: て-form of 疑う (うたがう, to suspect/doubt). Suspecting someone and laughing at a story are completely different reactions. 疑 and 笑 are different kanji.
例: 彼 (かれ) のジョークを聞 (き) いてみんなが笑 (わら) った。 — Everyone laughed upon hearing his joke.

question: 病院で ＿血液型＿ を調べました。
explanation:
血液型 is read けつえきがた and means "blood type".
血液型 (けつえきがた) is an on-yomi compound: 血 (ケツ, blood) + 液 (エキ, liquid) + 型 (がた, type/mold). The full word means "blood type" — the ABO or Rh classification of one's blood. The sentence 「病院で血液型を調べました」 means "I had my blood type checked at the hospital." The reading challenge is three-kanji: ケツ + エキ + がた. 血 uses its on-yomi ケツ (not ち, which is the kun-yomi for blood in general). 液 uses the on-yomi エキ — a tricky one because it looks similar to 役 (エキ/やく, role/service). 型 uses the kun-like compound reading がた (type). Distractors ちいきがた and けついきがた suggest wrong vowel lengths or readings.
✗ ちいきがた misreads 血液 as ちいき. ちいき (地域, region) is a real word but uses entirely different kanji. 血 reads ケツ (or ち kun-yomi), not ち+ combined with 液 (エキ).
✗ けついきがた inserts an extra い between けつ and えき, producing けつい+きがた — a non-standard segmentation. The correct reading is けつ + えき as a unit (blood + liquid), not けつい + きがた.
✗ ちえきがた misreads 血 as ちえ. 血 reads ケツ in on-yomi or ち in kun-yomi, but not ちえ. Combining ちえ with がた would suggest a word for wisdom (知恵, ちえ), not blood type.
例: 日本 (にほん) では血液型 (けつえきがた) で性格 (せいかく) を判断 (はんだん) する人 (ひと) が多 (おお) い。 — In Japan, many people judge personality by blood type.

question: ＿湖＿ の上を白い鳥が飛んでいる。
explanation:
湖 is read みずうみ because it means "lake", and white birds are flying above a lake.
湖 (みずうみ) = lake — a body of freshwater enclosed by land. The sentence says 「湖 (みずうみ) の上 (うえ) を白 (しろ) い鳥 (とり) が飛 (と) んでいる」 — "White birds are flying above the lake." 湖 is a pure kun-yomi reading: みず (water) + うみ (sea/large body of water) — literally "water-sea", a body of water that is like a sea but made of freshwater. The on-yomi is こ, as in 湖畔 (こはん, lakeside).
✗ みなと: reading for 港 (みなと, harbor/port). A harbor is a coastal docking area for ships, not an enclosed freshwater lake. 港 and 湖 are different kanji.
✗ いけ: reading for 池 (いけ, pond). A pond is much smaller than a lake and is often man-made. 池 and 湖 are different kanji of different scales.
✗ なみ: reading for 波 (なみ, wave). Waves are a feature of water surfaces, not a body of water itself. 波 and 湖 are entirely different.
例: その湖 (みずうみ) の水 (みず) はとても澄 (す) んでいて美 (うつく) しかった。 — The water of that lake was very clear and beautiful.

question: この時代の生活にどんな ＿変化＿ があったのか、調べてみたい。
explanation:
変化 is read へんか and means "change" — what changes occurred in life during this era.
変化 (へんか) is an on-yomi compound: 変 (ヘン, change/strange) + 化 (カ, transform/become). Together the word means "a change" or "transformation" — the process of something shifting from one state to another. The sentence 「この時代の生活にどんな変化があったのか、調べてみたい」 means "I want to investigate what kinds of changes occurred in the lifestyle of this era." The reading challenge is distinguishing へんか from the similar-sounding ぶんか (文化, culture) and あんか (安価, low price). 変 reads ヘン (with the h-sound), not ブン or アン. 化 reads カ in this compound.
✗ ぶんか (文化) means "culture". 文 (ブン) + 化 (カ). Cultural change and change in lifestyle are related, but 変 does not read ぶん. 文化 is a completely different compound.
✗ あんか (安価) means "low price". 安 (アン, safe/cheap) + 価 (カ, price). This is a different compound altogether; 変 does not read あん.
✗ べんか voices ヘン to ベン. 変 reads ヘン (unvoiced h-), not ベン (voiced b-). ベン belongs to 便 (convenience/stool) or 弁 (speech/petal), not 変 (change).
例: コロナ禍 (ころなか) 以降 (いこう) 、働き方 (はたらきかた) に大 (おお) きな変化 (へんか) が起 (お) きた。 — Since the COVID-19 pandemic, there have been major changes in how people work.

question: 休んでいる学生が何人いるか、 ＿伝えました＿ 。
explanation:
伝えました is read つたえました and means "conveyed / told" — reporting the number of absent students.
伝える (つたえる) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to convey", "to pass on", or "to report information to someone". The polite past form 伝えました (つたえました) expresses the completed act of conveying information. The sentence 「休んでいる学生が何人いるか、伝えました」 means "I told (someone) how many students were absent." The kanji 伝 contains the 人 (person) radical on the left, suggesting a person passing something along. Its on-yomi デン appears in: 伝統 (でんとう, tradition), 伝言 (でんごん, message), 電伝 is less common. When 伝 appears as a standalone verb, it is always read つた.
✗ こたえました is the polite past form of 答える (こたえる), meaning "to answer". Answering a question and conveying information are related but different: 答える responds to something asked, while 伝える passes information proactively.
✗ おしえました is the polite past form of 教える (おしえる), meaning "to teach" or "to tell". Teaching has a pedagogical tone; 伝える is neutral information transfer. Both can mean "to tell" but 伝えました fits better for reporting a count.
✗ かぞえました is the polite past form of 数える (かぞえる), meaning "to count". Counting the students and conveying the number to someone are two separate actions; 伝 does not read かぞ.
例: 会議 (かいぎ) の結果 (けっか) を部長 (ぶちょう) に伝 (つた) えておいてください。 — Please convey the results of the meeting to the department manager.

question: その ＿荷物＿ を運んでください。
explanation:
荷物 is read にもつ because 荷 takes on-yomi に and 物 takes on-yomi もつ, forming the standard compound for "luggage" or "a load."
荷物 (にもつ) means "luggage," "baggage," or "a package" — something carried or transported. Both kanji use on-yomi: 荷 (に) = cargo/load, and 物 (もつ/ぶつ) = thing/object. In this compound, 物 takes the reading もつ, which is somewhat unusual — most on-yomi readings of 物 are ぶつ (as in 動物 どうぶつ, animal; 食物 しょくもつ, food). The reading もつ is specific to 荷物 (にもつ) and a few other compounds. The sentence says: "Please carry that luggage 荷物 (にもつ)." The distractors test whether students confuse the reading of 荷 (に vs しな) and 物 (もつ vs もの/もの). Specifically: しなもの → 品物 (しなもの, goods/articles) uses the kanji 品 + 物 with kun-yomi readings, not the on-yomi compound 荷物.
✗ しなもつ is a non-standard hybrid reading mixing the kun-yomi しな (品, goods) with the on-yomi もつ of 物. The correct word for goods/articles is 品物 (しなもの), and the correct word for baggage is 荷物 (にもつ). しなもつ is not a real word.
✗ しなもの is the reading of 品物 (しなもの), meaning "goods" or "articles." 品物 uses the kanji 品 (しな, goods/quality) + 物 (もの), both in kun-yomi. The question tests 荷物, which uses different kanji and different readings.
✗ にもの sounds like 煮物 (にもの), a Japanese dish of simmered vegetables. It uses 煮 (に, to simmer) + 物 (もの). This is a real word but an entirely different meaning from 荷物 (luggage). 荷 and 煮 both read に, making this a careful kanji-meaning question.
例: 引っ越しの荷物 (にもつ) をトラックに積 (つ) んでもらった。 — I had my moving luggage loaded onto the truck.

question: 毎日、 ＿平均＿ 1時間くらい勉強しています。
explanation:
平均 is read へいきん — 平 reads へい and 均 reads きん, meaning "average".
平均 (へいきん) = average/mean. 平 (へい) = flat/equal, 均 (きん) = even/balanced. 「毎日 (まいにち) 、平均 (へいきん) 1時間 (じかん) くらい勉強 (べんきょう) しています」 — "I study about an average of one hour every day."
✗ へんきん: へん for 平 is wrong. 平 reads へい (long vowel), not へん.
✗ へんやく: wrong へん for 平 and wrong やく for 均. 均 reads きん.
✗ へいやく: correct へい for 平 but wrong やく for 均. 均 reads きん.
例: このクラスの平均点 (へいきんてん) は75点 (てん) でした。 — The average score in this class was 75 points.

question: この学校では、留学生に奨学金が ＿支給＿ されます。
explanation:
支給 is read しきゅう and means "provision / disbursement" — scholarships are provided to international students.
支給 (しきゅう) is an on-yomi compound: 支 (シ, support/branch) + 給 (キュウ, supply/provide). Together the word means "providing (funds or materials) to someone" — used for salary payments, benefit provision, and scholarship disbursement. The sentence 「この学校では、留学生に奨学金が支給されます」 means "At this school, scholarships are provided to international students." The reading challenge is シキュウ: 支 reads シ (short, not シュ), and 給 reads キュウ (long vowel, two morae). Distractors confuse シ with ジ (voiced) or misread キュウ as ごう or じ.
✗ しごう misreads 給 as ごう instead of きゅう. 給 reads キュウ (the k-sound followed by yuu), not ごう. ごう belongs to 合 (combine) or 号 (number).
✗ じきゅう voices the first kanji — 支 reads シ (unvoiced s-), not ジ (voiced z-). While the second element キュウ is correct, the first kanji reading is wrong.
✗ じごう gets both readings wrong — voices 支 to ジ and misreads 給 as ごう. Both errors combined.
例: 会社 (かいしゃ) から交通費 (こうつうひ) が支給 (しきゅう) されるので、通勤 (つうきん) の負担 (ふたん) が少 (すく) ない。 — Since commuting expenses are covered by the company, the financial burden of commuting is low.

question: このグラフは、毎月の雨の量を ＿表した＿ ものです。
explanation:
表した is read あらわした and means "represented / showed" — a graph showing monthly rainfall.
表す (あらわす) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to represent", "to express", or "to display". The ta-form 表した (あらわした) expresses the completed representation. The sentence 「このグラフは、毎月の雨の量を表したものです」 means "This graph is something that represents the monthly rainfall." The kanji 表 reads あらわ when used as a verb. Note that the correct answer has a period after it (「あらわした。」) in the options, which is part of the display format.
