The analysis is identical to hash 19a9b7d975ce1102 — both test あらわす (表す) in the context of a graph representing data. The distinction from similar verbs holds: 示す (しめす) points out directly, 表す (あらわす) reveals or makes something visible.
✗ しめした is the past form of 示す (しめす), meaning "to indicate / to present". While 示す and 表す can both describe visual information, 表 does not read しめ. 示す tends to be used for direct pointing or demonstrating.
✗ さした is the past form of 指す (さす), meaning "to point to". Pointing at something and representing it in a graph are different; 表 does not read さ.
✗ うつした is the past form of 写す (うつす), meaning "to copy" or "to photograph". Copying and representing are different; 表 does not read うつ.
例: このグラフは気温 (きおん) の変化 (へんか) を折 (おり) れ線 (せん) で表 (あらわ) しています。 — This graph represents the changes in temperature as a line chart.

question: 会場には大勢の ＿観客＿ がいた。
explanation:
観客 is read かんきゃく — 観 reads かん and 客 reads きゃく, meaning "audience / spectators".
観客 (かんきゃく) = audience or spectators. 観 (かん) = to watch, 客 (きゃく) = guest/visitor. 「会場 (かいじょう) には大勢 (おおぜい) の観客 (かんきゃく) がいた」 — "There was a large audience at the venue." Key: 客 reads きゃく (unvoiced k), not ぎゃく (voiced g).
✗ けんぎゃく: wrong けん for 観 and voiced ぎゃく for 客. 観 reads かん; 客 reads きゃく (unvoiced).
✗ かんぎゃく: correct かん for 観 but voiced ぎゃく for 客. 客 reads きゃく (unvoiced k), not ぎゃく. ぎゃく = reading for 逆 (reverse).
✗ けんきゃく: wrong けん for 観. 観 reads かん, not けん.
例: コンサートには数千人 (すうせんにん) の観客 (かんきゃく) が集 (あつ) まった。 — Thousands of audience members gathered for the concert.

question: 田村さんが ＿払って＿ くれました。
explanation:
払って is read はらって, meaning "paid" — Tamura-san paid on behalf of the speaker.
払う (はらう) means "to pay" or "to brush off." In this context, the meaning is clearly "to pay." The sentence says: "Tamura-san paid for me." The te-form 払って (はらって) combined with くれました expresses that Tamura-san did the action as a favor to the speaker. The kanji 払 uses the kun-yomi はら in verb form. Its on-yomi ふつ appears in the formal compound 払拭 (ふっしょく, to wipe away), but in everyday speech the verb always reads はらう. The radical of 払 is 扌(手, hand), consistent with many action verbs: 指 (ゆび, finger), 持 (もつ, to hold), 払 (はらう, to pay/brush). The distractors are all te-form verbs that could plausibly follow a human subject, which is why this question tests careful reading of the kanji 払 rather than grammatical intuition.
✗ くばって is the te-form of 配る (くばる), meaning "to distribute" or "to hand out." Distributing something and paying money are different actions. 配 does not read はら, and 払 does not read くば.
✗ かざって is the te-form of 飾る (かざる), meaning "to decorate." Decorating and paying have nothing in common semantically, and 払 does not read かざ.
✗ ひろって is the te-form of 拾う (ひろう), meaning "to pick up" (something off the ground). Picking something up and paying are unrelated actions. 払 does not read ひろ.
例: 電気代 (でんきだい) をまだ払 (はら) っていないので、早 (はや) く払 (はら) わなければならない。 — I haven't paid the electricity bill yet, so I need to pay it soon.

question: ホテルには3時ごろ ＿到着＿ します。
explanation:
到着 is read とうちゃく because 到 takes on-yomi とう and 着 takes on-yomi ちゃく, forming the standard word for "arrival."
到着 (とうちゃく) means "arrival" — the act of reaching a destination. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 到 (とう) means "to reach" or "to arrive at" (as in 到達 とうたつ, to reach a goal), and 着 (ちゃく) means "to arrive" or "to wear" (as in 着く つく, to arrive, and 着替え きがえ, change of clothes). Together 到着 is the formal Sino-Japanese word for arrival, used in timetables, announcements, and polite speech. The sentence says: "I will arrive 到着 (とうちゃく) at the hotel around 3 o'clock." Two reading traps here. First, 到 must keep its long vowel: とう (two morae), not the short と. Second, 着 reads ちゃく in this compound (on-yomi), not the kun-yomi つく or the shorter ちゃ. The combination とうちゃく is also the standard form in station announcements: ○○着 (ちゃく) means "arrival at ○○."
✗ とうつく keeps the long vowel とう for 到 correctly, but uses the kun-yomi つく for 着. In this Sino-Japanese compound, 着 takes its on-yomi ちゃく, not the kun-yomi つく (which is used in verb form: 着く). The compound 到着 always reads とうちゃく.
✗ とちゃく drops the long vowel from 到, shortening とう to と. 到 (とう) requires the long vowel — reading it as と alone reduces it to one mora and misrepresents the character's on-yomi.
✗ とつく combines the truncated reading と (dropping the long vowel from 到) with the kun-yomi つく for 着. Both halves are wrong: 到 must be とう, and 着 must be ちゃく in this compound.
例: 飛行機 (ひこうき) は予定 (よてい) より30分早 (ぷんはや) く到着 (とうちゃく) した。 — The plane arrived 30 minutes earlier than scheduled.

question: 山下さんが説明を ＿加えました＿ 。
explanation:
加えました is read くわえました and means "added" — Yamashita added to the explanation.
加える (くわえる) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to add" or "to supplement". The polite past form 加えました (くわえました) expresses the completed act of adding something. The sentence 「山下さんが説明を加えました」 means "Yamashita added to the explanation." The kanji 加 contains the 力 (power/force) radical on the right, suggesting adding strength or impact. Its on-yomi カ appears in compounds: 追加 (ついか, addition), 加減 (かげん, adjustment/moderation), 参加 (さんか, participation). When 加 appears as a standalone verb with える, the reading is always くわえ.
✗ つたえました is the polite past form of 伝える (つたえる), meaning "to convey / to communicate". Conveying information and adding to information are related but different; 加 does not read つたえ.
✗ おえました is the polite past form of 終える (おえる), meaning "to finish / to complete". Finishing an explanation and adding to it are opposite actions; 加 does not read おえ.
✗ かえました is the polite past form of 変える (かえる), meaning "to change", or 帰る (かえる), "to return". Changing an explanation and adding to it are different; 加 does not read かえ.
例: スープに少 (すこ) しコショウを加 (くわ) えると、味 (あじ) が引 (ひ) き締 (し) まる。 — Adding a little pepper to the soup tightens the flavor.

question: 今から ＿訓練＿ を行います。
explanation:
訓練 is read くんれん because 訓 takes on-yomi くん and 練 takes on-yomi れん, forming the standard compound for "training" or "drill."
訓練 (くんれん) means "training," "drill," or "practice" — systematic repeated practice to build skills, especially in emergency procedures, military, or sports contexts. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 訓 (くん) = instruction/reading/teaching, and 練 (れん) = to train/to practice repeatedly. Together they describe systematic instructional practice. The sentence says: "We will now conduct training 訓練 (くんれん)." 訓練を行います is typical in emergency drills, workplace training, or military exercises. The reading challenge: 訓 reads くん (unvoiced, two morae: く + ん), not the voiced ぐん. ぐん is the reading of 軍 (army) or 郡 (county district), not 訓. The four options test all voiced/unvoiced combinations: くんれん (correct) vs くんれい (wrong 令) vs ぐんれい (voiced + wrong) vs ぐんれん (voiced). 練 reads れん (unvoiced) — not the voiced れい. 令 reads れい (not れん); 令 is used in 命令 (めいれい, order) and 法令 (ほうれい, ordinance).
✗ くんれい changes 練 (れん, to train) to a れい reading. 練 reads れん, not れい. れい is the reading of 令 (order) or 礼 (etiquette). 訓令 (くんれい) is actually a real administrative term meaning "directive/instruction" — but it uses 令 (order), not 練 (training). 訓令 and 訓練 are different words.
✗ ぐんれい voices 訓 to ぐん and changes 練 to れい. The on-yomi of 訓 is くん (unvoiced). ぐん is the reading of 軍 (military/army). 軍令 (ぐんれい) means "military order" — a completely different compound using different kanji.
✗ ぐんれん voices 訓 to ぐん while reading 練 correctly as れん. 訓 reads くん (unvoiced), not ぐん. ぐんれん might suggest 軍練 (military drill), but the question tests 訓練, which reads くんれん.
例: 毎年 (まいとし) 消防訓練 (しょうぼうくんれん) が行 (おこな) われ、全員 (ぜんいん) が参加 (さんか) している。 — Fire drills are held every year, and everyone participates.

question: この ＿豆＿ はスープに使うといいですよ。
explanation:
豆 is read まめ because it means "bean", and the sentence recommends using beans in soup.
豆 (まめ) = bean or legume. The sentence says 「この豆 (まめ) はスープに使 (つか) うといいですよ」 — "These beans are great to use in soup." 豆 read as まめ is the kun-yomi used when referring to the food item. The kanji 豆 is itself a radical (a pictograph of a ceremonial vessel or a bean pod). 豆 also reads とう in compounds: 大豆 (だいず, soybean), 納豆 (なっとう, fermented soybeans).
✗ こな: reading for 粉 (こな, flour/powder). Flour and beans are different ingredients — 粉 and 豆 are different kanji.
✗ いも: reading for 芋 (いも, potato/taro/yam). Root vegetables and beans are different foods. 芋 and 豆 are different kanji.
✗ かい: reading for 貝 (かい, shellfish/shell). Shellfish and beans are different foods. 貝 and 豆 are different kanji with completely different meanings.
例: この料理 (りょうり) には豆 (まめ) がたっぷり入 (はい) っていて栄養 (えいよう) がある。 — This dish has plenty of beans in it and is nutritious.

question: 社会には ＿共通＿ のルールがあります。
explanation:
共通 is read きょうつう and means "common / shared by all".
共通 (きょうつう) is an on-yomi compound: 共 (キョウ, together/shared) + 通 (ツウ, pass through/common). Together the word means "common to all" or "mutually shared". The sentence 「社会には共通のルールがあります」 means "Society has rules that are common to everyone." The reading challenge is distinguishing キョウ (共) from コウ (交): 共 reads キョウ (together), while 交 reads コウ (exchange/cross). The full on-yomi pair キョウ + ツウ requires the long vowel ツウ (two morae). Distractor きょうつ drops that final mora. 共 appears in: 共同 (きょうどう, joint/cooperative), 共有 (きょうゆう, shared), 公共 (こうきょう, public).
✗ きょうつ drops the long vowel from ツウ (通). The correct on-yomi of 通 is ツウ (two morae), not ツ (one mora). Shortening it produces a non-word.
✗ こうつう (交通) means "traffic" or "transportation". 交 (コウ, exchange/cross) + 通 (ツウ, pass through). This is a real word but uses a different first kanji — 交 (こう), not 共 (きょう).
✗ こうつ drops the long vowel from ツウ and also misreads the first kanji as コウ. Both errors combined produce a non-word with the wrong first kanji reading.
例: 二人 (ふたり) には音楽 (おんがく) という共通 (きょうつう) の趣味 (しゅみ) がある。 — The two of them share music as a common hobby.

question: 来年から ＿税金＿ が上がるそうだ。
explanation:
税金 is read ぜいきん because 税 takes on-yomi ぜい and 金 takes on-yomi きん, forming the standard compound for "tax."
税金 (ぜいきん) means "tax" — money paid to the government. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 税 (ぜい) = tax/duty, and 金 (きん) = money/gold. Together they describe tax money — the monetary payment to government authority. The sentence says: "I heard that taxes 税金 (ぜいきん) will increase next year." 税金が上がる = "taxes will go up" is a common social and political topic. The reading challenge: 税 reads ぜい (voiced, long vowel), not the unvoiced せい or the contracted ぜっ. The four options test the voiced/unvoiced distinction for 税 (ぜい vs せい) and the contracted sokuon for both syllables (ぜっ vs ぜい). Correct: ぜい (voiced, long vowel) + きん = ぜいきん. 税 also appears in 消費税 (しょうひぜい, consumption tax), 所得税 (しょとくぜい, income tax), and 免税 (めんぜい, tax-free). 金 as on-yomi きん appears in 現金 (げんきん, cash), 金額 (きんがく, amount of money), and 税金 (ぜいきん).
✗ ぜっきん contracts 税 to a sokuon ぜっ. 税 reads ぜい (two morae: ぜ + い), not the contracted ぜっ (single mora with glottal stop). There is no reason for a sokuon contraction here.
✗ せいきん unvoices 税 to せい. The on-yomi of 税 is ぜい (voiced). The voiced ぜ is essential — unvoicing it to せ produces a non-standard reading that does not correspond to 税. せいきん might suggest 清金 or 正金 — different words.
✗ せっきん combines both errors: unvoices 税 to せ and contracts to a sokuon せっ. The on-yomi of 税 is ぜい — voiced and with a long vowel. せっきん does not correspond to any standard reading of 税金.
例: 消費税 (しょうひぜい) が上 (あ) がると、日用品 (にちようひん) の値段 (ねだん) も高 (たか) くなる。 — When consumption tax goes up, the prices of daily necessities also rise.

question: ここは ＿汚い＿ から、ほかの所へ行きましょう。
explanation:
汚い is read きたない and means "dirty / filthy" — the speaker suggests going somewhere else.
汚い (きたない) is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "dirty", "filthy", or "messy". The sentence 「ここは汚いから、ほかの所へ行きましょう」 means "This place is dirty, so let us go somewhere else." The reading きたない uses a kun-yomi that is not immediately predictable from the kanji's visual form — this is a memorization point for N3. The on-yomi オ appears in: 汚染 (おせん, pollution/contamination), 汚点 (おてん, stain/blemish), 汚職 (おしょく, corruption). The four distractors test whether learners distinguish the correct adjective meaning from related sensory adjectives: narrow (せまい), smelly (くさい), noisy (うるさい).
✗ せまい is the reading of 狭い, meaning "narrow". A narrow place and a dirty place are different; 汚 does not read せま.
✗ くさい is the reading of 臭い, meaning "smelly". Dirty and smelly often co-occur, but they are different adjectives; 汚 does not read くさ.
✗ うるさい means "noisy / annoying". Noise and dirtiness are unrelated properties; 汚 does not read うるさ.
例: 公園 (こうえん) のトイレが汚 (きたな) かったので、別 (べつ) の場所 (ばしょ) のトイレを使 (つか) った。 — The toilet in the park was dirty, so I used a toilet somewhere else.

question: ＿商品＿ に傷がないか確認します。
explanation:
商品 is read しょうひん — 商 reads しょう and 品 reads ひん, meaning "merchandise / product".
商品 (しょうひん) = merchandise, product, or goods for sale. 商 (しょう) = commerce/trade, 品 (ひん) = item/quality. Together: a commercial item — a product. The sentence says 「商品 (しょうひん) に傷 (きず) がないか確認 (かくにん) します」 — "I will check whether there are any scratches on the product." 商 reads しょう (long vowel, two morae), not shortened しょ. 品 reads ひん (voiced n at end), not ひ or びん.
✗ しょひん: shortens 商 to しょ, dropping the long vowel. 商 reads しょう (two morae), not しょ.
✗ せいひん: reads 商 as せい. せい is not a reading for 商; せい belongs to 製 (せい, manufacture) or 生 (せい, life/raw). せいひん (製品) = manufactured product, but the kanji on the page is 商, not 製.
✗ せひん: shortened せ for 商 (wrong) and ひん for 品 (correct). 商 reads しょう, not せ.
例: この商品 (しょうひん) は品質 (ひんしつ) が高 (たか) くて人気 (にんき) がある。 — This product is popular because of its high quality.

question: まだ ＿冷えて＿ いないので、もう少し待ってください。
explanation:
冷えて is read ひえて because 冷える means "to get cold / to cool down", fitting the instruction to wait for something to chill.
冷える (ひえる) = to get cold, to cool down (intransitive). Its て-form is 冷 (ひ) えて. The sentence says 「まだ冷 (ひ) えていないので、もう少 (すこ) し待 (ま) ってください」 — "It has not cooled down yet, so please wait a little longer." 冷える is intransitive; its transitive counterpart is 冷やす (ひやす, to chill/cool something).
✗ もえて: て-form of 燃える (もえる, to burn). Burning is the opposite of getting cold. 燃 and 冷 are different kanji.
✗ にえて: て-form of 煮える (にえる, to boil/simmer). Boiling involves heat, not cooling. 煮 and 冷 are different kanji.
✗ うえて: て-form of 飢える (うえる, to starve/be hungry) or 植える (うえる, to plant). Neither meaning relates to temperature. 飢/植 and 冷 are different kanji.
例: 夏 (なつ) は冷 (ひ) えたビールが一番 (いちばん) おいしい。 — In summer, cold beer is the most delicious.

question: 体の調子がよくないので、 ＿早退し＿ た。
explanation:
早退し is read そうたいし and means "left early" — the speaker left early because they were not feeling well.
早退 (そうたい) is an on-yomi compound: 早 (ソウ, early) + 退 (タイ, withdraw/leave). Together the word means "leaving early" — departing from school or work before the normal end time due to illness or some other reason. The sentence 「体の調子がよくないので、早退した」 means "Because I was not feeling well, I left early." The reading challenge is ソウタイ: both kanji use their on-yomi. 早 reads ソウ (not はや in compounds — はや is the kun-yomi for the adjective 早い). 退 reads タイ. Distractors test the voiced vs. unvoiced boundary: そうてい, ぞうたい, ぞうてい.
✗ そうてい misreads 退 as テイ instead of タイ. 退 reads タイ (with an a-vowel), not テイ (with an e-vowel). テイ belongs to 停 (stop) or 定 (fixed), not 退 (withdraw).
✗ ぞうたい voices 早 to ゾウ. 早 reads ソウ (unvoiced s-sound), not ゾウ (voiced z-sound). ゾウ belongs to 像 (image) or 象 (elephant), not 早 (early).
✗ ぞうてい voices 早 (should be ソウ) and misreads 退 as テイ (should be タイ). Both errors combined.
例: 熱 (ねつ) が出 (で) てきたので、上司 (じょうし) に早退 (そうたい) を申 (もう) し出 (で) た。 — When I developed a fever, I asked my supervisor for permission to leave early.

question: 大事なことばに ＿下線を＿ 引いてください。
explanation:
下線 is read かせん because both kanji take their on-yomi in this compound, giving the compound its standard phonetic shape.
下線 (かせん) means "underline" — a line drawn under text to mark it. Both characters take their on-yomi here: 下 (か) and 線 (せん). This on-yomi pattern is typical for two-kanji Sino-Japanese compounds related to writing and annotation. The sentence says: "Please draw an underline 下線 (かせん) under important words." The verb 引く (ひく) meaning "to draw (a line)" pairs naturally with 下線 (かせん). Note that 下 has two common readings: the on-yomi か appears in compounds like 下線 (かせん) and 地下 (ちか, underground), while the kun-yomi した appears in 下 (した, below) and 下さい (ください). Similarly, 線 (せん) is used in 新幹線 (しんかんせん, bullet train) and 直線 (ちょくせん, straight line). When these two combine, the double-on-yomi reading か + せん = かせん is the only standard option. Learners sometimes hesitate between か and ge-, but 下 only takes its voiced げ reading in classical forms, not in modern compounds like this one.
✗ げぜん would require 下 to read げ and 線 to read ぜん. The voiced げ is not a standard on-yomi for 下 in modern compounds, and ぜん is not a reading of 線 at all. This combination does not correspond to any real word.
✗ かぜん assigns か to 下 correctly, but ぜん is not a reading of 線. The character 線 reads せん, not ぜん. Voicing the second syllable here creates a non-existent reading.
✗ げせん gives 下 the reading げ, which is not its standard modern on-yomi. 下 reads か (on-yomi) or した/しも/さ (kun-yomi). The form げ does not match 下 in this compound.
例: 重要な部分 (じゅうような ぶぶん) に下線 (かせん) を引 (ひ) いてください。 — Please draw an underline under the important part.

question: ＿転んだ＿ ときに、割ってしまったみたいです。
explanation:
転んだ is read ころんだ and means "fell / tumbled" — fell and seems to have broken something.
転ぶ (ころぶ) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to fall down" or "to tumble". The n-form past 転んだ (ころんだ) expresses the completed action of falling. The sentence 「転んだときに、割ってしまったみたいです」 means "It seems I broke (something) when I fell." The kanji 転 contains the 車 (vehicle/wheel) radical, suggesting rotation or rolling — consistent with tumbling. Its on-yomi テン appears in: 転職 (てんしょく, job change), 回転 (かいてん, rotation), 逆転 (ぎゃくてん, reversal). When 転 stands as the falling/tumbling verb, the reading is always ころ.
✗ はこんだ is the past form of 運ぶ (はこぶ), meaning "to carry / to transport". Carrying something and falling down are different; 転 does not read はこ.
✗ ふんだ is the past form of 踏む (ふむ), meaning "to step on". Stepping on something and tumbling down are different actions; 転 does not read ふ.
✗ つつんだ is the past form of 包む (つつむ), meaning "to wrap". Wrapping and falling are completely different; 転 does not read つつ.
例: 雨 (あめ) で道 (みち) が濡 (ぬ) れていたため、転 (ころ) んで膝 (ひざ) をすりむいた。 — Because the road was wet from rain, I slipped and fell and scraped my knee.

question: 今日の講義の ＿主要な＿ テーマは二つです。
explanation:
主要な is read しゅような — 主 reads しゅ (main) and 要 reads よう (important), meaning "main / principal".
主要 (しゅよう) = main, principal, most important. 主 (しゅ) = main/master, 要 (よう) = important/essential. Together: the most important elements. The sentence says 「今日 (きょう) の講義 (こうぎ) の主要 (しゅよう) なテーマは二 (ふた) つです」 — "The main themes of today's lecture are two." As a な-adjective before a noun, it becomes 主要な (しゅような). Note: 主 reads しゅ (one mora, short), not じゅ (voiced) or しゅよ (truncated).
✗ じゅよう: voices 主 to じゅ. 主 reads しゅ (unvoiced), not じゅ (voiced). じゅ belongs to kanji like 授 (じゅ, to grant) or 受 (じゅ, to receive).
✗ しゅよ: shortens よう to よ for 要. 要 reads よう (two morae, long vowel), not よ alone. The long vowel is essential.
✗ じゅよ: both wrong — voiced じゅ for 主 and shortened よ for 要.
例: この会議 (かいぎ) の主要 (しゅよう) な議題 (ぎだい) は三 (みっ) つです。 — The main agenda items of this meeting are three.

question: 今でもときどき ＿過去＿ のことを思い出す。
explanation:
過去 is read かこ because 過 takes on-yomi か and 去 takes on-yomi こ, forming the short two-mora compound meaning "the past."
過去 (かこ) means "the past" — time that has already passed. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 過 (か) = to pass/exceed, and 去 (こ/きょ) = to leave/go away. Together 過去 describes time that has passed and gone. The sentence says: "Even now I sometimes remember things from the past 過去 (かこ)." The critical reading issue is that neither syllable carries a long vowel: か (one mora) + こ (one mora) = かこ (two morae total). Learners may be tempted to add a long vowel — かきょ, かこう, or かきょう — influenced by the Japanese word 経緯 (いきさつ, circumstances) or other similar-sounding past-related expressions. But 過去 is exactly か + こ — two short morae, no more. 過 also appears in 過ぎる (すぎる, to pass by/too much) and 通過 (つうか, to pass through). 去 also appears in 去年 (きょねん, last year) and 退去 (たいきょ, evacuation).
✗ かきょ assigns 去 the reading きょ. The on-yomi of 去 includes both こ (used in 過去) and きょ (used in 去年 きょねん, last year). In the compound 過去, 去 reads こ, not きょ. The reading split of 去 (こ vs きょ) is a well-known trap.
✗ かこう adds a long vowel to 去, making it こう. The on-yomi of 去 is a short こ in this word — no long vowel. こう would correspond to 光 or 行 or other kanji, not 去.
✗ かきょう combines both errors: the きょ reading of 去 and an added long vowel う. Neither change is supported by the standard reading of 過去. かきょう sounds like 花京 or other unrelated words.
例: 過去 (かこ) の失敗 (しっぱい) を反省 (はんせい) して、次 (つぎ) に活 (い) かすことが大切 (たいせつ) だ。 — It is important to reflect on past failures and make use of them next time.

question: 中村部長と ＿直接＿ 話した。
explanation:
直接 is read ちょくせつ — 直 reads ちょく and 接 reads せつ, meaning "directly / face-to-face".
直接 (ちょくせつ) = directly, without intermediary. 直 (ちょく) = straight/direct, 接 (せつ) = to connect/touch. 「中村部長 (なかむらぶちょう) と直接 (ちょくせつ) 話 (はな) した」 — "I spoke directly with Section Chief Nakamura." Both ちょく and せつ are unvoiced.
✗ ちょくぜつ: correct ちょく for 直 but voices 接 to ぜつ. 接 reads せつ (unvoiced s), not ぜつ (voiced z). ぜつ belongs to 絶 (ぜつ, to cut off).
✗ ちょうせつ: elongates ちょく to ちょう. 直 reads ちょく (with final k), not ちょう. ちょう belongs to 長 or 調.
✗ ちょうぜつ: both wrong — ちょう for 直 (should be ちょく) and ぜつ for 接 (should be せつ).
例: 直接 (ちょくせつ) 連絡 (れんらく) するよりメールのほうがいい。 — Sending an email is better than contacting directly.

question: これはすぐには ＿燃えません＿ 。
explanation:
燃えません is read もえません because 燃える means "to burn / to catch fire", fitting the description of something that does not burn.
燃える (もえる) = to burn, to catch fire (intransitive). Its negative polite form is 燃 (も) えません. The sentence says 「これはすぐには燃 (も) えません」 — "This will not burn easily." 燃える is the intransitive verb; its transitive counterpart is 燃やす (もやす, to burn something). The kanji 燃 contains 火 (fire) on the left and 然 on the right — 然 itself contains 灬 (fire) at the bottom, doubling the fire imagery.
✗ にえません: negative polite of 煮える (にえる, to boil/simmer — food cooking in liquid). Boiling food and burning are different processes. 煮 and 燃 are different kanji.
✗ ひえません: negative polite of 冷える (ひえる, to get cold/to chill). Getting cold is the opposite of burning. 冷 and 燃 are different kanji.
✗ きえません: negative polite of 消える (きえる, to disappear/go out — as in a flame going out). While fire-related, 消える means to be extinguished, not to burn. 消 and 燃 are different kanji.
例: このゴミは燃 (も) えないゴミなので、分 (わ) けて捨 (す) ててください。 — This trash is non-burnable, so please separate it when discarding.

question: この ＿位置＿ に車を止めてください。
explanation:
位置 is read いち — 位 reads い and 置 reads ち, meaning "position / location".
位置 (いち) = position or location — where something is placed. 位 (い) = rank/position, 置 (ち) = to place/put. Together: the place where something is set. The sentence says 「この位置 (いち) に車 (くるま) を止 (と) めてください」 — "Please park the car in this position." Compare: 位置 (いち, abstract position/location) vs 場所 (ばしょ, physical place) — 位置 is more precise and technical.
✗ とじ: wrong readings for both kanji. 位 reads い (not と) and 置 reads ち (not じ). とじ belongs to 閉じる (とじる, to close) or 綴じる (とじる, to bind).
✗ いじ: correct い for 位 but wrong じ (voiced) for 置. 置 reads ち (unvoiced), not じ (voiced). いじ means "stubbornness / mean-spiritedness" (意地, いじ) — a different word.
✗ とち: wrong と for 位. 位 reads い, not と. とち reads 土地 (とち, land/property) — a completely different word.
例: 家具 (かぐ) の位置 (いち) を変 (か) えたら、部屋 (へや) が広 (ひろ) く感 (かん) じた。 — After changing the position of the furniture, the room felt more spacious.

question: ＿計算＿ ができたので見てください。
explanation:
計算 is read けいさん — 計 reads けい and 算 reads さん, meaning "calculation".
計算 (けいさん) = calculation or arithmetic. 計 (けい) = to measure/count, 算 (さん) = to calculate/count. Together: performing a numerical calculation. The sentence says 「計算 (けいさん) ができたので見 (み) てください」 — "The calculation is done, please take a look." The key: 算 reads さん (unvoiced s), not ざん (voiced z). Compare: 計算 (calculation) vs 計画 (けいかく, plan) — both start with けい but differ in the second kanji.
✗ けいかく: correct けい for 計 but wrong かく for 算. 算 reads さん, not かく. かく is the reading for 画 (picture/plan) in 計画 (けいかく, plan) — a different second kanji.
✗ けいざん: correct けい for 計 but voices 算 to ざん. 算 reads さん (unvoiced s), not ざん (voiced z).
✗ けいがく: correct けい for 計 but uses がく for 算. がく belongs to 学 (がく, study/learning) or 楽 (がく, music). 算 reads さん.
例: 頭 (あたま) の中 (なか) で計算 (けいさん) するのが得意 (とくい) だ。 — I am good at doing calculations in my head.

question: ずっとパソコンを使っていて疲れたので、腕を ＿回して＿ みた。
explanation:
回して is read まわして and means "rotating / turning" — the speaker turns their arm to relieve tiredness.
回す (まわす) is a transitive verb meaning "to turn" or "to rotate (something)". The te-form 回して (まわして) here is followed by みた (tried doing), giving the meaning "tried turning (it)". The sentence says: 「ずっとパソコンを使っていて疲れたので、腕を回してみた」 — "Because I had been using a computer for a long time and got tired, I tried rotating my arm." The kanji 回 is read まわ with its kun-yomi when used as a standalone verb. Its on-yomi カイ appears in compounds like 回転 (かいてん, rotation) and 回答 (かいとう, answer/response). The physical action of circling one's arm matches the core meaning of 回 — going around in a circuit.
✗ おして is the te-form of 押す (おす), meaning "to push". Pushing an arm and rotating an arm are different actions, and 回 does not read おし.
✗ おろして is the te-form of 降ろす (おろす) or 下ろす, meaning "to lower / to put down". Lowering an arm and rotating it are different motions; 回 has no reading おろ.
✗ のばして is the te-form of 伸ばす (のばす), meaning "to stretch / to extend". Stretching an arm and rotating it are distinct movements; 回 does not read のば.
例: 首 (くび) をゆっくり回 (まわ) して、肩 (かた) のこりをほぐした。 — I slowly rotated my neck to loosen up the stiffness in my shoulders.

question: ここは ＿禁煙＿ です。
explanation:
禁煙 is read きんえん — 禁 reads きん and 煙 reads えん, meaning "no smoking".
禁煙 (きんえん) = no smoking / smoking prohibition. 禁 (きん) = to prohibit/forbid, 煙 (えん) = smoke. Together: smoke is forbidden — no smoking. The sentence says 「ここは禁煙 (きんえん) です」 — "Smoking is prohibited here." 禁 reads きん (with the nasal ん), not きね. 煙 reads えん (on-yomi), not ねん or ねん.
✗ きねん: reads 禁 as きね instead of きん. 禁 reads きん (with nasal ん at the end). きねん means "commemoration" (記念, きねん) — a completely different word.
✗ きえん: reads 禁 as き (dropping the ん). 禁 must read きん (two morae ending in ん). きえん might suggest 気炎 (flame of enthusiasm) but is not how 禁煙 reads.
✗ きんねん: correct きん for 禁 but reads 煙 as ねん instead of えん. 煙 reads えん (on-yomi starting with え). きんねん means "recent years" (近年, きんねん) — a different word.
例: この建物内 (たてものない) は全面禁煙 (ぜんめんきんえん) です。 — The entire interior of this building is a no-smoking zone.

question: きれいに ＿結んで＿ ください。
explanation:
結んで is read むすんで and means "tie / knot (it)" — please tie it neatly.
結ぶ (むすぶ) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to tie", "to knot", or "to connect". The te-form 結んで (むすんで) in the sentence 「きれいに結んでください」 means "Please tie it neatly." The kanji 結 contains the 糸 (thread/yarn) radical, visually consistent with tying or connecting threads. Its on-yomi ケツ appears in compounds: 結果 (けっか, result), 結婚 (けっこん, marriage), 結局 (けっきょく, in the end). When 結 appears as a standalone verb with む, the reading is always むすぶ. The action of tying and the concept of connecting (as in 結婚, "tying two lives together") share this same kanji.
✗ たたんで is the te-form of 畳む (たたむ), meaning "to fold". Folding something and tying something are different actions; 結 does not read たたん.
✗ つつんで is the te-form of 包む (つつむ), meaning "to wrap". Wrapping and tying are related but different — wrapping covers something, tying creates a knot. 結 does not read つつん.
✗ ならんで is the te-form of 並ぶ (ならぶ), meaning "to line up / to stand in a row". Lining up and tying are entirely different; 結 does not read ならん.
例: 誕生日 (たんじょうび) のプレゼントをリボンで結 (むす) んで渡 (わた) した。 — I tied a ribbon around the birthday present and handed it over.

question: ＿手術＿ をしなくても治りますから、大丈夫ですよ。
explanation:
手術 is read しゅじゅつ — 手 reads しゅ and 術 reads じゅつ, meaning "surgery / operation".
手術 (しゅじゅつ) = surgery or a medical operation. 手 (しゅ/て) = hand, and 術 (じゅつ) = technique/art/method. Together: a technical operation performed by hand — surgery. The sentence says 「手術 (しゅじゅつ) をしなくても治 (なお) りますから、大丈夫 (だいじょうぶ) ですよ」 — "It will heal without surgery, so you will be fine." Note: in this compound, 手 takes on-yomi しゅ (not kun-yomi て). 手 as しゅ appears in technical/formal compounds; as て it appears in everyday words.
✗ てじゅつ: uses kun-yomi て for 手. In the compound 手術, 手 takes on-yomi しゅ, not kun-yomi て. てじゅつ is not a real word.
✗ しゅしゅつ: correct しゅ for 手 but しゅつ for 術. 術 reads じゅつ (voiced j), not しゅつ (unvoiced sh). しゅつ belongs to 出 (しゅつ, exit/go out) or 術 read incorrectly.
✗ てしゅつ: wrong て for 手 (kun-yomi, should be on-yomi しゅ) and wrong しゅつ for 術 (should be voiced じゅつ). Both readings are incorrect.
例: 手術 (しゅじゅつ) は成功 (せいこう) し、患者 (かんじゃ) はすぐに回復 (かいふく) した。 — The surgery was successful and the patient recovered quickly.

question: ＿塩＿ は台所にありました。
explanation:
塩 is read しお and means "salt" — found in the kitchen.
塩 (しお) means "salt". The sentence 「塩は台所にありました」 means "The salt was in the kitchen." The kun-yomi しお is the everyday reading for this kanji when it appears alone as a noun. The on-yomi エン appears in compounds: 食塩 (しょくえん, table salt), 塩分 (えんぶん, salt content), 塩化 (えんか, chloride/chlorination). The 土 (earth) radical plus the 鹵 (salt marsh) component inside 塩 visually hint at a mineral substance drawn from the earth. The four distractors represent cooking and food items that could all be found in a kitchen, testing whether learners distinguish their kanji: あぶら (油, oil), まめ (豆, bean), しお (塩, salt), こめ (米, rice).
✗ あぶら is the reading of 油, meaning "oil". Oil and salt are both kitchen staples, but 塩 does not read あぶら. 油 contains the 氵 radical (water/liquid), consistent with a liquid fat.
✗ まめ is the reading of 豆, meaning "bean". Beans and salt are both food items, but 塩 does not read まめ. 豆 is written with a vessel/container shape representing a bean pod.
✗ こめ is the reading of 米, meaning "(uncooked) rice". Rice and salt are both kitchen staples, but 塩 does not read こめ.
例: パスタを茹 (ゆ) でるとき、お湯 (ゆ) にひとつまみの塩 (しお) を入 (い) れると味 (あじ) がよくなる。 — When boiling pasta, adding a pinch of salt to the water brings out the flavor.

question: 彼は犬に ＿命令＿ した。
explanation:
命令 is read めいれい — 命 reads めい and 令 reads れい, meaning "command / order".
命令 (めいれい) = a command or order. 命 (めい) = life/command, 令 (れい) = order/directive. 「彼 (かれ) は犬 (いぬ) に命令 (めいれい) した」 — "He gave commands to the dog." 命 reads めい (two morae, long い). Related: 命令形 (めいれいけい, imperative form).
✗ めれん: drops the long vowel of めい to め. 命 reads めい (two morae), not め.
✗ めいれん: correct めい for 命 but れん for 令. 令 reads れい, not れん. れん belongs to 連 or 練.
✗ めれい: drops long vowel of めい to め. 命 must read めい.
例: 監督 (かんとく) は選手 (せんしゅ) に交代 (こうたい) を命令 (めいれい) した。 — The coach ordered the player to substitute.

question: 手紙には ＿恋しい＿ 人を思う気持ちが書かれていた。
explanation:
恋しい is read こいしい because it means "yearning / longing for someone", fitting a letter expressing longing for a loved one.
恋しい (こいしい) = yearning for someone you love or miss deeply — a longing that aches. The sentence says 「手紙 (てがみ) には恋 (こい) しい人 (ひと) を思 (おも) う気持 (きも) ちが書 (か) かれていた」 — "The letter contained the feeling of longing for a beloved person." 恋しい expresses the bittersweet feeling of missing someone dear — stronger and more romantic than 懐かしい (nostalgia). The kanji 恋 contains 亦 on top and 心 (heart) at the bottom — a heart overflowing with longing.
✗ したしい: reading for 親しい (したしい, close/intimate). Being close to someone and longing for someone are different feelings. 親 and 恋 are different kanji.
✗ なつかしい: reading for 懐かしい (なつかしい, nostalgic/dear to one's heart). Nostalgia is a warm feeling for the past; 恋しい is active longing/yearning. Different intensities and different kanji.
✗ やさしい: reading for 優しい (やさしい, kind/gentle). Kindness and romantic longing are different feelings. 優 and 恋 are entirely different kanji.
例: 遠 (とお) くに住 (す) む家族 (かぞく) が恋 (こい) しくなることがある。 — Sometimes I long for my family who live far away.

question: ＿機械が＿ 故障した。
explanation:
機械 is read きかい because 機 takes on-yomi き and 械 takes on-yomi かい, forming the standard compound for "machine."
機械 (きかい) means "machine" or "machinery" — a mechanical device or apparatus. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 機 (き) = machine/opportunity/moment, and 械 (かい) = shackle/machine/instrument. Together they describe a mechanical device. The sentence says: "The machine 機械 (きかい) broke down." 機械が故障する = "the machine broke down" is a natural technical sentence. The key reading challenge: 機 reads き (unvoiced), not the voiced ぎ. The on-yomi of 機 is き (機会 きかい, opportunity; 機械 きかい, machine; 飛行機 ひこうき, airplane). The four options systematically test voiced (ぎ) vs unvoiced (き) for the first kanji 機: ぎかい vs きかい, and then add variants for the second syllable. 機 must read き (unvoiced) — ぎかい, きけい, and ぎけい are all wrong. The only correct reading is きかい.
✗ ぎかい voices 機 to ぎ. The on-yomi of 機 is き (unvoiced), not ぎ (voiced). ぎかい (議会) is a real word meaning "parliament," written with 議 (ぎ, deliberation) + 会 (かい, meeting). That is a completely different compound.
✗ きけい reads 機 correctly as き but changes 械 to けい. 械 reads かい in this compound. けい is the reading of 系 (system), 計 (calculate), or 刑 (penalty) — not 械.
✗ ぎけい voices 機 to ぎ and changes 械 to けい. Both halves are wrong. ぎけい does not correspond to 機械 at all.
例: 工場 (こうじょう) の機械 (きかい) が止 (と) まってしまい、生産 (せいさん) が一時 (いちじ) 中断 (ちゅうだん) された。 — The factory machine stopped, and production was temporarily halted.

question: 今月は ＿休日が＿ 多かった。
explanation:
休日 is read きゅうじつ (here きゅうじっ) and means "holiday / day off".
休日 (きゅうじつ) is an on-yomi compound: 休 (キュウ, rest) + 日 (ジツ, day). Together they mean "a rest day" or "a day off". The sentence says 「今月は休日が多かった」 — "This month had many holidays." Both kanji use their on-yomi: キュウ + ジツ. Note that before a voiced syllable, the ジツ can be heard as じっ depending on pitch pattern, which is reflected in the correct answer. The on-yomi ジツ for 日 appears when 日 is the second element in a time-related compound, as seen also in 本日 (ほんじつ, today, formal) and 祝日 (しゅくじつ, public holiday). This vowel alternation — にち vs ジツ — is a key N3 reading challenge.
✗ しゅくじつ (祝日, national holiday) is a real word but uses a different kanji — 祝 (しゅく, celebrate) instead of 休 (きゅう, rest). 休日 and 祝日 are related but not the same: 休日 is any day off, while 祝日 is specifically a public holiday.
✗ きゅうにち does not exist as a standard compound. The second kanji 日 in time compounds reads ジツ (not にち) when it follows キュウ in this pairing. にち appears in words like 毎日 (まいにち) where the pattern is different.
✗ しゅくにち is not a standard word either. It mismatches 祝 with a wrong reading of 日 (にち instead of じつ). This option tries to combine two wrong readings at once.
例: 今週 (こんしゅう) は休日 (きゅうじつ) が二日 (ふつか) あるので、旅行 (りょこう) の計画 (けいかく) を立 (た) てた。 — This week has two days off, so I made plans for a trip.

question: この ＿部分＿ をよく見てください。
explanation:
部分 is read ぶぶん — 部 reads ぶ and 分 reads ぶん, meaning "part / section".
部分 (ぶぶん) = a part or section of something. 部 (ぶ) = department/section, 分 (ぶん) = portion/part. The sentence says 「この部分 (ぶぶん) をよく見 (み) てください」 — "Please look carefully at this part." 部 reads ぶ (one mora, voiced) and 分 reads ぶん (one mora + ん, voiced). Both are voiced — the key trap is adding extra vowels: ぶふん or ぶうぶん.
✗ ぶふん: correct ぶ for 部 but unvoiced ふん for 分. 分 reads voiced ぶん, not unvoiced ふん. ふん is a different word (粉 = ふん, powder; or 噴 = ふん, to spout).
✗ ぶうぶん: elongates 部 to ぶう. 部 reads ぶ (one mora), not ぶう (two morae). ぶう is an onomatopoeia for a buzzing or puffing sound.
✗ ぶうふん: elongates 部 to ぶう (wrong) and uses unvoiced ふん for 分 (wrong). Both components are incorrect.
例: この部分 (ぶぶん) の意味 (いみ) がわからないので教 (おし) えてください。 — I don't understand the meaning of this part, so please explain it.

question: 池田さんは木村さんを ＿疑って＿ いるようだ。
explanation:
疑って is read うたがって and means "suspecting" — Ikeda seems to be suspecting Kimura.
疑う (うたがう) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to suspect" or "to doubt". The te-form 疑って (うたがって) is used in the sentence 「池田さんは木村さんを疑っているようだ」 — "It seems that Ikeda is suspecting Kimura." The ~ているようだ (seem to be doing) ending makes the statement an inference about an ongoing attitude. 疑 (うたが) has no on-yomi reading that appears in everyday verbs; the kun-yomi うたがう is the only verb form. The on-yomi ギ is reserved for noun compounds: 疑問 (ぎもん, doubt/question), 疑惑 (ぎわく, suspicion as a noun). Note that this question is essentially a duplicate of hash 03ab26b02d63cb87 in the same batch but with a different sentence context — the reading is the same.
✗ しかって is the te-form of 叱る (しかる), meaning "to scold". Scolding and suspecting are different interpersonal actions; 疑 does not read しか.
✗ こわがって is the te-form of 怖がる (こわがる), meaning "to be afraid of / to fear". Being afraid of someone and suspecting them are different emotional states; 疑 does not read こわが.
✗ きらって is the te-form of 嫌う (きらう), meaning "to dislike". Disliking Kimura and suspecting Kimura are different attitudes; 疑 does not read きら.
例: 自分 (じぶん) の記憶 (きおく) を疑 (うたが) い始 (はじ) めたとき、メモを見 (み) て確認 (かくにん) した。 — When I started to doubt my own memory, I checked my notes to confirm.

question: 中島さんは数学が ＿得意＿ らしい。
explanation:
得意 is read とくい because 得 takes on-yomi とく and 意 takes on-yomi い, forming the standard compound for "being good at something."
得意 (とくい) means "good at something" or "one's specialty" — the area where you excel and feel confident. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 得 (とく) = to gain/to be able to, and 意 (い) = intention/feeling/mind. Together they convey the idea of something one has naturally "gotten a feel for." The sentence says: "Nakajima-san seems to be good at mathematics." The reading pattern here is exactly the same as the earlier 得意 entry (hash 580e0f849224cde4), which used dance as the subject. This entry uses math (数学 すうがく) instead. Both test the same reading: とくい. The trap is consistently the same: adding a long vowel (とうい) or voicing (どくい / どうい). 得 reads とく (unvoiced, short vowel), and 意 reads い (single mora). The compound reads とく + い = とくい, nothing more.
✗ とうい inserts a long vowel after と, producing とう instead of とく. 得 reads とく (short, two morae: と + く), not the elongated とう. とうい would correspond to 問い (とうい) in some dialects, but 得意 reads とくい.
✗ どくい voices 得 to どく. The on-yomi of 得 is とく (unvoiced). Voicing it produces どく, which is the reading of 毒 (どく, poison) — a completely different kanji.
✗ どうい voices 得 and also adds a long vowel, producing どう. The actual reading is とく — unvoiced and without a long vowel. どうい (同意) is a real word meaning "agreement," written with 同意, not 得意.
例: 数学 (すうがく) は得意 (とくい) だが、語学 (ごがく) は苦手 (にがて) だ。 — I am good at math but not good at languages.

question: 息子は来年 ＿卒業＿ します。
explanation:
卒業 is read そつぎょう — on-yomi compound meaning "graduation".
卒業 (そつぎょう): 卒 (そつ) = to complete, 業 (ぎょう) = studies. The sentence says 「息子 (むすこ) は来年 (らいねん) 卒業 (そつぎょう) します」 — "My son will graduate next year."
✗ さつきょう: さつ not a reading for 卒. 卒 reads そつ.
✗ そつきょう: correct そつ for 卒 but きょう for 業 is wrong. 業 reads voiced ぎょう.
✗ さつぎょう: wrong さつ for 卒.
例: 大学 (だいがく) を卒業 (そつぎょう) してすぐ就職 (しゅうしょく) した。 — She found a job right after graduating.

question: 留学について先生に ＿相談＿ した。
explanation:
相談 is read そうだん and means "consultation / talking something over".
相談 (そうだん) is an on-yomi compound: 相 (ソウ, mutual/together) + 談 (ダン, talk/discussion). Together the word means "a mutual discussion" — consulting or talking something over with another person. The sentence 「留学について先生に相談した」 means "I consulted my teacher about studying abroad." The reading challenge is ソウダン: 相 reads ソウ (not しょう or そ), and 談 reads ダン (voiced, not タン). Distractors swap ソウ with しょう (a common mistake) or the voiced ダン with unvoiced タン. 相 appears in: 相互 (そうご, mutual), 首相 (しゅしょう, prime minister — using the on-yomi ショウ here). 談 appears in: 会談 (かいだん, conference), 冗談 (じょうだん, joke).
✗ しょうたん misreads 相 as しょう instead of そう. 相 reads ソウ (long o, voiced consonant start), not しょう. しょう belongs to 商 (trade) or 章 (chapter), not 相.
✗ しょうだん applies the wrong reading しょう for 相 while getting ダン right. 相 does not read しょう in this compound; it reads ソウ.
✗ そうたん reads 相 correctly as そう but misreads 談 as タン (unvoiced) instead of the correct ダン (voiced). 談 always uses the voiced ダン on-yomi.
例: 進路 (しんろ) について親 (おや) に相談 (そうだん) してから、最終的 (さいしゅうてき) な決断 (けつだん) をした。 — I consulted my parents about my future path before making the final decision.

question: ＿確か＿ にかばんにしまいました。
explanation:
確か is read たしか, meaning "certainly / I'm sure that" — the speaker says they definitely put it in the bag.
確か (たしか) is an adverb meaning "certainly," "I'm sure that," or "if I'm not mistaken." It expresses confidence in a recollection or belief. The sentence says: "I'm certain 確か (たしか) I put it in the bag." かばんにしまいました = "I stored it in the bag." The speaker is asserting this with confidence. The kanji 確 uses the kun-yomi たし in this adverb form: 確か (たしか, certainly), 確かめる (たしかめる, to confirm/check). Its on-yomi かく appears in compounds like 確認 (かくにん, confirmation), 確実 (かくじつ, certain), and 正確 (せいかく, accurate). The critical reading trick: たしか starts with た, not し. Learners sometimes confuse 確か (たしか) with 静か (しずか, quiet) — both end in か and describe a state, but their kanji and readings are completely different. The distractor しずか is precisely this confusion.
✗ しずか is the reading of 静か (しずか), meaning "quiet" or "calm." 静 and 確 are completely different kanji. Saying "I quietly put it in the bag" does not match the meaning of the sentence, which expresses certainty.
✗ たじか is a slightly altered version of たしか with the syllable order shifted (し → じ, voiced). 確 reads たし (unvoiced し), not たじ (voiced じ). たじか is not a real word.
✗ しすか does not correspond to any real word at all. It is neither a known reading of 確 nor a recognized Japanese word. This option tests basic sound awareness.
例: 確 (たし) かに昨日 (きのう) その書類 (しょるい) を送 (おく) りました。 — I'm certain I sent that document yesterday.

question: 子どもたちが ＿遊ぶ＿ 声が聞こえます。
explanation:
遊ぶ is read あそぶ and means "to play" — the sounds of children playing.
遊ぶ (あそぶ) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to play" or "to have fun". The dictionary form 遊ぶ (あそぶ) in the sentence 「子どもたちが遊ぶ声が聞こえます」 means "The voices of the children playing can be heard." Here 遊ぶ modifies 声 (こえ, voice/sound) as a relative clause. The kanji 遊 contains the 辶 (movement) radical, and the component on the right suggests a flag or banner waving — movement without fixed purpose, consistent with the idea of playing freely. The on-yomi ユウ appears in: 遊覧 (ゆうらん, excursion), 遊園地 (ゆうえんち, amusement park). When 遊 stands as a verb, the reading is always あそ.
✗ よぶ is the reading of 呼ぶ, meaning "to call / to invite". Calling someone and playing are different actions; 遊 does not read よ.
✗ まなぶ is the reading of 学ぶ, meaning "to learn / to study". Learning and playing are often presented as contrasts; 遊 does not read まな.
✗ さけぶ is the reading of 叫ぶ, meaning "to shout / to scream". Shouting and playing are related in the context of children's voices, but they are different verbs; 遊 does not read さけ.
例: 放課後 (ほうかご) 、子 (こ) どもたちは公園 (こうえん) で夕方 (ゆうがた) まで遊 (あそ) んでいた。 — After school, the children played in the park until evening.

question: 店の人はみんな同じ ＿制服＿ を着ていた。
explanation:
制服 is read せいふく and means "uniform" — all shop staff wearing the same uniform.
制服 (せいふく) is an on-yomi compound: 制 (セイ, regulate/control) + 服 (フク, clothing). Together the word means "regulated clothing" — a uniform. The sentence 「店の人はみんな同じ制服を着ていた」 means "Everyone in the store was wearing the same uniform." The reading challenge is せいふく: 制 reads セイ (not ようor ようふ), and 服 reads フク (short, not フウ). The distractors introduce the wrong first-kanji reading ようふ- (suggesting 洋服, ようふく, Western-style clothing) or a nonstandard ending. 洋服 (ようふく) is a real word meaning "Western clothes" but its first kanji 洋 reads ヨウ, not セイ.
✗ ようふく (洋服) means "Western-style clothing". 洋 (ヨウ) means ocean/Western, not control/regulate. 洋服 and 制服 are different words: 洋服 is any Western clothing, while 制服 is a regulated uniform.
✗ せいふう misreads 服 as フウ instead of フク. The on-yomi of 服 is フク (short, one mora after フ), not the long フウ. せいふう is not a standard reading of 制服.
✗ ようふう combines the wrong first kanji reading ヨウ (洋) with the wrong second reading フウ (instead of フク). Both elements are incorrect.
例: この学校 (がっこう) では、毎日 (まいにち) 制服 (せいふく) を着 (き) て登校 (とうこう) しなければならない。 — At this school, students must wear their uniform to school every day.

question: 鈴木さんが ＿換えて＿ くれました。
explanation:
換えて is read かえて because 換える means "to exchange / to replace", fitting the context of Suzuki-san making a replacement.
換える (かえる) = to exchange, to replace, to swap. Its て-form is 換 (か) えて. The sentence says 「鈴木 (すずき) さんが換 (か) えてくれました」 — "Suzuki-san replaced/exchanged it for me." 換える is the transitive verb for swapping one thing for another (e.g., replacing a battery, exchanging currency). The kanji 換 contains 扌 (hand) on the left and 奐 on the right — the hand making an exchange. Note: Japanese has several homophones of かえる: 換える (exchange), 変える (かえる, to change), 替える (かえる, to substitute), 帰る (かえる, to return home).
✗ くわえて: て-form of 加える (くわえる, to add/include). Adding something is different from exchanging it. 加 and 換 are different kanji.
✗ つかまえて: て-form of 捕まえる (つかまえる, to catch/grab). Catching something is completely different from exchanging it.
✗ つたえて: て-form of 伝える (つたえる, to convey/transmit). Conveying information is different from exchanging an object.
例: 電池 (でんち) が切 (き) れたので、新 (あたら) しいものに換 (か) えた。 — The battery ran out, so I replaced it with a new one.

question: ＿血圧＿ が前よりも高かったようです。
explanation:
血圧 is read けつあつ — 血 reads けつ (blood) and 圧 reads あつ (pressure), meaning "blood pressure".
血圧 (けつあつ) = blood pressure. The sentence says 「血圧 (けつあつ) が前 (まえ) よりも高 (たか) かったようです」 — "It seems blood pressure was higher than before." This is the second occurrence of 血圧 in this batch (same word, different sentence). 血 reads on-yomi けつ (not kun-yomi ち) in medical compounds. 圧 reads あつ.
✗ ちど: kun-yomi ち for 血 (wrong in this medical compound) and ど for 圧 (completely wrong — 圧 reads あつ, not ど). Double error.
✗ けっど: correct けっ for 血 in a geminate context (血液 = けつえき → けっ before e) but ど for 圧 is completely wrong. 圧 reads あつ, not ど.
✗ ちあつ: kun-yomi ち for 血 (instead of on-yomi けつ). In the medical compound 血圧, 血 takes on-yomi けつ. ちあつ is not the standard medical reading.
例: 毎朝 (まいあさ) 血圧 (けつあつ) を測 (はか) る習慣 (しゅうかん) がある。 — I have a habit of measuring my blood pressure every morning.

question: ＿改札＿ の前で会いましょう。
explanation:
改札 is read かいさつ because 改 takes on-yomi かい and 札 takes on-yomi さつ, forming the compound for "ticket gate."
改札 (かいさつ) means "ticket gate" or "ticket barrier" — the inspection point at a train station where passengers pass their tickets or IC cards. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 改 (かい) = to reform/to check/to change, and 札 (さつ) = card/bill/label. Together 改札 describes the place where tickets (札) are checked (改) — a ticket examination checkpoint. The sentence says: "Let's meet in front of the ticket gate 改札 (かいさつ)." 改札口 (かいさつぐち, ticket gate opening) is also common. The reading challenge involves distinguishing four options with similar sound shapes. The correct one is fully unvoiced: かい (か + い) + さつ (さ + つ). 改 reads かい (unvoiced), not けい (which would be 計 or 経). 札 reads さつ (unvoiced), not せつ (which would be 説 or 節). The compound is extremely common in daily life, and knowing its exact reading is essential for navigating Japanese train stations.
✗ けいせつ assigns けい to 改 and せつ to 札. 改 reads かい, not けい. けい is the on-yomi of 計 (calculate), 系 (system), or 経 (pass through). Neither applies here.
✗ けいさつ assigns けい to 改 but reads 札 correctly as さつ. 改 does not read けい. けいさつ is actually 警察 (けいさつ, police) — a real word, but using entirely different kanji.
✗ かいせっ reads 改 correctly as かい but changes 札 to a non-standard contracted form せっ. 札 reads さつ (two morae: さ + つ) — there is no reason to contract it to a sokuon せっ. This option also mixes up the vowel (sa vs se).
例: Suicaカードを使 (つか) えば、改札 (かいさつ) をスムーズに通 (とお) ることができる。 — Using a Suica card, you can pass through the ticket gate smoothly.

question: この前よりも ＿遅く＿ なってしまいました。
explanation:
遅く is read おそく because 遅い means "slow / late", fitting something that has become later than before.
遅い (おそい) = slow or late. Its adverbial form 遅 (おそ) く. The sentence says 「この前 (まえ) よりも遅 (おそ) くなってしまいました」 — "It has become later than before." 遅い describes both being slow in speed and being late in time. 遅く (おそく) + なる = to become late/slower. The kanji 遅 contains 辶 (movement) on the left and 犀 (rhinoceros) on the right — the slow rhino.
✗ きたなく: く-form of 汚い (きたない, dirty). Getting dirtier is unrelated to getting later. 汚 and 遅 are different kanji.
✗ みじかく: く-form of 短い (みじかい, short). Getting shorter is unrelated to getting later. 短 and 遅 are different kanji.
✗ とおく: く-form of 遠い (とおい, far/distant). Getting farther away is different from getting later. 遠 and 遅 look similar (both have 辶) but are different kanji with different meanings.
例: 電車 (でんしゃ) が遅 (おそ) くなったせいで、会議 (かいぎ) に間 (ま) に合 (あ) わなかった。 — Because the train was late, I didn't make it to the meeting on time.

question: このペンを使って ＿線＿ を書いてください。
explanation:
線 is read せん and means "a line".
線 (せん) means "a line" — a drawn or imaginary straight line. The sentence 「このペンを使って線を書いてください」 means "Please draw a line using this pen." The on-yomi セン is the only standard reading for 線 when it appears as a standalone noun. This kanji appears widely: 電車の線 (railway line), 直線 (ちょくせん, straight line), 点線 (てんせん, dotted line), 下線 (かせん, underline). The 糸 (thread) radical at the left visually suggests a continuous strand — something drawn out into a line. The distractors test whether learners distinguish 線 (line) from other strokes and drawings: ず (map/figure), え (picture), もじ (character/letter).
✗ ず is the reading of 図, meaning "a diagram" or "a map". A line and a diagram are different things — a diagram contains lines but is more complex. 線 does not read ず.
✗ え is the reading of 絵, meaning "a picture / painting". A line is a single stroke; a picture is a complete visual composition. 線 does not read え.
✗ もじ is the reading of 文字, meaning "a character / a letter". Characters are written symbols, not bare lines. 線 does not read もじ.
例: 地図 (ちず) の上 (うえ) に赤 (あか) い線 (せん) を引 (ひ) いて、目的地 (もくてきち) までのルートを示 (しめ) した。 — I drew a red line on the map to indicate the route to the destination.

question: 夏休みは ＿調査＿ に行くつもりです。
explanation:
調査 is read ちょうさ because 調 takes on-yomi ちょう and 査 takes on-yomi さ, forming the standard word for "investigation" or "survey."
調査 (ちょうさ) means "investigation," "survey," or "research" — systematically examining something to gather information. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 調 (ちょう) = to examine/to adjust/melody, and 査 (さ) = to investigate/to inspect. Together they describe a thorough examination. The sentence says: "I plan to go on a survey 調査 (ちょうさ) during summer vacation." 調査に行く is natural for fieldwork or research trips. The reading challenge involves the final syllable of 調 (ちょう, long vowel) and the distinction between さ and さつ for 査. ちょうさ has only two syllables in the second kanji (さ, one mora), not three (さつ, two morae). Compare: 検察 (けんさつ) uses 察 (さつ), while 調査 (ちょうさ) uses 査 (さ). The distractors ちょうさつ and かんさつ test this exactly. 観察 (かんさつ, observation) is a related concept but uses 観 (かん, to observe) and 察 (さつ, to perceive) — different kanji for different methods of inquiry.
✗ ちょうさつ extends さ to さつ, implying 察 (さつ, to perceive/inspect) instead of 査 (さ, to examine). 調察 is not a standard compound. 察 is used in 観察 (かんさつ, observation) and 捜査 (そうさ, criminal investigation). 査 and 察 are different kanji with different readings.
✗ かんさ assigns the reading かん to 調. 調 reads ちょう (on-yomi) in this compound, not かん. かん is the on-yomi of 関 (involve), 間 (interval), or 官 (government official) — not 調.
✗ かんさつ is the reading of 観察 (かんさつ), meaning "observation." It uses the kanji 観 (かん, to observe carefully) + 察 (さつ, to perceive). 観察 is systematic watching; 調査 is systematic investigating/surveying. Different methods, different kanji.
例: 研究者 (けんきゅうしゃ) たちが現地 (げんち) に行 (い) って詳 (くわ) しく調査 (ちょうさ) した。 — The researchers went to the site and conducted a detailed investigation.

question: 今朝、 ＿郵便＿ が届きました。
explanation:
郵便 is read ゆうびん — 郵 reads ゆう and 便 reads びん, meaning "postal mail".
郵便 (ゆうびん) = postal mail — the postal system or a piece of mail. 郵 (ゆう) = postal, 便 (びん) = convenience/service/flight/mail. The sentence says 「今朝 (けさ) 、郵便 (ゆうびん) が届 (とど) きました」 — "The mail arrived this morning." 郵 reads ゆう (long vowel), not ゆ. 便 reads びん (voiced, two morae) in this compound, not べん or びん-shortened. Related: 郵便局 (ゆうびんきょく, post office), 郵便番号 (ゆうびんばんごう, postal code).
✗ ゆべん: shortens 郵 to ゆ (wrong — 郵 reads ゆう) and shortens 便 to べん (unvoiced — 便 reads voiced びん in this compound).
✗ ゆびん: shortens 郵 to ゆ, dropping the long vowel. 郵 reads ゆう (two morae), not ゆ alone.
✗ ゆうべん: correct ゆう for 郵 but unvoiced べん for 便. 便 reads voiced びん (two morae, voiced b) in 郵便, not unvoiced べん.
例: 郵便 (ゆうびん) でお送 (おく) りしますので、数日 (すうじつ) お待 (ま) ちください。 — I will send it by mail, so please wait a few days.

question: ＿腰＿ に薬を塗ぬってもらった。
explanation:
腰 is read こし because it means "lower back / hips", fitting the context of having medicine applied to the lower back.
腰 (こし) = lower back or hips — the region of the body between the ribs and the buttocks. The sentence says 「腰 (こし) に薬 (くすり) を塗 (ぬ) ってもらった」 — "I had medicine applied to my lower back." 腰が痛い (こしがいたい, lower back pain) is one of the most common complaints in Japan. The kanji 腰 contains 月 (flesh/body radical) on the left and 要 (essential) on the right — the lower back being essential to body movement.
✗ むね: reading for 胸 (むね, chest/breast). The chest is the front upper torso, not the lower back. 胸 and 腰 are different body parts with different kanji.
✗ かた: reading for 肩 (かた, shoulder). The shoulder is the upper body joint, not the lower back. 肩 and 腰 are different body parts.
✗ くび: reading for 首 (くび, neck). The neck connects the head to the torso, not at the lower back region. 首 and 腰 are different body parts.
例: 長時間 (ちょうじかん) 座 (すわ) っていると腰 (こし) が痛 (いた) くなる。 — Sitting for a long time makes your lower back hurt.

question: 歩いているうちに ＿方角＿ がわからなくなった。
explanation:
方角 is read ほうがく because 方 takes on-yomi ほう and 角 takes on-yomi かく, voiced to がく after the compound boundary.
方角 (ほうがく) means "direction" — as in compass directions (north, south, east, west) or the general sense of "which way." The compound uses the on-yomi of both kanji: 方 (ほう) means "direction" or "way," and 角 (かく/かど) means "angle" or "corner." In this compound, 角 takes its on-yomi かく, which voices to がく after 方: ほう + かく → ほうがく. The sentence says: "While walking, I lost track of the direction 方角 (ほうがく)." This is a natural use for 方角 — getting lost or disoriented. The word 方向 (ほうこう), meaning "direction" in a more general or movement-oriented sense, is a near-synonym but uses different kanji: 向 (こう/む) instead of 角. The key difference: 方角 (ほうがく) refers to compass-point direction, while 方向 (ほうこう) refers to the direction something is facing or moving. The on-yomi of 角 (かく → voiced がく) vs. the on-yomi of 向 (こう) is the core reading distinction here.
✗ ほうこう is the reading of 方向 (ほうこう), meaning "direction" in the sense of facing or movement (例: 進む方向 すすむほうこう, the direction one is moving). It is a real word but uses 向 (こう), not 角 (がく). The question tests 方角, which specifically uses 角.
✗ ほうかく uses 角 correctly but leaves it unvoiced as かく rather than the voiced がく. After ほう, the following consonant voices: かく → がく. ほうかく is not a standard reading of 方角.
✗ ほうごう suggests 合 (ごう, to combine/fit), producing 方合 — not a standard word. 合 (ごう) appears in 合計 (ごうけい, total) but has no connection to direction or 角 (angle/corner).
例: 初めて来 (き) た町 (まち) では方角 (ほうがく) がわからなくなりやすい。 — In a town you are visiting for the first time, it is easy to lose your sense of direction.

question: これを ＿包んで＿ もらえませんか。
explanation:
包んで is read つつんで and means "wrap (it)" — a request to have something wrapped.
包む (つつむ) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to wrap" or "to envelop". The te-form 包んで (つつんで) in the sentence 「これを包んでもらえませんか」 means "Could you please wrap this?" — a polite request at a shop. The kanji 包 visually depicts something folded inside wrapping — the 勹 (wrapping) radical enclosing 己. Its on-yomi ホウ appears in: 包装 (ほうそう, packaging/wrapping), 包括 (ほうかつ, comprehensive inclusion). The distractors test the distinction between wrapping (つつむ), tying (むすぶ), knitting (あむ), and carrying (はこぶ) — all actions involving enclosing or holding something.
✗ むすんで is the te-form of 結ぶ (むすぶ), meaning "to tie". Tying creates a knot with cord; wrapping covers something in paper or cloth. 包 does not read むすん.
✗ あんで is the te-form of 編む (あむ), meaning "to knit" or "to braid". Knitting and wrapping are completely different; 包 does not read あん.
✗ はこんで is the te-form of 運ぶ (はこぶ), meaning "to carry / to transport". Carrying and wrapping are different — carrying involves moving, while wrapping involves enclosing. 包 does not read はこん.
例: 贈 (おく) り物 (もの) として包 (つつ) んでもらったので、中身 (なかみ) がわからなくてわくわくした。 — Since it was wrapped as a gift, I was excited not knowing what was inside.

question: ＿昼食＿ の後は工場見学です。
explanation:
昼食 is read ちゅうしょく and means "lunch".
昼食 (ちゅうしょく) is an on-yomi compound: 昼 (チュウ, daytime/noon) + 食 (ショク, meal/eat). Together the word means "the midday meal" — a formal register word for lunch. The sentence 「昼食の後は工場見学です」 means "After lunch, there is a factory tour." The key reading distinctions: 昼 reads チュウ (not ちょう or しょう) in compounds; 食 reads ショク (not しゅう or しょ). Distractors test three common errors: confusing チュウ with ちょう or しゅう, and ショク with various similar sounds. In everyday speech, お昼 (おひる) is more casual, while 昼食 is used in formal contexts like schedules or menus.
✗ しょうしょく could suggest 少食 (eating little) or a non-standard reading. Neither element matches 昼食 — 昼 reads チュウ, not しょう.
✗ ちょうしょく (朝食) means "breakfast" — the morning meal. 朝 (ちょう, morning) + 食 (ショク). This is a real word but for the wrong meal. 昼 (daytime) reads チュウ, not ちょう.
✗ しゅうしょく (就職) means "finding employment". 就 (シュウ, take up a position) + 職 (ショク, occupation). Completely different domain — employment vs. eating. Also, 昼 does not read しゅう.
例: 昼食 (ちゅうしょく) の時間 (じかん) は30分 (さんじゅっぷん) しかないので、近 (ちか) くの食堂 (しょくどう) に行 (い) く。 — I have only 30 minutes for lunch, so I go to the nearby cafeteria.

question: 1０時に ＿予約＿ をお願いします。
explanation:
予約 is read よやく — 予 reads よ and 約 reads やく, meaning "reservation / appointment".
予約 (よやく) = reservation or appointment — a promise made in advance. 予 (よ) = in advance, 約 (やく) = promise/approximately. 「1０時に予約 (よやく) をお願 (ねが) いします」 — "Please make a reservation for 10 o'clock." 予 reads よ (one mora), not よう.
✗ ようやく is a real adverb meaning "finally / at last" but it is written 漸く — not how 予約 reads. 予 reads よ (one mora), not よう (two morae).
✗ よよく: wrong よく for 約. 約 reads やく (vowel あ), not よく.
✗ ようよく: elongated よう for 予 (wrong) and wrong よく for 約.
例: レストランの予約 (よやく) は三日前 (みっかまえ) にした。 — I made the restaurant reservation three days in advance.

question: ＿若かった＿
explanation:
若かった is read わかかった and means "was young".
若い (わかい) is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "young". The past form 若かった (わかかった) means "was young". This is a standalone adjective form with no sentence context in the question — the task is purely to identify the reading of 若かった. The kun-yomi わか is the only reading for 若 as an adjective. The on-yomi ジャク appears in compounds: 若干 (じゃっかん, a few/somewhat), 老若 (ろうにゃく, old and young). When 若 appears as an い-adjective, the reading is always わかい / わかかった. The past inflection わかかった adds -かった (past marker) to the stem わか.
✗ わるかった is the past form of 悪い (わるい, bad/poor). "Was bad" and "was young" are completely different meanings; 若 does not read わる.
✗ さむかった is the past form of 寒い (さむい, cold/chilly weather). "Was cold" and "was young" are different; 若 does not read さむ.
✗ こわかった is the past form of 怖い (こわい, scary/frightening). "Was scary" and "was young" are different; 若 does not read こわ.
例: 祖父 (そふ) は若 (わか) かった頃 (ころ) の話 (はなし) をよく聞 (き) かせてくれた。 — My grandfather often told me stories about when he was young.

question: ＿上品＿ な人ですね。
explanation:
上品 is read じょうひん — 上 reads じょう and 品 reads ひん, meaning "elegant / refined".
上品 (じょうひん) = elegant, refined, of high quality or taste — as a な-adjective. 上 (じょう) = upper/superior, 品 (ひん) = item/quality. Together: of superior quality — refined and tasteful. The sentence says 「上品 (じょうひん) な人 (ひと) ですね」 — "What a refined person." 上 reads じょう (long vowel, two morae), not じょ alone. 品 reads ひん (unvoiced h), not びん.
✗ じょうびん: voices 品 to びん. 品 reads ひん (unvoiced h), not びん (voiced b). びん belongs to 瓶 (びん, bottle) or 便 (びん, mail/flight service).
✗ じょひん: shortens 上 to じょ, dropping the long vowel. 上 reads じょう (two morae), not じょ alone.
✗ じょびん: shortens 上 to じょ (wrong) and voices 品 to びん (wrong). Both readings are incorrect.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) は言葉 (ことば) づかいがとても上品 (じょうひん) だ。 — Her use of language is very refined.

question: 山田さんに ＿助けて＿ もらった
explanation:
助けて is read たすけて, meaning "helped" — Yamada-san helped the speaker.
助ける (たすける) means "to help," "to rescue," or "to save someone" — particularly helping someone in a difficult situation. The te-form 助けて (たすけて) combined with もらった expresses that Yamada-san performed this helpful action for the speaker. The sentence says: "Yamada-san helped 助けて (たすけて) me." 助けてもらう = "to have someone help you" is a standard benefactive construction. The kanji 助 uses the kun-yomi たす in verb form. Its on-yomi じょ appears in compounds like 助言 (じょげん, advice), 助手 (じょしゅ, assistant), and 援助 (えんじょ, support/aid). The distractors are all te-form verbs with similar sound structure or meaning clusters: 届けて (とどけて, to deliver), 受けて (うけて, to receive), and 片づけて (かたづけて, to tidy up). None of these means "to help."
✗ とどけて is the te-form of 届ける (とどける), meaning "to deliver" or "to convey." Delivering something and helping someone are different actions. 助 does not read とどけ.
✗ うけて is the te-form of 受ける (うける), meaning "to receive" or "to undergo." Receiving something is a passive action; helping is an active one. 助 does not read うけ.
✗ かたづけて is the te-form of 片づける (かたづける), meaning "to tidy up" or "to clean up." Tidying and helping someone in difficulty are different actions. 助 does not read かたづけ.
例: 迷子 (まいご) になった子供 (こども) を助 (たす) けて、家族 (かぞく) のところまで連 (つ) れて行 (い) った。 — I helped the lost child and brought them to their family.

question: ＿未来＿ を考えてみる
explanation:
未来 is read みらい and means "the future".
未来 (みらい) is an on-yomi compound: 未 (ミ, not yet) + 来 (ライ, come/arrive). Together the word means "that which has not yet come" — the future. The sentence 「未来を考えてみる」 means "I try to think about the future." The reading challenge is ミライ: 未 reads ミ (one mora), and 来 reads ライ (long vowel, two morae). Distractor しょうらい (将来) is a real word also meaning "the future" but uses different kanji — 将 (ショウ, general/leading) + 来 (ライ). Both 未来 and 将来 mean "the future" but 未来 often has a more philosophical or distant-future nuance, while 将来 is frequently used for one's personal career future.
✗ しょらい drops the long vowel from 将 (ショウ → しょ). Even setting aside which compound is intended, shortening ショウ to しょ produces a non-standard reading.
✗ しょうらい (将来) is a real word meaning "the future / one's future prospects". But 未来 uses 未 (not yet), not 将 (leading/general). The kanji are entirely different.
✗ みいらい adds an extra い between み and らい, creating a three-syllable first element. 未 reads ミ (one mora), not ミイ (two morae). The extra length is wrong.
例: 子 (こ) どもたちのために、より良 (よ) い未来 (みらい) を作 (つく) る責任 (せきにん) がある。 — We have a responsibility to build a better future for our children.

question: この電車は ＿各駅＿ に止まります
explanation:
各駅 is read かくえき — 各 reads かく (each) and 駅 reads えき (station), meaning "each/every station".
各駅 (かくえき) = each/every station. 各 (かく) = each/every, 駅 (えき) = train station. 「この電車 (でんしゃ) は各駅 (かくえき) に止 (と) まります」 — "This train stops at every station." Trains stopping at all stations are called 各駅停車 (かくえきていしゃ, local train). 各 reads かく (unvoiced), not がく or きゃく.
✗ がくえき: voices 各 to がく. 各 reads かく (unvoiced k). がく belongs to 学 (study) or 楽 (music).
✗ きゃくえき: reads 各 as きゃく. きゃく is the reading for 客 (guest/customer), a different kanji.
✗ ぎゃくえき: ぎゃく is the reading for 逆 (reverse/opposite). Completely unrelated to 各.
例: 急 (いそ) いでいたので各駅停車 (かくえきていしゃ) ではなく急行 (きゅうこう) に乗 (の) った。 — Since I was in a hurry, I took the express instead of the local train.

question: 誰が ＿勝った＿ んですか？
explanation:
勝った is read かった, meaning "won" — the question asks who won a competition.
勝つ (かつ) means "to win" or "to defeat." Its past tense 勝った (かった) means "won." The sentence says: "Who won 勝った (かった)?" This is a simple post-match question. The kanji 勝 uses the kun-yomi か in verb form. Its on-yomi しょう appears in compounds like 勝利 (しょうり, victory), 優勝 (ゆうしょう, championship), and 勝敗 (しょうはい, victory or defeat). The four distractors are all past-tense て-form verbs ending in った, testing whether students recognize the kanji 勝 (to win) from its reading かった. 飾る (かざる, to decorate), 折る (おる, to break/fold), and 残る (のこる, to remain) all have the same -った ending pattern but completely different meanings. The critical kanji recognition: 勝 = win, not decorate, not fold, not remain.
✗ かざった is the past tense of 飾る (かざる), meaning "to decorate." Decorating and winning are unrelated actions. 勝 does not read かざった.
✗ おった is the past tense of 折る (おる), meaning "to break" or "to fold." Breaking or folding and winning have nothing in common. 勝 does not read おった.
✗ のこった is the past tense of 残る (のこる), meaning "to remain" or "to be left over." Remaining and winning are different outcomes. 勝 does not read のこった.
例: 決勝戦 (けっしょうせん) でライバルチームに勝 (か) って、優勝 (ゆうしょう) した。 — We beat our rival team in the final and won the championship.

question: 彼に初めて会ったときの ＿印象＿ はどうでしたか？
explanation:
印象 is read いんしょう because 印 takes on-yomi いん and 象 takes on-yomi しょう, forming the compound meaning "impression."
印象 (いんしょう) means "impression" — the feeling or image you form of a person or thing upon meeting them. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 印 (いん) = seal/mark/imprint, and 象 (しょう) = form/image/phenomenon. Together they convey the image that has been "stamped" in your mind upon first contact — hence an impression. The sentence says: "What was your impression 印象 (いんしょう) when you first met him?" 初めて会ったときの印象 is a typical conversational or interview question. 印 also appears in 印鑑 (いんかん, personal seal) and 印刷 (いんさつ, printing). 象 also appears in 現象 (げんしょう, phenomenon), 象徴 (しょうちょう, symbol), and 対象 (たいしょう, target/subject). The distractors methodically test the voiced/unvoiced pair (いん vs にん) for 印, and the long/short vowel (しょう vs そう) for 象. 印 reads いん (unvoiced い), not the voiced にん. 象 reads しょう (with long vowel), not the short そう.
✗ いんそう changes the reading of 象 from しょう to そう. The on-yomi of 象 is しょう (with long vowel). そう is the reading of 層 (layer) or 走 (run), not 象. Dropping the ょ and the long vowel changes the meaning entirely.
✗ にんしょう voices 印 to にん. The on-yomi of 印 is いん (unvoiced), not にん (voiced). にん is the reading of 人 (person) or 認 (recognize) — for example 認証 (にんしょう, authentication). That compound uses 認 and 証, not 印 and 象.
✗ にんそう voices 印 to にん and shortens 象 to そう. Both changes are wrong. にんそう (人相) is a real word meaning "facial features/physiognomy," written with 人 (にん) + 相 (そう). It is a completely different compound from 印象.
例: 面接 (めんせつ) では第一印象 (だいいちいんしょう) がとても大切 (たいせつ) だと言 (い) われている。 — It is said that first impressions are very important in job interviews.

question: まず、この問題を ＿調査＿ します。
explanation:
調査 is read ちょうさ — 調 reads ちょう and 査 reads さ, meaning "investigation / survey".
調査 (ちょうさ) = investigation, survey. 調 (ちょう) = to examine, 査 (さ) = to inspect. 「まず、この問題 (もんだい) を調査 (ちょうさ) します」 — "First, we will investigate this problem."
✗ ちょうさつ: adds つ after さ. 査 reads さ (one mora), not さつ.
✗ ちょさ: shortens ちょう to ちょ. 調 reads ちょう (long vowel).
✗ ちょさつ: wrong shortened ちょ for 調 and wrong さつ for 査.
例: アンケートで利用者 (りようしゃ) の意見 (いけん) を調査 (ちょうさ) した。 — We surveyed user opinions through a questionnaire.

question: どんな ＿種類＿ がありますか。
explanation:
種類 is read しゅるい because 種 takes on-yomi しゅ and 類 takes on-yomi るい, forming the standard word for "type" or "kind."
種類 (しゅるい) means "type," "kind," or "variety" — a category or classification of things. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 種 (しゅ) = seed/type/variety, and 類 (るい) = category/similar kind. Together they indicate different categories or varieties of something. The sentence says: "What kinds 種類 (しゅるい) do you have?" This is a common question in shops. The reading challenge is that 種 must read しゅ (not じゅ — unvoiced), and 類 must read るい (not れい). The four options test all combinations of voiced/unvoiced (し vs じ) and the vowel sequence (る + い vs れ + い). Correct: しゅ + るい = しゅるい. 種 also appears in 種類 (しゅるい), 種目 (しゅもく, event category), and 品種 (ひんしゅ, variety/breed). 類 also appears in 分類 (ぶんるい, classification), 類義語 (るいぎご, synonym), and 人類 (じんるい, humanity).
✗ しゅれい changes るい to れい — a different vowel sequence. 類 reads るい, not れい. れい is the reading of 例 (example), 礼 (etiquette), or 令 (order) — completely different characters.
✗ じゅれい voices 種 to じゅ and changes 類 to れい. The on-yomi of 種 is しゅ (unvoiced). じゅ would correspond to 受 (じゅ, to receive) or 寿 (じゅ, longevity). Neither reading matches 種.
✗ じゅるい voices 種 to じゅ while reading 類 correctly as るい. The voiced じゅ is wrong for 種, which reads しゅ (unvoiced). The second half るい is correct, but the first half fails.
例: このショップにはアクセサリーの種類 (しゅるい) が豊富 (ほうふ) だ。 — This shop has a wide variety of accessories.

question: この辺は ＿岩＿ が多い場所だ。
explanation:
岩 is read いわ and means "rock / boulder".
岩 (いわ) means "a rock" or "a boulder" — a large, hard mass of stone in a natural setting. The sentence 「この辺は岩が多い場所だ」 means "This area is a place with many rocks." The kun-yomi いわ is the standard reading when 岩 stands alone as a noun. The on-yomi ガン appears in compounds such as 岩石 (がんせき, rock/stone, geological term) and 火成岩 (かせいがん, igneous rock). The kanji is composed of 山 (mountain) on top and 石 (stone) at the bottom — suggesting a large stone on a mountain, visually consistent with a boulder. The distractors test whether learners distinguish four types of natural terrain material.
✗ かい is the reading of 貝 (shell/shellfish). Shells and rocks are both natural hard objects, but 岩 does not read かい. 貝 (かい) and 岩 (いわ) are completely different kanji.
✗ すな is the reading of 砂, meaning "sand". Sand and rock are different materials — 砂 (すな) is fine and loose, while 岩 (いわ) is solid and massive. 岩 does not read すな.
✗ どろ is the reading of 泥, meaning "mud". Mud is wet and soft, the opposite of a hard rock. 岩 does not read どろ.
例: 川 (かわ) の中 (なか) に大 (おお) きな岩 (いわ) があって、水 (みず) が白 (しろ) く泡立 (あわだ) っていた。 — There was a large rock in the river, and the water foamed white around it.

question: たくさんの人と ＿交流＿ する。
explanation:
交流 is read こうりゅう — 交 reads こう and 流 reads りゅう, meaning "exchange / interaction".
交流 (こうりゅう) = exchange/interaction between people, cultures, or currents. 交 (こう) = to mingle/intersect, 流 (りゅう) = to flow. 「たくさんの人 (ひと) と交流 (こうりゅう) する」 — "To interact with many people." Also used in physics: 交流電気 (こうりゅうでんき, alternating current/AC).
✗ ごうりゅ: voices 交 to ごう (wrong — 交 reads unvoiced こう) and shortens 流 to りゅ (wrong — 流 reads りゅう with long vowel).
✗ ごうりゅう: voices 交 to ごう. 交 reads こう (unvoiced). ごう belongs to 号 or 合.
✗ こうりゅ: correct こう for 交 but shortens 流 to りゅ. 流 reads りゅう (long vowel), not りゅ.
例: この大学 (だいがく) は外国人学生 (がいこくじんがくせい) との交流 (こうりゅう) が盛 (さか) んだ。 — This university has active interaction with international students.

question: 荷物はフロントに ＿預けて＿ おきました。
explanation:
預けて is read あずけて, meaning "deposited / left in someone's care" — luggage was left at the front desk.
預ける (あずける) means "to deposit" or "to leave in someone's care." Its te-form 預けて (あずけて) combined with おきました (the preparatory form おく) expresses that the luggage was deliberately left at the front desk ahead of time. The sentence says: "I left the luggage 預けて (あずけて) at the front desk in advance." フロントに預けておく = "to leave at the front desk for safekeeping" is standard hotel or event vocabulary. This is the verb form of the same kanji tested in the two prior entries (hashes 7221a1458a050e3b and 78f2303124ed5ae2) — those were the noun stem form 預け; this is the te-form 預けて. The reading あずけ is the same in all three entries. The key distractor pair: とどけて (届ける, to deliver/report) vs あずけて (預ける, to leave for safekeeping). Both involve handing something over, but 届ける is one-directional delivery, while 預ける involves the recipient holding it temporarily until returned.
✗ とどけて is the te-form of 届ける (とどける), meaning "to deliver" or "to report to authorities." Delivering and entrusting for safekeeping are different: delivery is one-way (you give and the recipient keeps it); 預ける is temporary custody (you give and expect it back). 預 does not read とどけて.
✗ あすけて is a phonetically close but non-standard reading. 預 reads あずけ (voiced ず), not the unvoiced あすけ. This tests awareness of the voiced consonant in あずける.
✗ ととけて is a further phonetically distorted form of とどけて. Neither とどけ nor ととけ is a reading of 預. The correct reading is あずけ.
例: チェックアウト後 (ご) も荷物 (にもつ) をフロントに預 (あず) けて、夕方 (ゆうがた) まで観光 (かんこう) した。 — Even after checkout, I left my luggage at the front desk and sightsaw until evening.

question: わたしは ＿普通＿ 、7 時に起きます。
explanation:
普通 is read ふつう and means "usually / ordinarily".
普通 (ふつう) means "ordinary", "normal", or "usually". Both kanji use on-yomi: 普 (フ, universal/widespread) + 通 (ツウ, pass through/common). Together the word means "what is commonly spread" — the ordinary, typical state. The sentence 「わたしは普通、7時に起きます」 means "I usually wake up at 7 o'clock." The reading challenge is ふつう: 普 reads フ (short, one mora), and 通 reads ツウ (long vowel, two morae). Distractors add a long vowel to フ (making it ふう) or to both, or conflate the readings. 普 appears only in 普通 (ふつう) and 普及 (ふきゅう, dissemination) at N3 level — it is a relatively uncommon kanji outside these compounds.
✗ ふうだん adds a long vowel to 普 and replaces 通 with だん. Neither adjustment is correct — 普 reads フ (short), not フウ, and 通 reads ツウ, not だん.
✗ ふうつう adds a long vowel to 普, making it ふう instead of ふ. The on-yomi of 普 is a short フ (one mora). ふうつう is not a reading of 普通.
✗ ふだん could suggest 普段 (ふだん, usually/everyday) — a real word with similar meaning. But 普段 uses 段 (ダン, step/tier), not 通 (ツウ). 普段 and 普通 are near-synonyms but different compounds.
例: 普通 (ふつう) の新幹線 (しんかんせん) でも十分 (じゅうぶん) 速 (はや) いのに、もっと速 (はや) いのがあるとは驚 (おどろ) きだ。 — Even the regular shinkansen is fast enough, so it is surprising that there are even faster ones.

question: 理由もなく ＿疑って＿ はいけないと思う。
explanation:
疑って is read うたがって and means "doubting / suspecting" — the sentence warns against suspecting someone without reason.
疑う (うたがう) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to doubt" or "to suspect". The te-form 疑って (うたがって) connects to はいけないと思う to form "I think you should not doubt (someone)". The sentence as a whole reads: 「理由 (りゆう) もなく疑ってはいけないと思う」 — "I think you should not doubt (someone) without reason". The kanji 疑 is built from a complex structure suggesting hesitation or looking both ways before acting, which fits the meaning of doubt. The on-yomi ギ appears in compounds like 疑問 (ぎもん, question/doubt) and 疑惑 (ぎわく, suspicion), while the kun-yomi うたがう is used when the verb stands alone in conjugated form like this.
✗ ことわって is the te-form of 断る (ことわる), meaning "to refuse / to decline". Refusing someone and doubting someone are unrelated actions, and 疑 does not read ことわ.
✗ きらって is the te-form of 嫌う (きらう), meaning "to dislike / to hate". Disliking someone and suspecting them are different feelings; 疑 carries no reading beginning with きら.
✗ おこって is the te-form of 怒る (おこる), meaning "to get angry". Being angry and being suspicious are distinct emotions, and 疑 has no reading おこ.
例: 証拠 (しょうこ) もないのに人 (ひと) を疑 (うたが) うのはよくない。 — It is not right to suspect someone without evidence.

question: 来週は旅行で家を ＿留守＿ にします。
explanation:
留守 is read るす and means "being away from home / house-sitting while absent".
留守 (るす) means "being away from home" or the state where nobody is at the house. The sentence 「来週は旅行で家を留守にします」 means "Next week I will be away from home on a trip." 家を留守にする (いえをるすにする) is a set phrase meaning to leave one's house unoccupied. The reading るす is irregular — 留 typically reads リュウ (e.g., 留学, りゅうがく) but in this fixed compound it reads る. Similarly 守 typically reads シュ or まも, but in 留守 it reads す. This idiomatic reading makes the compound a classic N3 reading challenge: the on-yomi distractors りゅうす and りゅうしゅ apply the regular on-yomi to both kanji, which is incorrect for this specific word.
✗ るしゅ keeps る for 留 (which happens to be correct in this compound) but applies the standard on-yomi シュ for 守 instead of the special reading す. In 留守, 守 reads す, not しゅ.
✗ りゅうす applies the regular on-yomi リュウ to 留 (留 does read リュウ in 留学, etc.) but that regular reading does not apply in 留守. The compound uses the special reading る for 留.
✗ りゅうしゅ applies the regular on-yomi to both kanji: リュウ for 留 and シュ for 守. This would be the reading if 留守 followed standard rules, but it is an idiomatic compound with the special reading るす.
例: 留守 (るす) 中 (ちゅう) に荷物 (にもつ) が届 (とど) いてしまい、受 (う) け取 (と) れなかった。 — A package arrived while I was away, so I could not receive it.

question: このビルの ＿裏＿ に小さなレストランがあります。
explanation:
裏 is read うら, meaning "the back side" — here the back of a building, where a small restaurant is located.
裏 (うら) means "the back" or "the rear side" — the part of something not facing you, or the hidden/back portion. The sentence says: "At the back 裏 (うら) of this building, there is a small restaurant." Small shops and restaurants are commonly tucked behind larger buildings in Japanese cities, so ビルの裏 (ビルのうら, behind the building) is a very natural expression. This is a second question testing the same kanji 裏 (うら) — see also entry hash 5e526905403a7131, which tested the back of a box. The core meaning and reading are the same. The distractors here are そば (side/near), よこ (side/horizontal), and かげ (shadow), all of which describe different positional relationships but none of which is the standard word for the back side of a structure.
✗ そば is usually written in kana and means "nearby" or "beside." A restaurant nearby a building could be anywhere around it — not specifically behind it. 裏 specifically means the back side, which is a more precise location.
✗ よこ is the reading of 横 (よこ), meaning "the side" — horizontally beside something. A side restaurant and a back restaurant are at different positions. 裏 (うら) = back, 横 (よこ) = side.
✗ かげ is the reading of 影 (かげ), meaning "shadow" or "shade." A shadow is a cast image or shaded area — not the physical back of a building. 影 does not mean the rear/back side of a structure.
例: 有名 (ゆうめい) なレストランなのに、駅 (えき) のビルの裏 (うら) にあって目立 (めだ) たない。 — Even though it's a famous restaurant, it doesn't stand out because it's at the back of the station building.

question: それではゆっくり ＿呼吸＿ をしてください。
explanation:
呼吸 is read こきゅう — 呼 reads こ and 吸 reads きゅう, meaning "breathing / respiration".
呼吸 (こきゅう) = breathing or respiration. 呼 (こ) = to call/exhale, 吸 (きゅう) = to inhale/absorb. Together: the cycle of exhaling and inhaling — breathing.
