The sentence says 「それではゆっくり呼吸 (こきゅう) をしてください」 — "Now please breathe slowly." 呼吸 is used in medical instructions, yoga, meditation, and fitness contexts. The key reading trap: 呼 reads こ (not よ or こう), and 吸 reads きゅう (not ぎゅう, which would be voiced).
✗ こぎゅう: correct こ for 呼 but voices 吸 to ぎゅう. 吸 reads きゅう (unvoiced k), not ぎゅう (voiced g). ぎゅう belongs to 牛 (ぎゅう, cow/beef) — completely unrelated.
✗ よぎゅう: wrong よ for 呼 and voiced ぎゅう for 吸. 呼 reads こ, not よ. よ is a reading for 余 (よ, surplus) or 予 (よ, in advance).
✗ よきゅう: wrong よ for 呼 and correct きゅう for 吸. 呼 reads こ, not よ. Getting 吸 right (きゅう) is not enough if 呼 is misread.
例: 深 (ふか) い呼吸 (こきゅう) を繰 (く) り返 (かえ) すと、気分 (きぶん) が落 (お) ち着 (つ) く。 — Repeating deep breaths helps calm you down.

question: あの少年の ＿悲しそう＿ な顔か忘れられない。
explanation:
悲しそう is read かなしそう — 悲しい means "sad", 〜そう means the face looks that way.
悲しい (かなしい) = sad. With 〜そうな: 悲 (かな) しそうな顔 (かお) = a face that looks sad. 「あの少年 (しょうねん) の悲 (かな) しそうな顔 (かお) が忘 (わす) れられない」 — "I cannot forget that boy's sad-looking face."
✗ やさしそう = appearance of 優しい (kind). Different emotion.
✗ きびしそう = appearance of 厳しい (strict). 厳 ≠ 悲.
✗ さびしそう = appearance of 寂しい (lonely). 寂 ≠ 悲.
例: 悲 (かな) しそうな顔 (かお) で帰 (かえ) ってきた。 — He came back with a sad-looking face.

question: このあたりに ＿駐車＿ しましよう。
explanation:
駐車 is read ちゅうしや because 駐 takes on-yomi ちゅう and 車 takes on-yomi しや (written しゃ in modern kana, here transcribed as しや), forming the compound for "parking."
駐車 (ちゅうしゃ) means "parking" — stopping a vehicle and leaving it stationary. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 駐 (ちゅう) = to be stationed/to stop temporarily, and 車 (しゃ) = vehicle/car. Together they describe a vehicle (車) stopped and stationed (駐) somewhere. The sentence says: "Let's park 駐車 (ちゅうしゃ) around here." このあたりに駐車しましょう is a natural suggestion when looking for a parking spot. Note: the options in this question use the spelling しや (old kana orthography) for what in modern standard kana is しゃ (vehicle). The correct reading is ちゅうしゃ (modern) or ちゅうしや (old orthography) — same sound. The question tests recognizing ちゅう (long vowel, two morae: ち + ゅ + う) as the reading of 駐, vs the short しゅ or wrong starting syllables. 駐 also appears in 駐車場 (ちゅうしゃじょう, parking lot), 駐在員 (ちゅうざいいん, stationed employee/expatriate), and 駐日大使 (ちゅうにちたいし, ambassador to Japan).
✗ しゅしや drops the long vowel from 駐, shortening ちゅう to しゅ, and also changes the initial sound from ち to し. 駐 reads ちゅう (long vowel, starting with ち), not the short しゅ.
✗ しゅうし gives the first kanji a completely wrong reading しゅう (suggesting 週 or 集 rather than 駐), and drops the vehicle reading 車 (しゃ) entirely, replacing it with し. Both halves are wrong.
✗ ちゅしや reads 駐 as ちゅ (short, without the long vowel). 駐 reads ちゅう (three morae: ち + ゅ + う). Dropping the final う shortens the reading to two morae and does not match the standard on-yomi of 駐.
例: この近く (ちかく) には駐車場 (ちゅうしゃじょう) がないので、少 (すこ) し離 (はな) れた所 (ところ) に駐車 (ちゅうしゃ) した。 — There was no parking lot nearby, so I parked a little further away.

question: もう ＿逃げて＿ しまったようた。
explanation:
逃げて is read にげて because 逃げる means "to escape / to flee", fitting the description of something that has already run away.
逃げる (にげる) = to escape, to run away, to flee. Its て-form is 逃 (に) げて. The sentence says 「もう逃 (に) げてしまったようだ」 — "It seems (it) has already escaped." 逃げる is an ichidan verb. The kanji 逃 contains 辶 (movement) on the left and 兆 (omen/sign) on the right — moving at the first sign of danger.
✗ なげて: て-form of 投げる (なげる, to throw). Throwing something is completely different from fleeing. 投 and 逃 are different kanji, though they share a similar shape (both contain 辶 in a sense, but 投 uses 扌 not 辶).
✗ こげて: て-form of 焦げる (こげる, to get burned/charred). Getting burned is unrelated to fleeing. 焦 and 逃 are different kanji.
✗ あげて: て-form of 上げる (あげる, to raise/give). Raising or giving is unrelated to escaping. 上 and 逃 are different kanji.
例: 犯人 (はんにん) は警察 (けいさつ) から逃 (に) げた。 — The criminal escaped from the police.

question: ＿努力＿ することは大切だと思います。
explanation:
努力 is read どりょく — 努 reads ど and 力 reads りょく, meaning "effort / hard work".
努力 (どりょく) = effort, hard work, striving. 努 (ど) = to strive/exert, 力 (りょく) = strength/power. Together: exerting one's strength — making an effort. The sentence says 「努力 (どりょく) することは大切 (たいせつ) だと思 (おも) います」 — "I think making effort is important." 努 reads voiced ど (not unvoiced と). 力 reads りょく (on-yomi) in this compound. Note the options here have りよく (no long vowel) vs りょく (with long vowel) — 力 reads りょく in on-yomi compounds.
✗ どうりよく: elongates 努 to どう and shortens 力 to りよく. 努 reads ど (one mora), not どう. Also りよく is missing the long vowel — 力 reads りょく.
✗ とうりよく: unvoiced とう for 努 (wrong — 努 reads voiced ど, one mora) and short りよく for 力 (wrong — 力 reads りょく with long ょ).
✗ とりよく: unvoiced と for 努 (wrong — 努 reads voiced ど) and short りよく for 力 (wrong — 力 reads りょく).
例: 夢 (ゆめ) を実現 (じつげん) するためには、毎日 (まいにち) の努力 (どりょく) が欠 (か) かせない。 — Daily effort is essential for realizing one's dreams.

question: それは ＿過去＿ のことです。
explanation:
過去 is read かこ — 過 reads か and 去 reads こ, meaning "the past".
過去 (かこ) = the past — time that has already gone by. 過 (か) = to pass/exceed, 去 (こ) = to leave/go away. Together: time that has passed and gone. The sentence says 「それは過去 (かこ) のことです」 — "That is something from the past." Both kanji read with short on-yomi: か (one mora) and こ (one mora). The trap is elongating either to かこう or かきょ.
✗ かこう: elongates 去 to こう. 去 reads こ (one mora), not こう (two morae). こう is a reading for 向 (direction) or 校 (school).
✗ かきょ: reads 去 as きょ. 去 reads こ (on-yomi), not きょ. きょ belongs to kanji like 居 (きょ, to be/reside) or 距 (きょ, distance).
✗ かきよう: elongates 去 to きよう — doubly wrong. 去 reads こ, not きよう.
例: 過去 (かこ) を振 (ふ) り返 (かえ) るより、未来 (みらい) を見 (み) ることが大切 (たいせつ) だ。 — It is more important to look toward the future than to look back at the past.

question: 彼は話し方も ＿動作＿ もゆっくりしている。
explanation:
動作 is read どうさ because 動 takes on-yomi どう and 作 takes on-yomi さ, forming the compound meaning "movement" or "gesture."
動作 (どうさ) means "movement," "motion," or "gesture" — the physical way someone moves their body or the way a machine operates. Both kanji use on-yomi: 動 (どう) = to move, and 作 (さ/さく) = to make/act/operation. In this compound, 作 takes the shorter on-yomi さ (not さく). The sentence says: "His way of speaking and his movements 動作 (どうさ) are both slow." 動作がゆっくりしている = "movements are slow" is a natural expression. The voiced/unvoiced pair to watch is どうさ (voiced ど) vs とうさ (unvoiced と). 動 (どう) is always voiced in its on-yomi. 動 also appears in 行動 (こうどう, behavior), 運動 (うんどう, exercise), and 動物 (どうぶつ, animal). 作 also appears in 動作 (どうさ), 作品 (さくひん, work/artwork), and 操作 (そうさ, operation/control). The distractor どうさく suggests 動作 with the longer reading さく for 作, but in this compound 作 reads さ, not さく.
✗ とうさ uses the unvoiced とう for 動. The on-yomi of 動 is どう (voiced), not とう (unvoiced). とう is the reading of 到 (to reach) or 等 (equal), not 動 (to move).
✗ とうさく combines the unvoiced とう for 動 (wrong — should be どう) and the longer reading さく for 作. Both halves are incorrect: 動 reads どう and 作 reads さ in this compound.
✗ どうさく keeps the correct どう for 動 but uses the longer reading さく for 作. In the compound 動作, 作 takes its shorter on-yomi さ (one mora), not さく (two morae). どうさく is not the standard reading of 動作.
例: この機械 (きかい) の動作 (どうさ) を確認 (かくにん) してから使 (つか) ってください。 — Please check the operation of this machine before using it.

question: この国の人は ＿自然＿ を大切にしている。
explanation:
自然 is read しぜん because 自 takes the irregular on-yomi し and 然 takes on-yomi ぜん, forming the standard word for "nature."
自然 (しぜん) means "nature" — the natural world as it exists without human interference. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 自 (し) = self/own, and 然 (ぜん) = being/so/natural state. Together they describe things existing in their own natural state. The sentence says: "The people of this country treasure nature 自然 (しぜん)." 自然を大切にする = "to treasure/take care of nature" is a common environmental expression. This is a second question testing the same reading しぜん — see also entry hash 78b1841cf8ab8919, which used 美しい (beautiful) as context. The crucial reading point remains the same: 自 reads し (unvoiced) in 自然, not the more common じ (voiced). This is one of the well-known irregular on-yomi splits of 自 worth memorizing: じ appears in 自由 (じゆう, freedom) and 自動 (じどう, automatic), while し appears only in 自然 (しぜん) among common vocabulary.
✗ じぜん voices 自 to じ. In 自然, 自 reads し (unvoiced). じぜん is the reading of 事前 (じぜん, in advance/beforehand), a completely different word using 事 (matter) + 前 (before).
✗ しせん changes 然 to せん. 然 reads ぜん in this compound — the voiced ぜ is essential. せん is the reading of 線 (line), 泉 (spring), or 先 (ahead), not 然.
✗ じせん voices 自 to じ and also changes 然 to せん. Both halves are wrong. This combines the two errors of the other wrong options.
例: この地域 (ちいき) は自然 (しぜん) が豊 (ゆた) かで、多 (おお) くの野鳥 (やちょう) が生息 (せいそく) している。 — This region is rich in nature and is home to many wild birds.

question: あと 30 ＿秒＿ で完成します。
explanation:
秒 is read びょう and means "second" (unit of time).
秒 (びょう) means "a second" — the smallest standard unit of time. The sentence 「あと30秒で完成します」 means "It will be finished in 30 more seconds." The on-yomi ビョウ is the standard reading for this kanji. The kanji 秒 is composed of 禾 (rice plant/grain radical) + 少 (small/few), visually suggesting something tiny — fitting for the smallest unit of time. The reading challenge here is the voiced vs. unvoiced distinction: じょう (ジョウ), しょう (ショウ), びょう (ビョウ), and ひょう (ヒョウ) all follow a similar pattern. ビョウ (voiced) is the correct reading for the time unit 秒.
✗ じょう (ジョウ) corresponds to various kanji — 錠 (lock), 畳 (tatami), 条 (clause), etc. None of these is 秒. じょう does not refer to the time unit "second".
✗ しょう (ショウ) is the on-yomi of many kanji including 小 (small) and 少 (few/little). The component 少 is inside 秒, which may cause confusion, but 秒 reads ビョウ (voiced), not ショウ (unvoiced).
✗ ひょう (ヒョウ) is the on-yomi of kanji like 票 (ballot/vote) and 標 (mark/target). It is the unvoiced version of ビョウ, but the correct reading of 秒 is the voiced ビョウ.
例: 彼 (かれ) は100メートルを10秒 (びょう) 台 (だい) で走 (はし) れるほど速 (はや) い。 — He is so fast that he can run 100 meters in under 10 seconds.

question: 夏休みも ＿残り＿ 三日になってしまった。
explanation:
残り is read のこり, meaning "the remaining" — only three days of summer vacation are left.
残り (のこり) is a noun meaning "the remainder" or "what is left" — derived from the verb 残る (のこる, to remain). The sentence says: "Summer vacation also has only 3 days remaining 残り (のこり)." 残り三日になってしまった = "it has come down to just three days remaining" — expressing a bittersweet feeling that something is almost over. The kanji 残 uses the kun-yomi のこ in verb and noun forms: 残る (のこる, to remain), 残り (のこり, the remainder), and 残す (のこす, to leave behind). Its on-yomi ざん appears in 残業 (ざんぎょう, overtime) and 残念 (ざんねん, regret/disappointment). The four distractors are all no-ri pattern nouns (a verb stem + り used as a noun): もとり (non-standard), おわり (終わり, the end), のこり (残り, the remainder), and あまり (余り, the surplus/quite). 終わり means the end has already come; 余り means leftover surplus (or "quite"). 残り specifically means what has not yet finished — the time or amount still left to go.
✗ もとり does not correspond to any standard word. 元 (もと, origin) does not combine with り in this way as a standard noun. This is a phonetically constructed distractor with no real meaning.
✗ おわり is the reading of 終わり (おわり), meaning "the end." Summer vacation ending is described as having 3 days remaining, not as already being over. 残 does not read おわり.
✗ あまり is the reading of 余り (あまり), meaning "surplus" or "remainder after subtraction," and also functions as an adverb meaning "quite/too much" (あまり好きじゃない, I don't like it very much). While 余り (あまり) and 残り (のこり) both mean "what's left," 余り emphasizes excess or leftover after use, while 残り emphasizes time or quantity that has not yet been used up. 残 does not read あまり.
例: 試験 (しけん) まで残 (のこ) り一週間 (いっしゅうかん) なのに、まだ全部 (ぜんぶ) 勉強 (べんきょう) できていない。 — There is only one week left until the exam, and I still haven't studied everything.

question: このグラフは、人口の ＿増減＿ を表している。
explanation:
増減 is read ぞうげん — 増 reads ぞう and 減 reads げん, meaning "rise and fall".
増減 (ぞうげん) = fluctuation. 「このグラフは人口 (じんこう) の増減 (ぞうげん) を表 (あらわ) している」 — "This graph shows the rise and fall of the population." Voicing: 増 = ぞう (not じょう), 減 = げん (not けん).
✗ ぞうけん: correct ぞう for 増 but unvoiced けん for 減.
✗ じょうけん: wrong じょう for 増 and wrong けん for 減.
✗ じょうげん: correct げん for 減 but wrong じょう for 増.
例: 地方 (ちほう) の人口 (じんこう) の増減 (ぞうげん) をグラフで示 (しめ) した。 — The population fluctuation in rural areas was shown in a graph.

question: 面接の結果は、1 週間以内に ＿通知＿ します。
explanation:
通知 is read つうち because 通 takes on-yomi つう and 知 takes on-yomi ち, forming the standard word for "notification."
通知 (つうち) means "notification" or "notice" — officially informing someone of a result, decision, or fact. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 通 (つう) = to pass through/notify, and 知 (ち) = to know/to inform. Together they describe the act of making something known by sending information through to the recipient. The sentence says: "The results 結果 (けっか) of the interview 面接 (めんせつ) will be notified 通知 (つうち) within one week." This is a standard business communication phrase. The long vowel in つう is essential: つう (two morae: つ + う), not the short つ. And 知 reads ち (one mora), not the elongated し. The four options test two phonological axes: the long vowel (つう vs とお) and the unvoiced/voiced pair (ち vs し). Correct: つう + ち = つうち. 通 also appears in 通学 (つうがく, commuting to school), 通勤 (つうきん, commuting to work), and 交通 (こうつう, traffic/transportation).
✗ とおち uses とお for 通, as if reading it like 遠い (とおい, far) or 通り (とおり, street). The on-yomi of 通 in this compound is つう (not とお). とお is the kun-yomi used in 通り (とおり) and 通る (とおる, to pass through), not the on-yomi compound reading.
✗ つうし uses し instead of ち for 知. 知 reads ち (on-yomi) in compounds. し is the reading of 詩 (poem) or 市 (city), not 知. つうし might suggest 通史 (つうし, general history), which uses a different second kanji.
✗ とおし combines both errors: とお for 通 (should be つう) and し for 知 (should be ち). This reading does not correspond to 通知. とおし sounds like 通し (とおし), meaning "from start to finish" or "straight through" — a different word.
例: 合格 (ごうかく) の通知 (つうち) が届 (とど) いたとき、思 (おも) わず声 (こえ) を上 (あ) げてしまった。 — When the acceptance notification arrived, I couldn't help but let out a shout.

question: 庭に ＿生えた＿ 草にきれいな花が咲いていた。
explanation:
生えた is read はえた and means "grew / sprouted" — describing grass that grew in the garden.
生える (はえる) is a kun-yomi intransitive verb meaning "to grow" or "to sprout" — used for plants, grass, teeth, and hair that emerge naturally. The ta-form 生えた (はえた) modifies the noun 草 (くさ, grass): 「庭に生えた草にきれいな花が咲いていた」 — "The grass that had grown in the garden had beautiful flowers blooming." The kanji 生 has multiple kun-yomi: うまれる (to be born), いきる (to live), はえる (to grow/sprout), and multiple on-yomi including セイ and ショウ. The sprouting sense はえる is specific to natural emergence from the ground or from a surface, setting it apart from 育つ (そだつ, to grow up/be raised), which implies nurture.
✗ せいえた is not a valid reading of 生えた. While 生 can read セイ, the verb 生える uses the kun-yomi はえ, not the on-yomi. Attaching an on-yomi stem to a verb inflection ending is not standard Japanese.
✗ しようえた is not a reading of 生えた. しよう would correspond to 使用 (しよう, use) — a completely different word. 生 in this verb context always reads は.
✗ うえた is the past form of 植える (うえる), meaning "to plant (intentionally)". 植 (うえ) implies human planting action; 生える (はえる) implies natural growth without anyone planting. The meaning contrast is intentional vs. spontaneous.
例: 春 (はる) になると、土 (つち) からいろいろな芽 (め) が生 (は) えてくる。 — When spring comes, all sorts of sprouts emerge from the soil.

question: 外国で一人暮らしをしているので、国の料理が ＿恋しく＿ なる。
explanation:
恋しく is read こいしく and means "longing for / missing (something)" — missing home cooking while living abroad.
恋しい (こいしい) is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "longing for" or "missing (something cherished)". The adverb form 恋しく (こいしく) appears in the sentence 「外国で一人暮らしをしているので、国の料理が恋しくなる」 — "Because I am living alone abroad, I end up longing for my home country's food." The feeling 恋しい is a deep emotional longing — like homesickness for a person, a food, or a place — rather than simple desire. The on-yomi レン appears in: 恋愛 (れんあい, romantic love), 失恋 (しつれん, heartbreak). The four distractors describe related but distinct emotions: なつかしい (nostalgic), うれしい (happy), ほしい (wanting something).
✗ なつかしく comes from 懐かしい (なつかしい), meaning "nostalgic / fondly remembered". Nostalgia and longing overlap but differ: なつかしい is about a fond memory of the past, while 恋しい is about a current yearning for something absent.
✗ うれしく comes from 嬉しい (うれしい), meaning "happy / delighted". Being happy and longing for something are opposite emotional states — 恋しい describes an ache for something missing, not joy.
✗ ほしく comes from 欲しい (ほしい), meaning "wanting (an object)" or "wishing to have". 欲しい is more about desire for a specific thing, while 恋しい carries deeper emotional attachment and longing.
例: 長 (なが) い出張 (しゅっちょう) が続 (つづ) き、家族 (かぞく) が恋 (こい) しくてたまらなかった。 — After a long series of business trips, I was longing unbearably for my family.

question: これを ＿郵送＿ してください。
explanation:
郵送 is read ゆうそう — 郵 reads ゆう and 送 reads そう, meaning "mailing / sending by post".
郵送 (ゆうそう) = sending by mail/post. 郵 (ゆう) = postal/mail, 送 (そう) = to send. The sentence says 「これを郵送 (ゆうそう) してください」 — "Please send this by mail." 郵 reads ゆう (long vowel, two morae) — a common error is shortening to ゆ. Related: 郵便 (ゆうびん, postal mail), 郵便局 (ゆうびんきょく, post office).
✗ ほそう: wrong ほ for 郵 (should be ゆう) and wrong そう — wait, そう is correct for 送. But ほ is completely wrong for 郵. ほ belongs to 補 (ほ, to supplement) or 保 (ほ, to protect).
✗ ほうそう: ほう for 郵 is wrong. 郵 reads ゆう, not ほう. ほうそう reads 放送 (ほうそう, broadcast) — a different word entirely.
✗ ゆそう: shortens 郵 to ゆ, dropping the long vowel. 郵 reads ゆう (two morae). ゆそう is not a real word.
例: 書類 (しょるい) を郵送 (ゆうそう) する場合 (ばあい) は、封筒 (ふうとう) に入 (い) れて送 (おく) ってください。 — When sending documents by mail, please put them in an envelope.

question: その会社の ＿情報＿ はインターネットで見ました。
explanation:
情報 is read じょうほう and means "information".
情報 (じょうほう) is an on-yomi compound: 情 (ジョウ, feeling/condition/information) + 報 (ホウ, report/news). Together the word means "reported information" — news, data, or intelligence. The sentence 「その会社の情報はインターネットで見ました」 means "I found information about that company on the internet." The reading challenge is ジョウホウ: both kanji use their on-yomi with long vowels. ジョウ for 情 (two morae: jou) and ホウ for 報 (two morae: hou). Distractors mix up チョウ for 情 (wrong reading) and ボウ for 報 (wrong voiced reading). 情 appears in: 感情 (かんじょう, emotion), 事情 (じじょう, circumstances). 報 appears in: 報告 (ほうこく, report), 情報 (じょうほう, information).
✗ ちょうほう misreads 情 as チョウ. 情 reads ジョウ (with an initial j-sound and a long ou-vowel), not チョウ. チョウ belongs to 調 (investigate/tune) or 朝 (morning), not 情.
✗ じょうぼう voices 報 to ボウ. 報 reads ホウ (unvoiced h-), not ボウ (voiced b-). ボウ belongs to 望 (hope) or 棒 (rod), not 報 (report/news).
✗ ちょうぼう misreads both kanji — チョウ for 情 (should be ジョウ) and ボウ for 報 (should be ホウ). Both errors combined.
例: 個人 (こじん) 情報 (じょうほう) はインターネット上 (じょう) に不用意 (ふようい) に公開 (こうかい) しないほうがいい。 — You should not carelessly disclose personal information on the internet.

question: 兄は、 ＿現在＿ は海外で働いています。
explanation:
現在 is read げんざい — both kanji voiced (げん, ざい), meaning "currently / at present".
現在 (げんざい) = currently/at present. The sentence says 「兄 (あに) は現在 (げんざい) 海外 (かいがい) で働 (はたら) いています」. Both voiced: 現 = げん (not けん), 在 = ざい (not さい).
✗ けんさい: unvoiced けん for 現.
✗ げんさい: correct げん but unvoiced さい for 在.
✗ けんざい: unvoiced けん + correct ざい. Both must be voiced.
例: 現在 (げんざい) この路線 (ろせん) は工事中 (こうじちゅう) です。 — This line is currently under construction.

question: 小さくて ＿丸い＿ いすがほしいです
explanation:
丸い is read まるい, meaning "round" or "circular" — the sentence describes a small round chair.
丸い (まるい) is an i-adjective meaning "round," "circular," or "spherical." The kanji 丸 uses the kun-yomi まる in adjective form. The sentence says: "I want a small and round 丸い (まるい) chair." A round stool is a common furniture item, so this context is natural. The kun-yomi まる also appears in 丸 (まる, a circle/full), 丸め る (まるめる, to roll into a ball), and 日の丸 (ひのまる, the Japanese flag — literally "circle of the sun"). The on-yomi がん appears in 丸薬 (がんやく, pill/capsule) and 弾丸 (だんがん, bullet). The four distractor options are all common i-adjectives with the -い ending, testing whether the student can recognize the kanji 丸 as まる rather than matching it to another adjective by sound pattern.
✗ くろい is the reading of 黒い, meaning "black." A color adjective does not describe the shape of a chair. 丸 has no reading that begins with く.
✗ あおい is the reading of 青い, meaning "blue." Again a color adjective — 丸 does not read あお, and a color has nothing to do with describing a chair's shape as "round."
✗ かるい is the reading of 軽い, meaning "light" (in weight). While a light chair might also be desirable, the kanji here is 丸, which means "round" and reads まる, not かる.
例: 子供 (こども) は丸 (まる) いボールを抱 (だ) えて走 (はし) り回 (まわ) っていた。 — The child was running around holding a round ball.

question: その歌は日本でも ＿有名＿ です。
explanation:
有名 is read ゆうめい and means "famous / well-known".
有名 (ゆうめい) is an on-yomi compound: 有 (ユウ, to have/exist) + 名 (メイ, name/fame). Together the word means "having a (well-known) name" — famous. The sentence 「その歌は日本でも有名です」 means "That song is famous in Japan as well." The reading challenge is the long vowel in ユウ (two beats). Distractors ゆめ and ゆめい drop the vowel length entirely or shorten it, while ゆうめ cuts one mora short. The on-yomi ユウ for 有 appears in: 有名 (ゆうめい, famous), 有利 (ゆうり, advantageous), 有効 (ゆうこう, valid/effective). The on-yomi メイ for 名 appears in: 有名 (ゆうめい), 氏名 (しめい, full name), 名前 (なまえ uses kun-yomi).
✗ ゆめ shortens both kanji readings — 有 loses its long vowel ユウ→ゆ, and 名 loses its reading entirely to a single mora. This is not a reading of 有名.
✗ ゆめい shortens 有 from ユウ (two morae) to ゆ (one mora), producing an incorrect reading. The long vowel in ゆう is required.
✗ ゆうめ shortens 名 from メイ (two morae) to め (one mora), dropping the final い. The full reading is ゆうめい — both halves must be two morae each.
例: あの監督 (かんとく) は国際的 (こくさいてき) に有名 (ゆうめい) な映画 (えいが) を何本 (なんぼん) も撮 (と) っている。 — That director has made many internationally famous films.

question: そこの通りの ＿角＿ に、コンビニができたそうだ。
explanation:
角 is read かど meaning "corner", fitting the location of a convenience store at the street corner.
角 (かど) = corner — where two streets meet. 「そこの通 (とお) りの角 (かど) に、コンビニができたそうだ」 — "I heard a convenience store opened at the corner of that street." Also reads かく (square), つの (horn), but street-corner context → かど.
✗ そば = nearby/beside. Describes proximity, not a corner meeting-point.
✗ はし = reading for 端 (edge/end) or 橋 (bridge). Linear boundary, not a corner.
✗ よこ = reading for 横 (side). Lateral proximity, not a corner.
例: 左 (ひだり) の角 (かど) を曲 (ま) がると郵便局 (ゆうびんきょく) があります。 — Turn at the left corner and there is a post office.

question: 大切なものなので、丁寧に ＿包んで＿ ください。
explanation:
包んで is read つつんで, meaning "wrap" — the instruction is to wrap a precious item carefully.
包む (つつむ) means "to wrap" — covering something by folding material around it, like wrapping a gift or a fragile item. Its te-form 包んで (つつんで) is used in instructions. The sentence says: "Since this is something precious, please wrap 包んで (つつんで) it carefully 丁寧に (ていねいに)." The kanji 包 uses the kun-yomi つつ in verb form. Its on-yomi ほう appears in compounds like 包装 (ほうそう, packaging/wrapping), 包含 (ほうがん, inclusion), and 小包 (こづつみ, parcel/package). The radical of 包 is 勹 (wrapping), which visually shows something being enfolded — directly representing the act of wrapping. The distractors are all te-form verbs with similar sound patterns or contexts: 畳んで (たたんで, to fold/fold up), 運んで (はこんで, to carry), and 進んで (すすんで, to advance). Folding, carrying, and advancing are related to handling objects but none means to wrap.
✗ たたんで is the te-form of 畳む (たたむ), meaning "to fold" something flat — like folding laundry or a map. Folding flat and wrapping around are different actions. 包 does not read たたんで.
✗ はこんで is the te-form of 運ぶ (はこぶ), meaning "to carry" or "to transport." Carrying and wrapping are different: you carry something after wrapping it, not instead of wrapping. 包 does not read はこんで.
✗ すすんで is the te-form of 進む (すすむ), meaning "to advance" or "to go forward." Advancing has no connection to wrapping a precious object. 包 does not read すすんで.
例: プレゼントを丁寧 (ていねい) に包 (つつ) んで、リボンをつけた。 — I carefully wrapped the present and attached a ribbon.

question: それは、もう ＿計算＿ しました。
explanation:
計算 is read けいさん because 計 takes on-yomi けい and 算 takes on-yomi さん, forming the standard word for "calculation."
計算 (けいさん) means "calculation" or "computing a number." Both kanji take their on-yomi: 計 (けい) means "to count, measure, or plan," and 算 (さん) means "to calculate" or "arithmetic." Together they reinforce each other: counting (計) and calculating (算). The long vowel in けい is essential — けい is two morae (け + い), not a short け. The sentence says: "I already calculated 計算 (けいさん) that." 計算する is the standard verb for doing arithmetic or computing a total. 計 also appears in 計画 (けいかく, plan), 時計 (とけい, clock/watch), and 合計 (ごうけい, total). 算 also appears in 算数 (さんすう, arithmetic) and 暗算 (あんざん, mental arithmetic). The distractor けいけん reads 経験 (けいけん, experience) — a common N3 word, but 経験 uses 経 (けい) and 験 (けん), completely different kanji from 計算.
✗ けいけん is the reading of 経験 (けいけん), meaning "experience." It is a real and common word, but uses the kanji 経 (けい) and 験 (けん). Neither matches the kanji 計 or 算 in the question.
✗ けけん drops the long vowel from 計, shortening けい to けく. 計 reads けい with a long vowel — omitting the い produces a non-existent syllable sequence that does not correspond to any word.
✗ けさん drops the long vowel from 計, shortening けい to け. Without the elongated vowel, the reading of 計 is lost. けさん does not correspond to any real word using these kanji.
例: お会計 (おかいけい) の前に計算 (けいさん) を確認 (かくにん) してください。 — Please check the calculation before paying.

question: この店では、いろいろな ＿容器＿ を売っています。
explanation:
容器 is read ようき because 容 takes on-yomi よう and 器 takes on-yomi き, forming the compound meaning "container."
容器 (ようき) means "container" or "vessel" — any object that holds or stores something (jars, bottles, bowls, tanks). The compound uses the on-yomi of both kanji: 容 (よう) means "to hold, to contain" or "appearance/form," and 器 (き) means "vessel, tool, or implement." The sentence says: "This shop sells various types of containers 容器 (ようき)." The long vowel in よう is important — it is ようき (three beats: よ + う + き), not ようぎ. 容 appears in 容量 (ようりょう, capacity) and 内容 (ないよう, content). 器 appears in 食器 (しょっき, tableware) and 楽器 (がっき, musical instrument). The voicing ようぎ is a common trap, but 器 reads き (unvoiced) in this word. The distractors どうぐ and どうく are the word 道具 (どうぐ, tool/utensil) and a non-existent variant — both use entirely different kanji.
✗ ようぎ voices the second syllable as ぎ, but 器 reads き (unvoiced) in this compound. ようぎ (容疑) is a real word meaning "suspicion (of a crime)," written with different kanji — 疑 (ぎ). The sentence context of a shop selling items makes 容疑 nonsensical.
✗ どうぐ is the reading of 道具 (どうぐ), meaning "tool" or "implement." It uses the kanji 道 and 具, completely different from 容器. While tools and containers both relate to physical objects, the kanji being tested here (容器) does not read どうぐ.
✗ どうく does not correspond to any standard word. 道具 reads どうぐ with a voiced ぐ, not the unvoiced く offered here. This option is a phonetically distorted version of 道具.
例: プラスチック製 (せい) の容器 (ようき) は軽 (かる) くて便利 (べんり) だ。 — Plastic containers are light and convenient.

question: 山本さんは何と何を ＿比べた＿ んですか。
explanation:
比べた is read くらべた and means "compared" — what did Yamamoto compare?
比べる (くらべる) is a kun-yomi transitive verb meaning "to compare". The ta-form 比べた (くらべた) appears in the question 「山本さんは何と何を比べたんですか」 — "What did Yamamoto compare with what?" The kanji 比 contains two 匕 (person/spoon-like) components side by side — visually depicting two things placed next to each other for comparison. The on-yomi ヒ appears in: 比較 (ひかく, comparison), 比率 (ひりつ, ratio), 対比 (たいひ, contrast). When 比 appears as a standalone verb, the reading is always くら.
✗ ならべた is the past form of 並べる (ならべる), meaning "to line things up / to arrange". Arranging things in a row and comparing them are different — ならべる places things side by side physically, while くらべる evaluates their similarities/differences.
✗ しらべた is the past form of 調べる (しらべる), meaning "to investigate / to look into". Investigating and comparing are related (you might compare as part of an investigation), but they are different verbs and 比 does not read しら.
✗ えらべた is the past form of 選べる (えらべる, potential form of 選ぶ), meaning "to be able to choose". Choosing and comparing are related (you compare before choosing), but 比 does not read えら.
例: 去年 (きょねん) と今年 (ことし) のデータを比 (くら) べると、大 (おお) きな違 (ちが) いはなかった。 — When comparing last year's data with this year's, there was no major difference.

question: 書類が ＿複数＿ あるので、間違えないでください。
explanation:
複数 is read ふくすう and means "plural / multiple (items)".
複数 (ふくすう) is an on-yomi compound: 複 (フク, double/multiple) + 数 (スウ, number). Together the word means "plural" — more than one item. The sentence 「書類が複数あるので、間違えないでください」 means "There are multiple documents, so please do not mix them up." The reading ふくすう uses the on-yomi for both: フク + スウ. The phonological trap is the long vowel in スウ (two beats) versus the short ス. Japanese learners commonly drop the long vowel, producing the non-word ふくす. The kanji 複 uses the 衤 (clothing) radical with a component meaning "layered" — visually suggesting duplication or repetition.
✗ ふくす drops the long vowel from 数 (スウ). The on-yomi of 数 is スウ (long), not ス (short). ふくす is not a valid reading of this compound.
✗ ふうすう adds a long vowel to 複 instead — the on-yomi of 複 is フク (short), not フウ (long). Misplacing the length creates a non-word.
✗ ふうす gets both kanji wrong: 複 becomes フウ (too long) and 数 becomes ス (too short). Neither adjustment is correct.
例: この問題 (もんだい) には複数 (ふくすう) の解答 (かいとう) が考 (かんが) えられる。 — Multiple answers can be considered for this problem.

question: 昨日病院で ＿血圧＿ を計りました。
explanation:
血圧 is read けつあつ — 血 reads けつ (blood) and 圧 reads あつ (pressure), meaning "blood pressure".
血圧 (けつあつ) = blood pressure. 血 (けつ) = blood, 圧 (あつ) = pressure. The sentence says 「昨日 (きのう) 病院 (びょういん) で血圧 (けつあつ) を計 (はか) りました」 — "I measured my blood pressure at the hospital yesterday." 血 reads けつ in this on-yomi compound (not its kun-yomi ち). The compound けつあつ must be distinguished from ちあつ, which uses the kun-yomi ち for 血 — ちあつ is not the standard medical term; けつあつ is.
✗ けつやつ: correct けつ for 血 but wrong やつ for 圧. 圧 reads あつ, not やつ. やつ is a colloquial word for "thing/fellow" or the reading for 奴 (やつ), unrelated to 圧.
✗ ちあつ: uses kun-yomi ち for 血. While ち is the kun-yomi of 血 (ちしお = lifeblood, 血 = blood in poetry), the medical compound 血圧 uses on-yomi けつ + あつ = けつあつ.
✗ ちやつ: uses kun-yomi ち for 血 (already wrong) and wrong やつ for 圧. Both readings are incorrect.
例: 毎日 (まいにち) 血圧 (けつあつ) を測 (はか) るのが健康管理 (けんこうかんり) のコツだ。 — Measuring blood pressure every day is key to health management.

question: ここから見る ＿夕日＿ はきれいだ。
explanation:
夕日 is read ゆうひ and means "the setting sun / the evening sun".
夕日 (ゆうひ) is a kun-yomi compound: 夕 (ゆう, evening) + 日 (ひ, sun). Together the word means "the sun as seen in the evening" — the setting sun. The sentence 「ここから見る夕日はきれいだ」 means "The setting sun seen from here is beautiful." The reading challenge is ゆうひ: 夕 reads ゆう (long vowel) and 日 reads ひ (kun-yomi, not にち or じつ). When 日 appears as the second element of a nature/time compound with a kun-yomi first element, it almost always takes the kun-yomi ひ: 夕日 (ゆうひ), 朝日 (あさひ, morning sun), 日差し (ひざし, sunlight). The four distractors all drop the long vowel in ゆう or misread ひ as び (voiced).
✗ ゆび drops the long vowel from 夕 — 夕 reads ゆう (two morae), not ゆ (one mora). Also, ゆび is the reading of 指 (finger), an entirely different word.
✗ ゆひ drops the long vowel from 夕 (ゆう → ゆ) while reading 日 correctly as ひ. The long vowel in ゆう is essential.
✗ ゆうび keeps the long ゆう but voices ひ to び. 日 reads ひ (unvoiced h-sound) in this compound, not び (voiced b-sound).
例: 海 (うみ) に沈 (しず) む夕日 (ゆうひ) を眺 (なが) めながら、二人 (ふたり) でコーヒーを飲 (の) んだ。 — We drank coffee together while gazing at the sun setting into the sea.

question: そこに一人で行くのは ＿難しい＿ と思います。
explanation:
難しい is read むずかしい, meaning "difficult" — going to a certain place alone is described as hard.
難しい (むずかしい) is an i-adjective meaning "difficult" or "hard." The sentence says: "I think it is difficult 難しい (むずかしい) to go there alone." This is a common expression of uncertainty or concern about a challenging situation. The kanji 難 uses the kun-yomi むずか in adjective form. Its on-yomi なん appears in compounds like 難問 (なんもん, difficult question), 困難 (こんなん, difficulty/hardship), and 難易度 (なんいど, level of difficulty). The four distractors are all i-adjectives testing whether students can correctly recognize 難しい among visually or phonologically similar words: きびしい (厳しい, strict/harsh), めずらしい (珍しい, rare/unusual), さびしい (寂しい, lonely), and むずかしい (難しい, difficult). The key: 難 (むずか) is the kanji for difficulty, not strictness, rarity, or loneliness.
✗ きびしい is the reading of 厳しい (きびしい), meaning "strict" or "harsh." Strictness and difficulty are related but different: a strict teacher is 厳しい; a hard exam is 難しい. 難 does not read きびしい.
✗ めずらしい is the reading of 珍しい (めずらしい), meaning "rare" or "unusual." Something that is rare may or may not be difficult. 難 does not read めずらしい.
✗ さびしい is the reading of 寂しい (さびしい), meaning "lonely." Going alone to a place might feel lonely (さびしい) and also be difficult (むずかしい), but these are separate feelings. 難 does not read さびしい.
例: 日本語の敬語 (けいご) は外国人 (がいこくじん) にとって難 (むずか) しいと感 (かん) じる人 (ひと) が多 (おお) い。 — Many foreigners find Japanese honorific language difficult.

question: 中村さんから出張の ＿件＿ でお電話がありました。
explanation:
件 is read けん — it means "matter / case".
件 (けん) = matter, case. The sentence says 「中村 (なかむら) さんから出張 (しゅっちょう) の件 (けん) でお電話 (でんわ) がありました」 — "There was a call regarding the business trip matter."
✗ けい: not a reading for 件.
✗ よう: reading for 用 or 様, not 件.
✗ よん: reading for 四 (four). No connection.
例: ご注文 (ちゅうもん) の件 (けん) でご確認 (かくにん) ください。 — Please confirm the matter of your order.

question: ここを ＿横断＿ するときは気をつけてください。
explanation:
横断 is read おうだん — on-yomi compound meaning "crossing a road".
横断 (おうだん): 横 (おう) = horizontal, 断 (だん) = cut across. The sentence says 「ここを横断 (おうだん) するときは気をつけてください」 — "Please be careful when crossing here." Standard traffic term; 横断歩道 (おうだんほどう, pedestrian crossing) uses the same compound.
✗ おうざん: correct おう for 横 but ざん is not a reading for 断. 断 reads だん.
✗ きだん: き is not a reading for 横. 横 reads おう (on) or よこ (kun).
✗ きざん: ki is not a reading for 横 and ざん is not correct for 断.
例: 横断歩道 (おうだんほどう) では左右 (さゆう) を確認 (かくにん) してから渡 (わた) りましょう。 — At a pedestrian crossing, check both sides before crossing.

question: 每日 ＿復習＿ したので、よくできるようになつた。
explanation:
復習 is read ふくしゅう because 復 takes on-yomi ふく and 習 takes on-yomi しゅう, forming the compound meaning "to review" previously learned material.
復習 (ふくしゅう) means "review" — returning to material already studied to reinforce understanding. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 復 (ふく) = to return/repeat, and 習 (しゅう) = to practice/learn. Together they describe going back (復) to practice again (習). The sentence says: "Because I reviewed 復習 (ふくしゅう) every day, I was able to do well." 毎日復習したのでよくできるようになった is a natural cause-and-effect sentence about consistent study habits. This is the same compound as the earlier kana-writing entry (hash 97eed3555311061d), which tested the kanji selection. This entry tests the reading of the established kanji 復習. The long vowel in しゅう is important: 習 reads しゅう (three morae: し + ゅ + う). The distractors include ふうしゅう (wrong long vowel placement), れんしゅう (練習, practice), れいしゅう (non-standard), and ふくしゅう (correct).
✗ ふうしゅう misreads 復 as ふう (with a long vowel in the wrong place). 復 reads ふく (two morae: ふ + く), not the elongated ふう (two morae: ふ + う — which would correspond to 封 or 風). The elongation is in the wrong syllable.
✗ れんしゅう is the reading of 練習 (れんしゅう), meaning "practice" or "rehearsal." 練習 uses 練 (れん, to train/knead) + 習 (しゅう, to learn). It is a real word but uses different first kanji. 復 does not read れん.
✗ れいしゅう assigns れい to 復. 復 reads ふく, not れい. れい is the reading of 礼 (etiquette), 令 (order), or 例 (example) — not 復. れいしゅう does not correspond to any real word in this context.
例: 授業 (じゅぎょう) で習 (なら) ったことをその日のうちに復習 (ふくしゅう) するのが大切 (たいせつ) だ。 — It is important to review what you learned in class on the same day.

question: ＿小型＿ のラジオが欲しいです。
explanation:
小型 is read こがた because 小 takes the kun-yomi こ and 型 takes the kun-yomi がた, forming the compound meaning "small size / compact."
小型 (こがた) means "small size," "compact," or "miniaturized" — describing something that is a smaller version of its normal size. The compound uses the kun-yomi of both kanji: 小 (こ) = small, and 型 (がた) = size/type/mold. Together they describe the small-size version of something: 小型ラジオ (こがたラジオ, compact radio), 小型犬 (こがたいぬ, small dog), 小型車 (こがたしゃ, compact car). The sentence says: "I want a small 小型 (こがた) radio." The key distinction: 小 reads こ here (kun-yomi, short), not しょう (on-yomi used in 小学校 しょうがっこう, elementary school). And 型 reads がた (voiced) — the standard reading after 小. The distractor しようがた suggests 使用型 or a similar compound, wrongly applying on-yomi しょう to 小, while also applying longer readings where simpler ones apply.
✗ こかた leaves 型 unvoiced as かた. In the compound 小型, 型 takes the voiced reading がた (voiced after the connecting の in 〜型). こかた is not a standard reading of 小型.
✗ しようがた uses the on-yomi しょう (or possibly しよう, an extended reading) for 小. In 小型, 小 takes its kun-yomi こ — short and direct. しよう/しょう is used in formal Sino-Japanese compounds, not in this everyday sizing compound.
✗ しようかた combines the extended しよう reading for 小 and the unvoiced かた for 型. Both are wrong: 小 reads こ (kun-yomi) and 型 reads がた (voiced). Neither change is supported.
例: 小型 (こがた) のノートパソコンは持 (も) ち運 (はこ) びが簡単 (かんたん) だ。 — A compact laptop is easy to carry around.

question: 理由もないのに、人を ＿疑って＿ はいけない。
explanation:
疑って is read うたがって — 疑う means "to suspect / to doubt", fitting the warning not to doubt people without reason.
疑う (うたがう) = to suspect or doubt. て-form: 疑 (うたが) って. 「理由 (りゆう) もないのに、人 (ひと) を疑 (うたが) ってはいけない」 — "You must not suspect people without reason." Related: 疑問 (ぎもん, question/doubt), 疑惑 (ぎわく, suspicion).
✗ きらって: て-form of 嫌う (きらう, to dislike/hate). Disliking ≠ suspecting.
✗ こわがって: て-form of 怖がる (こわがる, to be afraid). Being afraid ≠ suspecting.
✗ しかって: て-form of 叱る (しかる, to scold). Scolding ≠ suspecting.
例: 証拠 (しょうこ) もなく人 (ひと) を疑 (うたが) うのは失礼 (しつれい) だ。 — It is rude to suspect someone without evidence.

question: ここから先は道が ＿細く＿ なっている。
explanation:
細く is read ほそく because 細い means "narrow / thin", fitting the description of the road becoming narrow.
細い (ほそい) = narrow, thin (describing width). Its adverbial/continuative form 細 (ほそ) く. The sentence says 「ここから先 (さき) は道 (みち) が細 (ほそ) くなっている」 — "From here onward, the road becomes narrow." 細い describes something thin in width — a narrow road, a thin rope, a slim figure. 細く (ほそく) is the く-form used to describe a change of state (なっている = has become).
✗ ひろく: く-form of 広い (ひろい, wide). Wide is the opposite of narrow. The sentence describes the road becoming narrow, not wide.
✗ ふとく: く-form of 太い (ふとい, thick/fat — describing girth). 太い describes bulk or circumference (a thick rope, a fat body), not width in the 2D sense. Also, the road is getting narrower, not thicker.
✗ せまく: く-form of 狭い (せまい, narrow — describing space). 狭い describes a cramped or confined space. While 細い (narrow in width) and 狭い (cramped) are both "narrow", the kanji on the page is 細, not 狭. 細い refers to thinness/narrowness of an object's width.
例: 山道 (やまみち) は途中 (とちゅう) から細 (ほそ) くなって歩 (ある) きにくかった。 — The mountain path became narrow midway and was difficult to walk.

question: 川井さんは明日、 ＿退院＿ するそうです。
explanation:
退院 is read たいいん because 退 takes on-yomi たい and 院 takes on-yomi いん, forming the compound meaning "leaving the hospital."
退院 (たいいん) means "leaving the hospital" — being discharged after recovering from illness or surgery. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 退 (たい) = to withdraw/retreat/leave, and 院 (いん) = institution/building (especially medical or academic). Together they describe withdrawing from the hospital institution. The sentence says: "I heard that Kawai-san will leave the hospital 退院 (たいいん) tomorrow." 退院する is the standard verb for hospital discharge. The reading challenge: 退 reads たい (unvoiced, long vowel たい = two morae), not voiced だい or shortened た. The four options test: たいいん (correct) vs たんいん, だいいん, and だんいん — all variations of voiced/unvoiced (た vs だ) and long/short vowel (たい vs たん). 退 always reads たい (long vowel, unvoiced). 院 reads いん in all four options correctly. 退 also appears in 退職 (たいしょく, retirement), 退場 (たいじょう, exit/removal from venue), and 引退 (いんたい, retirement from public life).
✗ たんいん changes たい to たん. 退 reads たい (long vowel た + い), not たん (た + ん). たん would suggest a nasal ending, but 退 has the vowel い, not the nasal ん.
✗ だいいん voices 退 to だい. The on-yomi of 退 is たい (unvoiced). Voicing it to だい is wrong. だいいん (大院) might suggest a large institution, but that is a different word.
✗ だんいん combines both errors: voices 退 to だ and shortens to だん. The on-yomi of 退 is たい — unvoiced and with a long い vowel. だんいん does not correspond to any standard compound.
例: 手術 (しゅじゅつ) から一週間 (いっしゅうかん) で退院 (たいいん) できた。 — I was able to leave the hospital one week after the surgery.

question: パーテイーには ＿夫婦＿ で参加します。
explanation:
夫婦 is read ふうふ — 夫 reads ふう and 婦 reads ふ, meaning "husband and wife / married couple".
夫婦 (ふうふ) = a married couple — husband and wife together. 夫 (ふう) = husband, 婦 (ふ) = wife/woman. The sentence says 「パーティーには夫婦 (ふうふ) で参加 (さんか) します」 — "We will attend the party as a couple." The reading trap: 夫 in this compound reads ふう (long vowel, two morae), not just ふ. 婦 reads ふ (one mora, short). ふうふ = ふう + ふ. Related: 夫婦仲 (ふうふなか, marital relationship), 老夫婦 (ろうふうふ, elderly couple).
✗ ふうふう elongates both kanji to two morae each (ふう + ふう). 婦 reads ふ (one mora), not ふう. ふうふう is an onomatopoeia for panting/blowing and is not how 夫婦 is read.
✗ ふふう shortens 夫 to ふ (one mora, wrong) and elongates 婦 to ふう (two morae, also wrong). The correct reading is ふうふ — long ふう for 夫, short ふ for 婦.
✗ ふふ shortens both kanji to one mora each. 夫 reads ふう (two morae), not ふ. ふふ is completely wrong for 夫婦.
例: 夫婦 (ふうふ) で旅行 (りょこう) に行くのが毎年 (まいとし) の楽 (たの) しみだ。 — Traveling together as a couple is our annual pleasure.

question: ＿留守＿ の間に誰か来たようだ。
explanation:
留守 is read るす — an irregular compound meaning "being away from home".
留守 (るす) = being away / no one is in. Irregular reading: 留 (る, shortened) + 守 (す, simplified). 「留守 (るす) の間 (あいだ) に誰 (だれ) か来 (き) たようだ」 — "It seems someone came while I was away." Must be memorized as a fixed unit.
✗ るしゅ: applies on-yomi しゅ to 守. 留守 is the fixed reading るす.
✗ りゅうす: on-yomi りゅう for 留 (as in 留学). In 留守, the reading shortens to る.
✗ りゅうしゅ: on-yomi りゅう + しゅ. 留守 is fixed: るす.
例: 留守 (るす) の間 (あいだ) に電話 (でんわ) があったようです。 — It seems there was a phone call while I was away.

question: これは、とても ＿高価＿ な花瓶だそうです。
explanation:
高価 is read こうか because 高 takes on-yomi こう and 価 takes on-yomi か, forming the compound meaning "high-priced / expensive."
高価 (こうか) is a na-adjective meaning "high-priced" or "expensive" — more formal and literary than 高い (たかい). The compound uses the on-yomi of both kanji: 高 (こう) = high/tall, and 価 (か) = price/value. Together 高価 (こうか) means something with a high price or value. The sentence says: "This flower vase is apparently a very high-priced 高価 (こうか) piece." The key reading challenge involves voiced vs unvoiced pairs: こうか (unvoiced か) vs ごうか (voiced initial ご) and こうが (voiced final が) vs ごうが. The correct answer is fully unvoiced: こう + か = こうか. The on-yomi of 高 is こう (not voiced ごう), and the on-yomi of 価 is か (not voiced が). The four options systematically vary these two voicing positions, making this a precision phonology question. 高 as on-yomi こう appears in 高速 (こうそく, high speed), 高校 (こうこう, high school), and 高価 (こうか). 価 as on-yomi か appears in 定価 (ていか, fixed price) and 物価 (ぶっか, price of goods).
✗ ごうか voices the first syllable, giving 高 the reading ごう. The on-yomi of 高 is こう (unvoiced), not ごう. ごうか is also homophonous with 豪華 (ごうか, luxurious/magnificent), a different word — one that exists but uses completely different kanji.
✗ こうが voices the second syllable, giving 価 the reading が. The on-yomi of 価 is か (unvoiced), not voiced が. こうが does not correspond to any standard compound.
✗ ごうが voices both syllables. Neither 高 (こう) nor 価 (か) takes a voiced reading in this compound. ごうが does not correspond to any real word.
例: このアクセサリーは見た目 (みため) はシンプルだが、高価 (こうか) な素材 (そざい) を使 (つか) っている。 — This accessory looks simple but uses expensive materials.

question: すみません、 ＿汚し＿ てしまいました。
explanation:
汚し is read よごして, meaning "dirtied / soiled" — the speaker is apologizing for making a mess.
汚す (よごす) means "to soil," "to dirty," or "to stain." Its te-form 汚して (よごして) is used in the progressive or apologetic construction. The sentence says: "I'm sorry, I have dirtied 汚して (よごして) it." すみません、汚してしまいました = "I'm sorry, I ended up dirtying it" — a typical apology when you accidentally soiled something. The kanji 汚 uses the kun-yomi よご in the transitive verb form: 汚す (よごす, to dirty something) and 汚れる (よごれる, to get dirty). Its on-yomi お appears in 汚染 (おせん, pollution/contamination) and 汚職 (おしょく, corruption). The four distractors are all te-form verbs describing damage or alteration: こわして (壊す, to break), おこして (起こす, to wake up/cause), and のこして (残す, to leave behind). All could follow すみません with different meanings, but only よごして fits the meaning of dirtying.
✗ こわして is the te-form of 壊す (こわす), meaning "to break" or "to destroy." Breaking something and dirtying something are different types of damage. 汚 does not read こわして.
✗ おこして is the te-form of 起こす (おこす), meaning "to wake someone up," "to cause (an incident)," or "to stand upright." Causing something or waking someone up is different from dirtying. 汚 does not read おこして.
✗ のこして is the te-form of 残す (のこす), meaning "to leave behind" or "to leave remaining." Leaving something and dirtying something are different actions. 汚 does not read のこして.
例: 食事 (しょくじ) 中 (ちゅう) に服 (ふく) を汚 (よご) してしまい、とても困 (こま) った。 — I accidentally dirtied my clothes during the meal and was quite flustered.

question: 体育館に ＿選手＿ が入ってきました。
explanation:
選手 is read せんしゅ and means "athlete / player".
選手 (せんしゅ) is an on-yomi compound: 選 (セン, select/choose) + 手 (シュ, hand — extended to mean a specialist or player). Together the word means "a chosen player" — an athlete or competitor who is selected to represent a team. The sentence 「体育館に選手が入ってきました」 means "The players entered the gymnasium." The reading challenge is シュ for 手 — in most everyday contexts 手 reads て (hand), but in compounds it uses the on-yomi シュ: 選手 (せんしゅ), 歌手 (かしゅ, singer), 投手 (とうしゅ, pitcher). Distractors mix in 週 (シュウ, week) to produce せんしゅう — a common phonological trap at N3.
✗ ぜんしゅ voices the first kanji — 選 reads セン (unvoiced), not ゼン (voiced). ゼン belongs to 全 (ぜん, all/complete), not 選 (せん, select).
✗ せんしゅう applies the on-yomi シュウ (week) to 手, lengthening it. But 手 reads シュ (short), not シュウ (long). The correct reading is せんしゅ, not せんしゅう.
✗ ぜんしゅう combines both errors: voiced ゼン for 選 and long シュウ for 手. ぜんしゅう could suggest 全集 (ぜんしゅう, complete works) — a real word, but not the reading of 選手.
例: この大会 (たいかい) には、世界中 (せかいじゅう) から400人 (よんひゃくにん) 以上 (いじょう) の選手 (せんしゅ) が参加 (さんか) している。 — More than 400 athletes from around the world are participating in this tournament.

question: 次は ＿月末＿ に来てください。
explanation:
月末 is read げつまつ because 月 takes on-yomi げつ and 末 takes on-yomi まつ, forming the compound meaning "end of the month."
月末 (げつまつ) means "the end of the month" — the last few days of a calendar month. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 月 (げつ) = month, and 末 (まつ) = end/tip. The sentence says: "Please come next time at the end of the month 月末 (げつまつ)." 月末 is commonly used in business and daily life for billing cycles, deadlines, and appointments: 月末払い (げつまつばらい, end-of-month payment). The reading of 月 varies significantly depending on context. Its on-yomi includes both がつ (used in month names: 一月 いちがつ January, 二月 にがつ February) and げつ (used in compounds like 月末 げつまつ, 月曜日 げつようび Monday). When combined with 末 (end), the compound always reads げつまつ, not がつまつ or がつまっ. 末 (まつ) also appears in 年末 (ねんまつ, year-end) and 週末 (しゅうまつ, weekend).
✗ げつもつ substitutes もつ for まつ as the reading of 末. 末 reads まつ in this compound. もつ is the on-yomi of 物 in 荷物 (にもつ) — a completely different kanji.
✗ がつまっ uses the month-name on-yomi がつ for 月 and contracts 末 to a sokuon まっ. 末 reads まつ (two morae), not a contracted まっ. Additionally, the compound 月末 uses げつ not がつ.
✗ がつもつ combines both errors: がつ for 月 and もつ for 末. 月 in 月末 reads げつ (not がつ), and 末 reads まつ (not もつ). Both halves are wrong.
例: 月末 (げつまつ) になると、いつも仕事 (しごと) が増 (ふ) える。 — Work always increases at the end of the month.

question: 箱の ＿裏＿ をよく見てください。
explanation:
裏 is read うら, meaning "the back side" — here the back of a box, where you often find ingredients or instructions.
裏 (うら) is a kun-yomi reading meaning "the back," "the reverse side," or "the inside of a surface." It contrasts with 表 (おもて), which means "the front" or "the outside." The sentence says: "Please look carefully at the back 裏 (うら) of the box." Checking the back of a box is exactly where you find important information — expiry dates, ingredients, instructions — so this context is completely natural. The kanji 裏 is used as a standalone noun (裏 = back side), making the kun-yomi うら the correct reading. The on-yomi り appears in formal compounds like 裏切り (うらぎり, betrayal, which mixes kun and on) and 表裏 (ひょうり, front and back). In everyday use, 裏 almost always reads うら. Distinguishing うら from the distractors requires recognizing that the other options (おく, ふた, よこ) are readings of entirely different kanji describing different spatial concepts.
✗ おく is the reading of 奥 (おく), meaning "the back/inside of a room or space" — the far end of an enclosed area, like the back of a closet. 奥 (おく) differs from 裏 (うら): 奥 refers to depth within a space, while 裏 refers to the reverse side of a flat surface.
✗ ふた is the reading of 蓋 (ふた), meaning "lid" or "cover." A lid is something placed on top to close, not the back side of a box.
✗ よこ is the reading of 横 (よこ), meaning "side" or "width." The side of a box and the back of a box are different surfaces. 横 (よこ) is not a reading of 裏.
例: この薬 (くすり) の説明 (せつめい) は箱 (はこ) の裏 (うら) に書 (か) いてある。 — The instructions for this medicine are written on the back of the box.

question: この町の ＿産業＿ について話を聞いた。
explanation:
産業 is read さんぎょう and means "industry" — the broad economic sector of a town.
産業 (さんぎょう) is an on-yomi compound: 産 (サン, produce/birth) + 業 (ギョウ, work/business). Together the word means "industry" — the economic activities that produce goods and services. The sentence 「この町の産業について話を聞いた」 means "I heard about the industries of this town." The reading サンギョウ uses the on-yomi of both: サン + ギョウ. Key confusion points: さんぎょう vs しょうぎょう (商業, commerce) vs ざんぎょう (残業, overtime). 産 (サン) relates to producing — 生産 (せいさん, production), 農産物 (のうさんぶつ, agricultural products). 業 (ギョウ) relates to the category of work.
✗ じょうぎょう does not correspond to a standard compound in this context. 常業 or similar are not common words meaning "the industries of a town".
✗ ざんぎょう (残業) means "overtime work" — staying late at the office. 残 (ザン, remaining) + 業 (ギョウ). This has nothing to do with a town's economic industries.
✗ しょうぎょう (商業) means "commerce / trade". 商 (ショウ, trade) + 業 (ギョウ). Commerce is a subset of industry, but 産業 is the broader term covering all economic sectors. The first kanji is different.
例: この地域 (ちいき) では観光 (かんこう) 産業 (さんぎょう) が盛 (さか) んで、多 (おお) くの旅行者 (りょこうしゃ) が訪 (おとず) れる。 — The tourism industry thrives in this region, attracting many visitors.

question: あしたの ＿朝刊＿ は休みです。
explanation:
朝刊 is read ちょうかん because 朝 takes on-yomi ちょう and 刊 takes on-yomi かん, forming the compound for "morning newspaper."
朝刊 (ちょうかん) means "morning newspaper" — an edition of a newspaper published in the morning. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 朝 (ちょう) = morning, and 刊 (かん) = publication/edition. The sentence says: "Tomorrow's morning newspaper 朝刊 (ちょうかん) will not be published." The key reading challenge: 朝 has both on-yomi ちょう and kun-yomi あさ. In this compound with another on-yomi kanji 刊 (かん), 朝 takes its on-yomi ちょう. Compare: 朝食 (ちょうしょく, breakfast — both on-yomi), but あさごはん (morning rice — both kun-yomi in a different expression). The long vowel ちょう (three morae: ち + ょ + う) must be preserved. The distractor ちょうがん misvoices 刊 (かん) to がん. 刊 reads かん (unvoiced) in all standard compounds: 週刊 (しゅうかん), 月刊 (げっかん), 朝刊 (ちょうかん). 夕刊 (ゆうかん) is the evening newspaper edition — the evening counterpart to 朝刊.
✗ ちょうがん voices the second syllable, giving 刊 the reading がん. 刊 reads kaん (unvoiced) in all compounds — there is no voiced variant がん. ちょうがん does not correspond to any real word.
✗ ちゅうかん uses ちゅう instead of ちょう for 朝. ちゅう could be the reading of 中 (middle) — as in 中間 (ちゅうかん, midpoint/interval). 朝 does not read ちゅう. The on-yomi of 朝 is ちょう, not ちゅう.
✗ ちゅうぶん assigns ちゅう to 朝 (wrong, as above) and ぶん to 刊. 刊 reads かん, not ぶん. ちゅうぶん corresponds to 中文 or 中分, neither of which relates to morning newspapers.
例: 毎朝 (まいあさ) コーヒーを飲 (の) みながら朝刊 (ちょうかん) を読 (よ) む。 — Every morning I read the morning newspaper while drinking coffee.

question: その話を聞いて、 中村さんは ＿断った＿ そうです。
explanation:
断った is read ことわった, meaning "refused / declined" — Nakamura-san turned down the offer after hearing the story.
断る (ことわる) means "to refuse," "to decline," or "to turn down." Its past tense 断った (ことわった) means "refused" or "said no." The sentence says: "After hearing that story, Nakamura-san apparently refused 断った (ことわった)." その話を聞いて断った = "after hearing the story, declined" — a natural sequence: hearing → deciding to refuse. The kanji 断 uses the kun-yomi ことわ in this verb form. Its on-yomi だん appears in 断言 (だんげん, to declare firmly), 断定 (だんてい, conclusion/determination), and 拒断 (not standard but related forms). The compound 断絶 (だんぜつ, severance) and 決断 (けつだん, decision) also use the on-yomi. The distractors are all past-tense verb forms ending in -った that express reactions to hearing something: こわがった (was afraid), あやまった (apologized), and うたがった (suspected).
✗ こわがった is the past tense of 怖がる (こわがる), meaning "to be afraid." Being afraid after hearing a story is plausible but different from refusing. 断 does not read こわがった.
✗ あやまった is the past tense of 謝る (あやまる), meaning "to apologize." Apologizing and refusing are both possible responses to hearing something, but they are different actions. 断 does not read あやまった.
✗ うたがった is the past tense of 疑う (うたがう), meaning "to suspect" or "to doubt." Suspecting and refusing are different mental states and actions. 断 does not read うたがった.
例: お世話 (おせわ) になった方 (かた) からの頼 (たの) みを断 (ことわ) るのは難 (むずか) しかった。 — It was difficult to turn down a request from someone who had helped me.

question: あしたは、2時に ＿広場＿ に集まってください。
explanation:
広場 is read ひろば because 広 takes kun-yomi ひろ and 場 takes kun-yomi ば, together meaning "a public open space" or "plaza."
広場 (ひろば) means "plaza," "open space," or "square" — a large open area where people gather. The compound uses the kun-yomi of both kanji: 広 (ひろ) = wide/broad, and 場 (ば) = place/space. Together they describe "a wide place" — an open public area. The sentence says: "Please gather at the plaza 広場 (ひろば) at 2 o'clock tomorrow." This is a typical meeting-spot instruction. The reading challenge is distinguishing kun-yomi ひろ + ば from the on-yomi alternatives. 広 has on-yomi こう (as in 広告 こうこく, advertisement) and kun-yomi ひろ(い) (wide). 場 has on-yomi じょう (as in 工場 こうじょう, factory; 会場 かいじょう, venue) and kun-yomi ば (as in 場所 ばしょ, place; 広場 ひろば). In 広場, both kanji use their kun-yomi — ひろ + ば = ひろば. The distractors test both the voiced/unvoiced (こうば vs こうじょう) and the on/kun split.
✗ ひろじょう uses the kun-yomi ひろ for 広 correctly but switches 場 to the on-yomi じょう. When both 広 and 場 use kun-yomi, the compound reads ひろば — not the on-yomi mix ひろじょう. ひろじょう is not a standard reading of 広場.
✗ こうば switches 広 to the on-yomi こう and uses the kun-yomi ば for 場. This mixed on-kun reading produces こうば — which is actually the reading of 工場 (こうば) in some dialects, but not of 広場. The standard compound 広場 always reads ひろば.
✗ こうじょう uses the on-yomi of both kanji: こう (広) + じょう (場). こうじょう is the reading of 工場 (こうじょう, factory) or 広場 written with on-yomi — but neither is correct for 広場. The standard reading is the kun-yomi pair ひろ + ば = ひろば.
例: 祭り (まつり) の日 (ひ) は広場 (ひろば) に多 (おお) くの人 (ひと) が集 (あつ) まった。 — On the day of the festival, many people gathered at the plaza.

question: 機械が ＿せいじょう＿ かどうかチェックした。
explanation:
せいじょう is written 正常 because 正 means "correct/proper" and 常 means "normal/usual," together meaning "normal" or "functioning properly."
正常 (せいじょう) is a na-adjective meaning "normal," "proper," or "functioning correctly." Both kanji take their on-yomi: 正 (せい) = correct/proper, and 常 (じょう) = normal/always/constant. Together they describe the normal, correct state of affairs. The sentence says: "I checked whether the machine 機械 (きかい) is functioning normally 正常 (せいじょう)." 正常かどうかチェックした = "checked whether it is normal." The word 正常 is commonly used in technical and medical contexts to describe systems operating within expected parameters. The four options test confusions between 正 (せい, correct) and 盛 (せい/さかん, prosperous/in full bloom) and 威 (い/おど, authority/intimidate), as well as between 常 (じょう, normal/usual) and 情 (じょう/なさけ, feelings/emotion). 正 (correct) + 常 (usual) = 正常. The alternatives swap kanji meaning correctness for ones meaning prosperity, authority, or emotion — none of which conveys "normal operation."
✗ 盛情 uses 盛 (せい/さかん, prosperous/flourishing) and 情 (じょう, feelings). Neither matches the meaning of normal operation. 盛 is used in 盛ん (さかん, thriving) and 繁盛 (はんじょう, prosperity). 盛情 is not a standard compound.
✗ 威常 uses 威 (い, authority/power/intimidation — 威力 いりょく, power; 威圧 いあつ, intimidation) instead of 正. Authority and correctness are different concepts. 威常 is not a real compound.
✗ 正情 uses the correct 正 (せい) but replaces 常 with 情 (じょう, emotion/feelings). 情 is used in 感情 (かんじょう, emotion) and 情報 (じょうほう, information). Feelings and normal state are different. 正情 is not a real compound.
例: 検査 (けんさ) の結果 (けっか) は正常 (せいじょう) で、特 (とく) に問題 (もんだい) はなかった。 — The test results were normal, and there were no particular issues.

question: 健康診断で ＿けつえき＿ 検査を受けた。
explanation:
けつえき is written 血液 because 血 means "blood" and 液 means "liquid," together meaning "blood" as a fluid in the medical sense.
血液 (けつえき) means "blood" in a formal or medical context — the liquid that circulates through the body. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 血 (けつ) = blood, and 液 (えき) = liquid/fluid. Together they describe blood as a biological fluid. The sentence says: "I underwent a blood test 血液 (けつえき) at the health checkup." 健康診断で血液検査を受ける = "to undergo a blood test at a physical examination" is standard medical vocabulary. Note that 血液 (けつえき) is the Sino-Japanese formal term, while 血 (ち) is the more colloquial word for blood (as in 血が出た ちがでた, blood came out). The four distractors introduce 意識 (いしき, consciousness), 園圧 (not a real compound), 血圧 (けつあつ, blood pressure), and 血液 (correct). 血圧 (けつあつ) and 血液 (けつえき) are both medical terms starting with 血 (けつ), making this a careful discrimination between second kanji: 圧 (あつ, pressure) vs 液 (えき, liquid). A blood pressure test and a blood test are different medical procedures.
✗ 意識 (いしき) means "consciousness" or "awareness" — a concept related to the mind, not blood. A consciousness test (意識検査) would check mental awareness. 意 (い, intention/mind) and 識 (しき, knowledge/recognize) have no connection to blood.
✗ 園圧 uses 園 (えん, garden/park — 公園 こうえん) and 圧 (あつ, pressure). 園圧 is not a real compound. 園 does not mean blood, and this combination has no medical meaning.
✗ 血圧 (けつあつ) means "blood pressure" — a real and important medical term. It uses 圧 (あつ, pressure) instead of 液 (えき, liquid). Blood pressure and a blood test are different examinations. The sentence says 血液検査 (blood test), not 血圧 (blood pressure).
例: 毎年 (まいとし) の健康診断 (けんこうしんだん) で血液 (けつえき) 検査 (けんさ) を受 (う) けて、コレステロール値 (ち) を確認 (かくにん) している。 — Every year I get a blood test at my health checkup to check my cholesterol levels.

question: 母親が子どもの後ろを ＿おって＿ 走っている。
explanation:
おって is written 追って because 追 means "to chase / to follow behind," which describes a mother running after her child.
追う (おう) means "to chase," "to follow," or "to pursue." Its te-form 追って (おって) describes the action in progress. The sentence says: "The mother is running 追って (おって) behind her child." The image is clear: the child is ahead, and the mother is running to follow or keep up. The kanji 追 uses the kun-yomi お in verb form. Its on-yomi つい appears in compounds like 追加 (ついか, addition), 追跡 (ついせき, pursuit/tracking), and 追放 (ついほう, exile). The distractors 送 (おくる, to send), 押 (おす, to push), and 折 (おる, to break/fold) all share the お- sound at the start of their kun-yomi, making this a careful discrimination between verbs that begin with お. Running behind someone specifically is the action of chasing/following — 追う (おう) — not sending, pushing, or breaking.
✗ 送って is the te-form of 送る (おくる), meaning "to send" or "to see someone off." Sending something and chasing after someone are different. 送 does not read おって (the correct conjugation is おくって).
✗ 押って is not the standard form of 押す (おす, to push). The te-form of 押す is 押して (おして), not 押って. Even setting that aside, pushing and chasing are different actions.
✗ 折って is the te-form of 折る (おる), meaning "to break" or "to fold." A mother running to follow her child is not folding or breaking anything. 折る has nothing to do with chasing.
例: 犯人 (はんにん) を追 (お) って警察 (けいさつ) が走 (はし) り出 (だ) した。 — The police rushed out in pursuit of the suspect.

question: 電車を ＿おりる＿ ときに、 かさを忘れてしまった。
explanation:
おりる is written 降りる because 降りる means "to get off / to descend", fitting someone getting off a train.
降りる (おりる) = to get off (a vehicle) or to descend. The sentence says 「電車 (でんしゃ) を降 (お) りるときに、かさを忘 (わす) れてしまった」 — "When I got off the train, I forgot my umbrella." 降りる is an ichidan verb (る-verb). Its reading おり comes from the kun-yomi of 降. 降る (ふる) means rain or snow falls — different reading, same kanji, different meaning. Context clarifies which reading applies.
✗ 移りる: 移 (い/うつ-る, to move/transfer) does not form おりる. 移る (うつる) = to move/transfer to a new place — a different action. 移りる is not a real word form (移る conjugates as うつる, not うつりる).
✗ 移る: correct kanji for 移 but the plain form うつる does not read おりる. 移る = to move/transfer; 降りる = to get off. Different meanings and different kanji.
✗ 降る: this is a real word — 降る (ふる) = rain or snow falls. But 降る reads ふる, not おりる. 降りる and 降る are different conjugations of 降 with different meanings and readings.
例: バスを降 (お) りてすぐ、財布 (さいふ) を忘 (わす) れたことに気 (き) づいた。 — Just after getting off the bus, I realized I had forgotten my wallet.

question: 大学に入ってから、 ＿しんちょう＿ が変わっていない。
explanation:
しんちょう is written 身長 because 身 means "body" and 長 means "length," together forming the word for "height" (one's body length).
身長 (しんちょう) means "height" — one's physical stature, measured from head to feet. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 身 (しん) = body/oneself, and 長 (ちょう) = long/length/chief. Together they describe the "length of the body" — one's height. The sentence says: "My height 身長 (しんちょう) has not changed since entering university." 身長が変わっていない is a natural expression for not having grown taller (or shorter) since a certain time. The key distinctions are 身 (しん, body) vs 背 (はい/せ, back/stature) for the first kanji, and 長 (ちょう, long) vs 張 (ちょう/は, to stretch/spread) for the second. 背中 (せなか) means the physical back of the body; 背後 (はいご) means behind someone. Neither 背中 nor 背後 means height. 身長 specifically measures the length (長) of the body (身). 体重 (たいじゅう, body weight) is the parallel compound measuring body weight.
✗ 背中 (せなか) means "the back" — the rear side of the torso. Height (how tall someone is) and the back of the body are completely different measurements. 背 does not read しん.
✗ 背後 (はいご) means "behind" someone — being at their back in a spatial sense. 背 (はい/せ) refers to the back, not body length. 身長 (しんちょう) is the specific compound for height.
✗ 身張 uses 身 (body) correctly for the first kanji but replaces 長 with 張 (ちょう/は, to stretch or spread). 張る (はる) means to stretch or paste something. 身張 is not a real word and does not mean height.
例: 彼 (かれ) は身長 (しんちょう) が180センチあり、バスケットボールが得意 (とくい) だ。 — He is 180 centimeters tall and is good at basketball.

question: ＿ものがたり＿ は誰でも知っている。
explanation:
ものがたり is written 物語 — 物 means "thing" and 語 means "story / language", together meaning "a story / tale".
物語 (ものがたり) = a story, tale, or narrative. 物 (もの) = thing/matter, 語 (がたり) = story/telling (voiced from かたり by rendaku). Together: a telling of things/events — a story. The sentence says 「その物語 (ものがたり) は誰 (だれ) でも知 (し) っている」 — "Everyone knows that story." 物語 covers fairy tales, novels, historical narratives, and legends. Note the rendaku: 語 (かたり) voices to がたり in this compound.
✗ 物化: 化 (か, transformation/化学=chemistry) instead of 語 (かたり/がたり, story). 物化 is not a standard compound meaning "story". 化 relates to change or chemistry.
✗ 物記: 記 (き, to record/diary) instead of 語 (story). 物記 is not a standard compound. Records and stories are different — 日記 (にっき, diary) uses 記, not 物語.
✗ 物源: 源 (みなもと/げん, source/origin) instead of 語 (story). 物源 is not a real word. The source of something and a story are different concepts.
例: その物語 (ものがたり) は子 (こ) どもから大人 (おとな) まで愛 (あい) されている。 — That story is loved by everyone from children to adults.

question: みんなで話し合って、問題を ＿かいけつ＿ した。
explanation:
かいけつ is written 解決 — 解 means "to untangle/solve" and 決 means "to decide/resolve".
解決 (かいけつ) = to resolve/solve a problem. 解 (かい) = to untangle/dissolve (理解, りかい), 決 (けつ) = to decide/resolve (決める, きめる). 「みんなで話 (はな) し合 (あ) って、問題 (もんだい) を解決 (かいけつ) した」 — "We discussed and resolved the problem."
✗ 改決: 改 (かい, to reform) instead of 解 (かい, to untangle). Both read かい but different meanings. 改決 is not a real word.
✗ 改結: 改 (reform) and 結 (けつ, to bind). Binding is opposite of resolving. Not a real word.
✗ 解結: correct 解 but wrong 結 (to bind) instead of 決 (to decide). 解結 is not a real word.
例: 話 (はな) し合 (あ) いで問題 (もんだい) が解決 (かいけつ) した。 — The problem was resolved through discussion.

question: 山口(やまぐち)さんに束京(とうきょう)を ＿あんない＿ してもらった。
explanation:
あんない is written 案内 — the kanji 案 (plan/proposal) plus 内 (inside/guide).
案内 (あんない) means "to guide" or "to show around". The kanji 案 (アン) carries the idea of a plan or a proposal; 内 (ナイ) means "inside" or "within". Together they form a word for showing someone the way through an unfamiliar space, literally "a guide from the inside". The sentence says Yamaguchi-san guided the speaker around Tokyo (東京, とうきょう). The verb form is 案内する (あんないする), so あんないしてもらった means "had (someone) guide me around". Among the four options, only 案内 uses the correct kanji for both sounds: ア for 案 and ナイ for 内. The other three options mix in wrong characters.
✗ 安内 uses 安 (アン, peaceful/cheap) instead of 案 (アン, plan/guide). The sound is the same — アン — but 安 never carries the meaning of guiding or showing around.
✗ 家内 reads かない, not あんない. 家内 (かない) is an old-fashioned word for "one's wife". The reading of 家 here is か, not あん.
✗ 室内 reads しつない, meaning "indoors" or "interior of a room". It is a real compound word, but its reading is completely different from あんない, and its meaning has nothing to do with guiding someone.
例: 受付 (うけつけ) の人 (ひと) が会議室 (かいぎしつ) まで案内 (あんない) してくれた。 — The receptionist guided us to the conference room.

question: わたしは ＿けんこう＿ のために毎日走っています。
explanation:
けんこう is written 健康 — 健 (healthy/strong) + 康 (health/peaceful), meaning "health".
健康 (けんこう) means "health" or "being healthy". Both kanji use on-yomi: 健 (ケン, healthy/strong) + 康 (コウ, peaceful/healthy). Together the word refers to the state of being physically and mentally well. The sentence 「わたしはけんこうのために毎日走っています」 means "I run every day for my health." Among the four options, the trap is 建康 — using 建 (ケン, build/construct) instead of 健 (ケン, healthy). Both 建 and 健 share the on-yomi ケン, and they look visually similar (the difference is a single component: 人 vs nothing on the left side). 庫 (こ, storehouse) is also substituted for 康 in another option, but コウ vs コ is a vowel-length difference.
✗ 建康 uses 建 (ケン, to build/construct) instead of 健 (ケン, healthy). 建 appears in 建物 (たてもの, building) and 建設 (けんせつ, construction). Both 建 and 健 read ケン, but the meaning is completely different.
✗ 健庫 uses 庫 (コ, storehouse) instead of 康 (コウ, health/peaceful). 庫 reads コ (short), not コウ (long). 車庫 (しゃこ, garage) uses 庫 with the short コ reading. Shortening コウ to コ produces a wrong character.
✗ 建庫 gets both kanji wrong — 建 instead of 健 and 庫 instead of 康. This option combines both substitution errors at once.
例: 健康 (けんこう) を維持 (いじ) するためには、規則正 (きそくただ) しい生活 (せいかつ) と適度 (てきど) な運動 (うんどう) が大切 (たいせつ) です。 — To maintain health, a regular lifestyle and moderate exercise are important.

question: 今年の夏は ＿きおん＿ が高かった。
explanation:
きおん is written 気温 — 気 means "air / atmosphere" and 温 means "warmth / temperature".
気温 (きおん) = air temperature. 気 (き) = air/atmosphere, 温 (おん) = warmth. 「今年 (ことし) の夏 (なつ) は気温 (きおん) が高 (たか) かった」 — "The temperature this summer was high." Standard meteorological term; 最高気温 (さいこうきおん, maximum temperature).
✗ 気湿: 湿 (しつ, humidity/damp) ≠ 温 (warmth). 湿度 (しつど, humidity) is a related weather term but 気湿 is not a real word.
✗ 気湯: 湯 (ゆ/とう, hot water) ≠ 温 (warmth). 気湯 is not a real word.
✗ 気混: 混 (こん, to mix) ≠ 温 (warmth). 気混 is not a real word.
例: 今日 (きょう) の最高気温 (さいこうきおん) は35度 (ど) に達 (たっ) した。 — Today's maximum temperature reached 35 degrees.

question: 頭が ＿いたい＿ ので、薬を飲んだ。
explanation:
いたい is written 痛い because 痛 means "painful / hurting," which describes a headache.
痛い (いたい) is an i-adjective meaning "painful" or "it hurts." The kanji 痛 uses the kun-yomi いた in adjective form. The sentence says: "Because my head 頭 (あたま) hurts 痛い (いたい), I took medicine." 頭が痛い (あたまがいたい) = "my head hurts" is one of the most common expressions used when describing illness or discomfort in Japanese. The on-yomi of 痛 is つう, appearing in 苦痛 (くつう, suffering/pain), 激痛 (げきつう, severe pain), and 鎮痛剤 (ちんつうざい, painkiller). The radical of 痛 is 疒 (illness/sickness radical), consistently used in health-related kanji: 病 (びょう, sick), 痛 (つう, pain), 疲 (ひ, tired), 癒 (ゆ, to heal). The four distractors — 病 (sick), 痛 (correct), 疫 (epidemic/plague), and 症 (symptom/condition) — all use the 疒 radical, making this a kanji meaning discrimination question within the illness category.
✗ 病い uses 病 (びょう/やまい), meaning "sick" or "disease." 頭が病い does not work naturally in Japanese. The correct word for a physical sensation of pain is 痛い (いたい), not 病い. 病 does not read いたい.
✗ 疫い uses 疫 (えき/やく), meaning "epidemic" or "plague." 疫 is used in 防疫 (ぼうえき, epidemic prevention) and 免疫 (めんえき, immunity). It does not mean individual pain and does not read いたい.
✗ 症い uses 症 (しょう), meaning "symptom" or "condition" as in 症状 (しょうじょう, symptoms) and 後遺症 (こういしょう, aftereffects). 症 is a medical term for conditions, not for the subjective feeling of pain. It does not read いたい.
例: 歯 (は) が痛 (いた) くて夜 (よる) も眠 (ねむ) れなかった。 — My tooth hurt so much I couldn't sleep at night.

question: このシャツは工場で ＿たいりょう＿ に作られている。
explanation:
たいりょう is written 大量 — 大 (large) + 量 (quantity/amount).
大量 (たいりょう) means "a large amount" or "in bulk". Both kanji use on-yomi: 大 (タイ, large) + 量 (リョウ, quantity). The sentence 「このシャツは工場でたいりょうに作られている」 means "These shirts are manufactured in large quantities at a factory." The key distinction is between 大 (タイ, large) and 多 (タ/おお, many/numerous). While both relate to size or quantity, 大量 (たいりょう) specifically means a large volume, while 多量 (たりょう) emphasizes "many units / an excessive amount" and is less common in manufacturing contexts. The radical 量 contains 里 at the bottom, suggesting measurement.
✗ 多量 reads たりょう, not たいりょう. 多 (タ/おお) means "numerous" and its on-yomi is タ, not タイ. The sound たい- corresponds to 大 (タイ), not 多 (タ).
✗ 多料 uses both the wrong first kanji (多 instead of 大) and the wrong second kanji (料 instead of 量). 料 (リョウ) means "fee / material", as in 料金 (りょうきん, fee). It does not mean "quantity".
✗ 大料 uses the correct first kanji (大) but the wrong second kanji (料). 料 means "fee or ingredient", not "quantity". The correct kanji for "amount" is 量.
例: 工場 (こうじょう) では毎日 (まいにち) 大量 (たいりょう) の製品 (せいひん) が作 (つく) られている。 — Large quantities of products are manufactured at the factory every day.

question: 9 東京は ＿げんざい＿ 午後３時です。
explanation:
げんざい is written 現在 because 現 means "present/current" and 在 means "to exist/to be present," together meaning "right now / the present time."
現在 (げんざい) means "the present time" or "currently" — it is used to indicate the current moment or current state of affairs. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 現 (げん) = present/actual/to appear, and 在 (ざい) = to exist/to be located. Together they mean "existing in the present moment." The sentence says: "It is currently 現在 (げんざい) 3:00 PM in Tokyo." This is a typical announcement or news broadcast phrasing. The key distinctions are 現 (げん, present/actual) vs 視 (し, to look/observe) for the first kanji, and 在 (ざい, to exist) vs 存 (そん/ぞん, to exist/preserve) for the second. 現 appears in 現在 (げんざい), 現実 (げんじつ, reality), and 現代 (げんだい, modern times). 在 appears in 現在 (げんざい), 存在 (そんざい, existence), and 在宅 (ざいたく, being home). 視 appears in 視力 (しりょく, eyesight) and 視野 (しや, field of vision). 存 appears in 存在 (そんざい) and 生存 (せいぞん, survival).
✗ 視在 uses 視 (し, to look/observe) instead of 現 (げん, present/actual). 視 is used in sight-related words like 視力 (しりょく, eyesight). It does not mean "current" or "present time" and does not read げん.
✗ 現存 has the correct first kanji 現 (げん) but uses 存 (そん/ぞん) instead of 在 (ざい). 現存 (げんそん) is actually a real word meaning "still in existence" (as in a historical artifact that still exists today), but it means existential persistence, not "the current time/currently."
✗ 視存 combines 視 (look/observe) and 存 (exist/preserve) — both wrong kanji. 視存 is not a real word. Neither character matches the meaning or reading of 現在.
例: 現在 (げんざい) の状況 (じょうきょう) を報告 (ほうこく) します。 — I will report on the current situation.

question: 10 こちらのサンプルは ＿ごじゆう＿ にお取りください。
explanation:
ごじゆう is written ご自由 because 自 means "oneself/free" and 由 means "reason/basis," forming 自由 (freedom), with the honorific prefix ご.
自由 (じゆう) means "freedom" or "as you please." In the phrase ご自由にお取りください (ごじゆうにおとりください), it means "please take freely" or "help yourself." The word 自由 uses the on-yomi of both kanji: 自 (じ) = self, own, and 由 (ゆう) = reason, origin, or basis. Together they convey the idea of "acting on one's own accord" — freedom. The honorific prefix ご is added to make the phrase polite, as in ご自由に (ごじゆうに, please feel free to). The two kanji that learners must distinguish are 自 (self) vs 事 (matter/thing) for the first position, and 由 (reason/origin) vs 有 (to have/exist) for the second. 自有 and ご事由 are not standard compounds. 事由 (じゆう) is an actual legal/formal word meaning "reason" or "grounds," written with 事 (matter) + 由 (reason), but the underlined kana ごじゆう in the context of "take freely" calls for 自由 (freedom), not 事由 (formal reason).
✗ ご事有 uses 事 (matter/thing) for the first kanji and 有 (to have/exist) for the second. 事有 is not a real compound. 有 means "to have" or "existence" (有名 ゆうめい, famous) and does not combine with 事 to mean freedom.
✗ ご事由 uses 事 (matter/thing) instead of 自 (self). 事由 (じゆう) is a legal term meaning "grounds" or "reason," not "freedom." The context — helping yourself to samples — requires 自由 (freedom to act), not 事由 (formal reason).
✗ ご自有 uses 自 correctly for the first kanji but swaps 由 for 有 (to have/exist). 自有 is not a standard word. 由 (ゆう) means reason or origin and is the second kanji in 自由; replacing it with 有 breaks the compound.
例: このカフェでは、コーヒーのおかわりが自由 (じゆう) です。 — At this cafe, coffee refills are free (unlimited).

question: 11 大学では ＿ほうりつ＿ を勉強ました。
explanation:
ほうりつ is written 法律 — 法 (law/method) + 律 (rule/regulation).
法律 (ほうりつ) means "law" in the legal sense — the body of rules governing society. Both kanji use on-yomi: 法 (ホウ, law/method) + 律 (リツ, rule/rhythm). Together they refer to enacted law (statutes). The sentence 「大学では法律を勉強しました」 means "I studied law at university." The trap is distinguishing 法 (ホウ) from 方 (ホウ), and 律 (リツ) from 立 (タツ). Both pairs share the same on-yomi (ホウ and リツ respectively), but the kanji are different. 法 contains the 氵 (water) radical — historically suggesting flowing from a source of justice. 律 contains a component suggesting measured order.
✗ 方立 uses 方 (ほう, direction/method) and 立 (たつ, stand up). 方 also reads ホウ, like 法, causing confusion. But 方立 is not a standard compound meaning law.
✗ 法立 uses the correct 法 (ほう) but replaces 律 with 立 (たつ/リツ). 立 reads リツ in some compounds (e.g., 独立 どくりつ), so the sound is superficially similar. However, 法律 requires 律 (rule), not 立 (stand).
✗ 方律 uses 方 instead of 法. While 方 and 法 both read ホウ, the legal meaning belongs to 法 (which has the 氵 radical). 方律 is not a standard compound.
例: その行為 (こうい) は法律 (ほうりつ) に違反 (いはん) しているので、許 (ゆる) されません。 — That action violates the law and is therefore not permitted.

question: 12 いつか京都をゆっくり ＿かんこう＿ したい。
explanation:
かんこう is written 観光 — 観 (view/observe) + 光 (light/scenery).
観光 (かんこう) means "sightseeing" or "tourism". Both kanji use on-yomi: 観 (カン, to view/observe) + 光 (コウ, light/radiance — here extended to mean the brilliant sights of a place). The sentence 「いつか京都をゆっくりかんこうしたい」 means "Someday I want to take my time sightseeing in Kyoto." The test distinguishes 観 from 歓 (also カン, but meaning "joy/welcome") and 光 from 察 (サツ, investigate). The 見 radical inside 観 signals vision/observation, whereas 歓 contains 欠 (mouth open in joy). Remembering that 観光 is about seeing (観) the scenery (光) helps lock in the correct kanji pair.
✗ 観察 reads かんさつ, not かんこう. 察 (サツ) means "to investigate / to sense", giving 観察 the meaning "observation" (careful watching). The second kanji is wrong.
✗ 歓光 uses 歓 (カン, joy/welcome) instead of 観 (カン, observe). 歓 appears in 歓迎 (かんげい, welcome) and 歓声 (かんせい, cheer). It does not mean watching/viewing scenery.
✗ 歓察 gets both kanji wrong — 歓 instead of 観, and 察 instead of 光. The sounds also fail to match: 歓察 would read かんさつ, not かんこう.
例: 観光 (かんこう) 客 (きゃく) が多 (おお) すぎて、有名 (ゆうめい) な神社 (じんじゃ) に入 (はい) れなかった。 — There were so many tourists that I could not get into the famous shrine.

question: 13 当日、この ＿けん＿ を忘れないようにしてください。
explanation:
けん (ticket/voucher) is written 券 — the speaker is told not to forget this ticket on the day.
券 (けん) means "a ticket" or "a voucher". The sentence 「当日、このけんを忘れないようにしてください」 means "Please make sure not to forget this ticket on the day of the event." The on-yomi ケン is the standard reading for 券 when it stands alone or at the end of a compound. It appears in: 入場券 (にゅうじょうけん, admission ticket), 乗車券 (じょうしゃけん, train ticket), 商品券 (しょうひんけん, gift voucher). Among the four options, the trap is distinguishing 券 (ticket) from 巻 (roll/volume), 募 (recruit), and 巷 (alleyway) — all of which have partially similar forms.
