✗ 'after' is the opposite direction. The word for 'after a point in time' is 以後 (いご) or 以降 (いこう). 以前 always refers to the earlier side of a boundary.
✗ 'during' is expressed by 〜の間 (あいだ/かん) or 〜中 (じゅう). 以前 does not describe an ongoing span of time; it points to an earlier period.
✗ 'between' is expressed by 〜の間 (あいだ) or 〜と〜の間に. 以前 does not mean 'between' — it marks a one-sided boundary in time (the earlier side).
例: 以前 (いぜん) はここに公園 (こうえん) があった。 — There used to be a park here before.

question: 「以後」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
以後 (いご) means 'after / from now on' — referring to a point in time onward from a stated reference.
以後 (いご) is a time expression meaning 'after (a stated point)' or 'from now on.' 以 (い) marks a boundary, and 後 (ご) means 'after / behind.' Together they describe everything on the later side of a time boundary: 今後 (こんご) 以後はそうしよう (let's do it that way from now on). 以後 can refer to a specific past or future boundary: 三月以後 (さんがついご) = from March onward. It is closely related to 以降 (いこう), which also means 'from ~ onward' and is slightly more formal. The pair 以前 (いぜん, before) ↔ 以後 (いご, after) is tested frequently at N3 because learners must distinguish the direction of the boundary. 以後 also appears in formal apologies: 以後気をつけます (I will be careful from now on).
✗ 'meanwhile' is expressed by その間 (あいだ/かん) or 一方で (いっぽうで). 以後 does not describe a simultaneous span; it marks a point and everything after it.
✗ 'before' is 以前 (いぜん). 以後 and 以前 are direct antonyms: 以後 = after, 以前 = before. The character difference is 後 (after) vs 前 (before).
✗ 'during' is expressed by 〜の間 (かん/あいだ) or 〜中 (じゅう). 以後 is a point-and-forward marker, not a duration marker.
例: その事件 (じけん) 以後 (いご)、彼 (かれ) の態度 (たいど) は大 (おお) きく変 (か) わった。 — After that incident, his attitude changed significantly.

question: 「単語」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
単語 is read たんご and means 'word' or 'vocabulary item.'
単語 (たんご) is the standard Japanese word for an individual vocabulary item — a single lexical unit that you look up in a dictionary. 単 (たん) has the on-yomi たん and means 'single' or 'simple'; it appears in 単純 (たんじゅん, simple) and 単独 (たんどく, alone). 語 (ご) has the on-yomi ご and means 'language' or 'word'; it appears in 日本語 (にほんご, Japanese), 英語 (えいご, English), and 外国語 (がいこくご, foreign language). Combining them: 単語 (たんご) = 'a single unit of language' = a word. Both kanji use their on-yomi, which is the typical pattern for two-character academic vocabulary.
✗ ひとご mixes the kun-yomi of 単 (ひと, 'one/alone') with a non-standard reading for 語. 語 does not normally produce ご after ひと in this compound.
✗ ひとこ treats 単 as ひと (plausible kun-yomi) and 語 as こ. こ is not a standard reading for 語 in any common word.
✗ たんこ gets the first kanji correct (たん) but reads 語 as こ instead of ご. The on-yomi of 語 is ご, not こ.
例: 毎日 (まいにち) 新 (あたら) しい単語 (たんご) を十個 (じゅっこ) 覚 (おぼ) えるようにしています。 — I try to memorize ten new words every day.

question: 「会員」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
会員 is read かいいん and means 'member' — a person who belongs to a group, club, or organization.
会員 (かいいん) means a member of a group, club, organization, or service. 会 (かい) has the on-yomi かい and means 'meeting,' 'association,' or 'club'; it appears in 会社 (かいしゃ, company), 学会 (がっかい, academic society), and 協会 (きょうかい, association). 員 (いん) has the on-yomi いん and means 'member' or 'personnel'; it appears in 社員 (しゃいん, company employee), 委員 (いいん, committee member), and 満員 (まんいん, fully occupied). Together: かいいん = 'member of an association' = member. Common uses: 会員登録 (かいいんとうろく, member registration), 会員証 (かいいんしょう, membership card), 会員限定 (かいいんげんてい, members-only).
✗ あいえん applies non-standard readings to both characters: あい for 会 (not a standard on-yomi of 会) and えん for 員 (not a reading of 員). This combination does not form a real word.
✗ かいえん gets the first character right (かい) but reads 員 as えん — not a standard reading of 員. The on-yomi of 員 is いん.
✗ あいいん applies the non-standard reading あい to 会 and the correct on-yomi いん to 員. The on-yomi of 会 is かい.
例: このジムは会員 (かいいん) になると、すべての施設 (しせつ) が使 (つか) えます。 — If you become a member of this gym, you can use all the facilities.

question: 「友人」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
友人 is read ゆうじん and means 'friend / close acquaintance.'
友人 (ゆうじん) is the on-yomi reading for this two-character compound meaning 'friend' or 'close acquaintance.' 友 (ゆう) means 'friend / companionship,' and 人 (じん) means 'person.' In formal and written Japanese, 友人 is preferred over the casual 友達 (ともだち). You see 友人 in formal introductions (友人のAさんです, 'This is my friend A'), in newspapers, and in polite letters. The on-yomi ゆう for 友 also appears in 友好 (ゆうこう, friendly relations) and 友情 (ゆうじょう, friendship as a feeling). The on-yomi じん for 人 is very common in compounds: 外国人 (がいこくじん, foreigner), 日本人 (にほんじん, Japanese person).
✗ ゆうにん substitutes にん for じん. 人 reads じん in this compound, not にん. Both にん and じん are on-yomi for 人, but じん is the correct one when combined with 友 (ゆう).
✗ ともにん uses the kun-yomi of 友 (とも) and the on-yomi of 人 (にん). Mixing kun-yomi and on-yomi in a compound this way is called 重箱読み (じゅうばこよみ) and does not apply here.
✗ ともひと uses kun-yomi for both characters: とも (友) and ひと (人). 友人 is an on-yomi compound, so kun-yomi for both produces a non-word in this context.
例: 大学 (だいがく) 時代 (じだい) の友人 (ゆうじん) に久 (ひさ) しぶりに会 (あ) った。 — I met up with a friend from university days after a long time.

question: 「対象」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
対象 is read たいしょう and means 'target' or 'subject' — the object that an action or study is directed at.
対象 (たいしょう) means a target, subject, or object of some action — the thing that a study, policy, service, or activity is aimed at. 対 (たい) has the on-yomi たい and means 'facing' or 'against'; it appears in 対応 (たいおう, response) and 対策 (たいさく, countermeasure). 象 (しょう) has the on-yomi しょう and means 'phenomenon,' 'appearance,' or 'symbol'; it appears in 現象 (げんしょう, phenomenon) and 象徴 (しょうちょう, symbol). Together: たいしょう = 'the thing facing you / the thing you are directing your attention at' = target or subject. Common uses: 研究対象 (けんきゅうたいしょう, research subject), 対象年齢 (たいしょうねんれい, target age group).
✗ ついしょう applies a non-standard ついreading to 対. 対 is not read つい in standard compound vocabulary; its on-yomi is たい.
✗ ついぞう applies the non-standard つい to 対 and reads 象 as ぞう (the elephant kun-yomi reading, 象 meaning elephant). 象 in this compound uses the on-yomi しょう, not the kun-yomi ぞう (elephant).
✗ たいぞう gets the first character right (たい) but reads 象 as ぞう (elephant). The on-yomi of 象 in compounds is しょう, not the animal reading ぞう.
例: このサービスは高齢者 (こうれいしゃ) を対象 (たいしょう) に設計 (せっけい) されている。 — This service is designed with elderly people as the target.

question: 「対策」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
対策 is read たいさく and means 'countermeasure' or 'measures to address a problem.'
対策 (たいさく) is an on-yomi compound. 対 (たい) means 'against / facing,' and 策 (さく) means 'plan / strategy / measure.' Together they describe concrete steps or plans designed to deal with a problem or threat. 対策を取る (たいさくをとる) = to take measures; 地震 (じしん) 対策 = earthquake preparedness; 対策を立てる (たてる) = to devise countermeasures. The reading たいさく uses on-yomi for both characters. 対 (たい) appears in 対話 (たいわ, dialogue), 対立 (たいりつ, confrontation), and 対応 (たいおう, response). 策 (さく) appears in 政策 (せいさく, policy) and 方策 (ほうさく, means/method). This is a core N3 word that appears in safety, environment, business, and public policy writing.
✗ ついせき assigns つい to 対 and せき to 策. 対 reads たい (on-yomi); つい is the on-yomi for characters like 追 (つい, to follow/pursue) or 対 in archaic usage. In standard vocabulary, 対 reads たい.
✗ たいせき reads 対 correctly as たい but assigns せき to 策. せき is the on-yomi for characters like 席 (せき, seat) or 積 (せき, accumulate). 策 reads さく, not せき.
✗ ついさく assigns つい to 対 (incorrect) but reads 策 correctly as さく. Half-correct is still wrong.
例: 感染症 (かんせんしょう) の拡大 (かくだい) を防 (ふせ) ぐための対策 (たいさく) が急 (きゅう) がれた。 — Countermeasures to prevent the spread of infection were urgently needed.

question: 地震の（＿＿＿）を考える必要があります。
explanation:
対策 (たいさく) fits because the sentence calls for 'measures' to address the earthquake — a concrete response plan.
対策 (たいさく) means 'countermeasure' or 'measures taken in response to a problem.' 対 (たい) means 'against / facing,' and 策 (さく) means 'plan / strategy.' Together they describe specific, practical steps designed to deal with a problem or threat. The sentence says 'We need to think about the ( ) for earthquakes,' which calls for a word meaning 'what to do about them.' 対策 fits perfectly: 地震 (じしん) の対策 (じしんのたいさく) = earthquake preparedness measures. This word appears in government announcements, safety manuals, and crisis management: 対策を立てる (たいさくをたてる, to develop measures), 対策を講じる (こうじる, to implement countermeasures). It is a core N3 word for problem-response vocabulary.
✗ 対象 (たいしょう) means 'target' or 'subject of attention' — the thing you are dealing with, not the plan for dealing with it. 地震の対象 would mean 'the target/object of an earthquake,' which does not make natural sense here.
✗ すべて可能 means 'all options possible' — a meta-answer indicating multiple choices could work. While several words could fill the blank in some contexts, the sentence specifically asks for thinking about a response plan, which points to 対策 as the clearest natural fit.
✗ 対応 (たいおう) means 'response' or 'handling' — reacting to something as it happens. It is similar to 対策 but more reactive. 対策 implies pre-planned steps or measures; 対応 implies adapting in the moment. Both can appear with 地震, but 「考える必要がある」(need to think about) suggests forward planning, which aligns more with 対策.
例: 地震 (じしん) に備 (そな) えた対策 (たいさく) をあらかじめ考 (かんが) えておく必要 (ひつよう) があります。 — It is necessary to think about earthquake preparedness measures in advance.

question: 「豊か」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
豊か is read ゆたか and means 'abundant' or 'rich' — full of something valuable.
豊か (ゆたか) is a な-adjective meaning 'abundant,' 'rich,' 'plentiful,' or 'full of.' It applies to material wealth (豊かな生活, ゆたかなせいかつ, a comfortable life), natural resources (資源が豊かな国, しげんがゆたかなくに, a resource-rich country), and non-material qualities (感情が豊か, かんじょうがゆたか, emotionally rich). The reading ゆたか is the kun-yomi used when the adjective stands alone. The on-yomi ほう appears in compounds: 豊富 (ほうふ, abundant) and 豊作 (ほうさく, bumper crop). The kanji 豊 depicts a ceremonial vessel overflowing with food — an image of abundance.
✗ とよか is not a reading for 豊か. とよ appears in place names like 豊中 (とよなか) or 豊田 (とよた), but for the adjective 豊か, the reading is ゆたか.
✗ ゆうか is not a reading for 豊か. ゆう does not appear in any standard reading for this kanji. The correct reading is ゆたか.
✗ ほうか misapplies the on-yomi ほう (used in 豊富 ほうふ, abundant) as a standalone adjective reading. When 豊か functions as a な-adjective on its own, the reading is always ゆたか.
例: この地域 (ちいき) は自然 (しぜん) が豊 (ゆた) かだ。 — This region is rich in nature.

question: 「貧しい」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
貧しい (まずしい) means 'poor' — lacking sufficient money or material resources to live comfortably.
貧しい (まずしい) is an i-adjective meaning 'poor' or 'impoverished.' The kanji 貧 combines 分 (divide) and 貝 (money/shell) — the image of dividing money into insufficient portions. The kun-yomi is まず, producing the adjective 貧しい (まずしい). The on-yomi is ひん, appearing in 貧困 (ひんこん, poverty) and 貧富 (ひんぷ, wealth and poverty). At N3, knowing both forms is useful: 「貧 (まず) しい生活 (せいかつ)」= 'a life of poverty'; 「貧困率 (ひんこんりつ)」= 'poverty rate.' The adverbial form is 貧しく (まずしく).
✗ average describes a middle condition. The Japanese equivalent is 平均的な (へいきんてきな) or 普通の (ふつうの). 貧しい is below average, not neutral.
✗ rich is 豊かな (ゆたかな) or 裕福な (ゆうふくな) — the direct antonym of 貧しい. 貧 and 富 (とみ) are a classic antonym pair.
✗ noble refers to high social status — 高貴な (こうきな) or 貴族の (きぞくの). Noble and poor are orthogonal: you can be both, or neither.
例: 彼 (かれ) は貧 (まず) しい家庭 (かてい) に生 (う) まれたが、努力 (どりょく) して医師 (いし) になった。 — He was born into a poor family but became a doctor through hard work.

question: 「展開」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
展開 is read てんかい and means 'development / unfolding.'
展開 (てんかい) is a noun and する-verb meaning 'to develop,' 'to unfold,' or 'to expand.' Both kanji use their on-yomi: 展 (てん) and 開 (かい). 展 conveys spreading out — seen in 展示 (てんじ, exhibition) and 展望 (てんぼう, outlook). 開 means opening — as in 開発 (かいはつ, development) and 公開 (こうかい, public release). Together, 展開 captures spreading open and progressing forward. Used for story plot development (物語の展開, ものがたりのてんかい), military maneuvers, and business expansion. 急展開 (きゅうてんかい, sudden turn of events) is a common N3 compound in news writing.
✗ のべかい uses のべ as a reading for 展. のべ belongs to 延 (extend/total), a different kanji — not 展.
✗ のべがい compounds an incorrect reading for 展 (のべ) with a voiced variant がい that does not exist for 開.
✗ てんがい uses the correct on-yomi てん for 展 but voices 開 to がい. 開 is read かい in 展開; voicing does not apply here.
例: 話 (はなし) が急 (きゅう) な展開 (てんかい) を見 (み) せた。 — The story took a sudden turn.

question: 「維持」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
維持 is read いじ and means 'maintenance / keeping something as it is.'
維持 (いじ) is a noun and する-verb meaning 'to maintain,' 'to keep up,' or 'to sustain.' Both kanji use their on-yomi: 維 (い) and 持 (じ). 維 means 'binding fiber' — also appearing in 維新 (いしん, restoration). 持 means 'to hold' — familiar from 持つ (もつ) and compounds like 保持 (ほじ, retention) and 支持 (しじ, support). 維持 describes keeping a situation, condition, or level steady. Common collocations: 健康を維持する (けんこうをいじする, maintain one's health), 秩序を維持する (ちつじょをいじする, maintain order).
✗ ゆいち misreads 維 as ゆい. The on-yomi of 維 is い — ゆい belongs to a different kanji (唯).
✗ いち reads 維 correctly as い but misreads 持 as ち. The on-yomi of 持 in compounds is じ, not ち.
✗ ゆいじ misreads 維 as ゆい, confusing it with 唯一 (ゆいいつ, unique/only one). 唯 and 維 are different kanji.
例: 体重 (たいじゅう) を維持 (いじ) するのは難 (むずか) しい。 — It is difficult to maintain one's weight.

question: 健康を（＿＿＿）するために運動します。
explanation:
健康を（ ）するために運動します — all three options (改善、維持、回復) work naturally, so 'すべて可能' is correct.
The sentence 「健康 (けんこう) を（ ）するために運動 (うんどう) します」 means 'I exercise in order to [do something with] my health.' Three different actions fit equally well. 改善 (かいぜん, improvement) → exercising to improve health that is currently below a desired level. 維持 (いじ, maintenance) → exercising to keep existing good health. 回復 (かいふく, recovery) → exercising to regain health lost to illness or inactivity. All three combine naturally with 健康を〜する and all represent real, common motivations for exercise. Because the sentence provides no context that excludes any of the three scenarios, all three fill the blank correctly.
✗ 改善 (かいぜん, improvement) alone is valid but not exclusively correct. It fits one scenario but 維持 and 回復 are equally natural collocates of 健康.
✗ 維持 (いじ, maintenance/preservation) alone is valid but not the only correct answer — it fits a different scenario than 改善 or 回復.
✗ 回復 (かいふく, recovery) alone is valid but not exclusive — it implies health had declined, which the sentence does not specify.
例: 毎日 (まいにち) 歩 (ある) くことで、健康 (けんこう) を維持 (いじ) しています。 — I maintain my health by walking every day.

question: 「改善」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
改善 is read かいぜん and means 'improvement' — making something better than it was before.
改善 (かいぜん) means improvement — the act of making something better. 改 (かい) has the on-yomi かい and means 'to reform' or 'to change'; it appears in 改革 (かいかく, reform) and 改良 (かいりょう, improvement). 善 (ぜん) has the on-yomi ぜん and means 'good' or 'better'; it appears in 善意 (ぜんい, good faith) and 最善 (さいぜん, the best possible). Together: かいぜん = 'changing to something good' = improvement. The word is famous internationally as a Japanese business concept (Toyota's kaizen philosophy of continuous incremental improvement). In everyday Japanese: 健康改善 (けんこうかいぜん, health improvement), 環境改善 (かんきょうかいぜん, environmental improvement).
✗ あらせん applies the kun-yomi あら of 改 (from 改める, あらためる) and a non-standard せん reading for 善. 善 uses its on-yomi ぜん, not せん.
✗ かいせん gets the first character right (かい) but reads 善 as せん — close to ぜん but missing the voiced consonant. The on-yomi of 善 is ぜん (voiced), not せん.
✗ あらぜん applies the kun-yomi あら to 改 and the correct on-yomi ぜん to 善. Half right, but 改 uses its on-yomi かい in this compound.
例: 業務 (ぎょうむ) の効率 (こうりつ) を改善 (かいぜん) するために、新 (あたら) しいシステムを導入 (どうにゅう) した。 — We introduced a new system in order to improve operational efficiency.

question: 「把握」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
把握 is read はあく and means 'to grasp / to understand fully.'
把握 (はあく) is a noun and verb (把握する) meaning 'to grasp,' 'to understand fully,' or 'to have a firm hold on' — both physically and mentally. 把 (は) means 'to hold / grip,' and 握 (あく) means 'to grip / squeeze.' Together they create the image of holding something firmly in both hands — and by extension, having a complete understanding of a situation. Common patterns: 状況 (じょうきょう) を把握する (to grasp the situation), 現状 (げんじょう) 把握 (grasping the current state), 全体 (ぜんたい) を把握する (to understand the whole picture). 把握 is a formal, written-style word — you would use 理解する (りかいする) in casual conversation, but 把握する in reports and official documents.
✗ ばにぎ uses the on-yomi of 把 (ba, voiced form) and a kun-yomi guess for 握 (にぎ, from 握る). This reading pattern does not apply to the compound 把握.
✗ ばあく voices the first character (は → ば) without cause. 把 reads は (unvoiced) in standard compounds. There is no rule that triggers voicing of は here.
✗ はにぎ correctly identifies the は reading for 把 but applies the kun-yomi にぎ for 握. The compound 把握 uses on-yomi for both: は + あく.
例: まず現状 (げんじょう) を把握 (はあく) することが大切 (たいせつ) です。 — First, it is important to fully grasp the current situation.

question: 「状況」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
状況 is read じょうきょう and means 'situation' or 'circumstances' — the current state of affairs.
状況 (じょうきょう) is an on-yomi compound. 状 (じょう) means 'form / condition / state,' and 況 (きょう) means 'circumstances / actual conditions.' Together they describe the current state of a situation at a given moment. 状況を説明する (じょうきょうをせつめいする) = to explain the situation; 緊急 (きんきゅう) の状況 = an emergency situation; 状況を判断する (はんだんする) = to assess the circumstances. The word describes both concrete physical situations (a scene at an accident) and abstract ones (the political situation). At N3, it appears broadly in news, reports, and everyday speech. 状 (じょう) also appears in 状態 (じょうたい, state/condition) and 現状 (げんじょう, current situation). 況 (きょう) appears in 不況 (ふきょう, economic recession) and 好況 (こうきょう, economic boom).
✗ そうかん assigns そう to 状 and かん to 況. 状 reads じょう (on-yomi), not そう. そう belongs to characters like 総 (そう, all/general) or 想 (そう, thought).
✗ じょうかん reads 状 correctly as じょう but assigns かん to 況. 況 reads きょう (on-yomi); かん belongs to characters like 感 (かん, feeling) or 間 (かん, space/time).
✗ そうきょう uses そう for 状 (incorrect) and きょう for 況 (correct). The second character reading is right, but the first is wrong.
例: 現在 (げんざい) の状況 (じょうきょう) を冷静 (れいせい) に分析 (ぶんせき) する必要 (ひつよう) がある。 — It is necessary to analyze the current situation calmly.

question: 状況を（＿＿＿）してから判断します。
explanation:
状況を（ ）してから判断します — all three options (理解、把握、確認) are natural here, so 'すべて可能' is correct.
The sentence 「状況 (じょうきょう) を（ ）してから判断 (はんだん) します」 means 'I will [do something with] the situation before making a judgment.' All three options fit naturally: 理解する (りかいする, to understand) — understanding the situation is a prerequisite for good judgment. 把握する (はあくする, to grasp/comprehend) — grasping the full picture before deciding is equally sound. 確認する (かくにんする, to confirm/verify) — checking facts before judging is also prudent. Each represents a different but equally valid cognitive step taken before making a decision. Because nothing in the sentence excludes any of them, all three fill the blank correctly.
✗ 理解 (りかい, understanding) alone is valid but not exclusively correct — 把握 and 確認 work equally well.
✗ 把握 (はあく, grasping/comprehending) alone is valid but not the only correct choice. 把握する emphasizes comprehending the whole picture, which is natural before judging.
✗ 確認 (かくにん, confirmation/verification) alone is valid. Verifying facts before judging is sensible, but so are 理解 and 把握.
例: まず状況 (じょうきょう) を把握 (はあく) してから、次 (つぎ) の手 (て) を考 (かんが) えましょう。 — Let us first grasp the situation, then think about the next step.

question: 「実施」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
実施 is read じっし and means 'implementation / putting something into practice.'
実施 (じっし) is a noun and suru-verb meaning 'implementation,' 'execution,' or 'carrying out' a plan or policy. 実 (じっ) means 'actual / real,' and 施 (し) means 'to carry out / to apply.' Together they describe putting something into actual practice — moving from plan to action. 計画 (けいかく) を実施する (to implement a plan), 試験 (しけん) を実施する (to administer an exam), 政策 (せいさく) の実施 (policy implementation). 実施 is a formal, official word that appears in government, business, and academic contexts. Like 実証, the reading uses じっ (contracted on-yomi for 実) before the し sound.
✗ みつし uses the kun-yomi み for 実 and invents つ before し. 実 reads じっ (on-yomi contracted) in this compound, not み.
✗ みし uses the kun-yomi み for 実 and on-yomi し for 施. The first character needs the on-yomi じっ.
✗ じつし uses the uncontracted on-yomi じつ rather than the contracted じっ. Before し, 実 contracts to じっ — the double consonant (促音) is phonologically required.
例: 新しい政策 (せいさく) が来月 (らいげつ) から実施 (じっし) される。 — The new policy will be implemented starting next month.

question: 「実績」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
実績 is read じっせき and means 'actual results' or 'track record' — past achievements as concrete evidence.
実績 (じっせき) means actual results, track record, or past achievements — the concrete record of what has been accomplished. 実 (じっ) has the on-yomi じつ, which becomes じっ before さ-row sounds (gemination rule); 績 (せき) has the on-yomi せき and means 'achievement' or 'accomplishment'; it appears in 成績 (せいせき, grades/performance) and 功績 (こうせき, meritorious achievement). Together: じっせき = 'actual concrete achievements' = track record or results. Common uses: 販売実績 (はんばいじっせき, sales record), 実績を積む (じっせきをつむ, to build up a track record). The gemination (じっ) is triggered because 実 precedes the さ-row sound せ.
✗ じつせき applies the standard on-yomi じつ to 実 without gemination. However, when 実 precedes さ-row sounds, the standard form is じっせき (geminated). じつせき is not used in standard modern Japanese.
✗ みせき applies a kun-yomi み to 実 (み is a real kun-yomi of 実 meaning 'fruit'), but 実績 uses the on-yomi じっ, not the kun-yomi み.
✗ みつせき combines a non-standard reading みつ for 実 and the correct on-yomi せき for 績. Neither みつ is a standard reading of 実 in this compound.
例: この会社 (かいしゃ) は豊富 (ほうふ) な実績 (じっせき) があり、多 (おお) くのクライアントに信頼 (しんらい) されている。 — This company has an extensive track record and is trusted by many clients.

question: 「実現」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
実現 is read じつげん and means 'realization' — making something real that was previously a dream or plan.
実現 (じつげん) means to realize, to bring into being, or to make real — turning a dream, plan, or possibility into actual reality. 実 (じつ) has the on-yomi じつ and means 'reality,' 'substance,' or 'fruit'; it appears in 現実 (げんじつ, reality) and 実際 (じっさい, in actuality). 現 (げん) has the on-yomi げん and means 'to appear' or 'to manifest'; it appears in 現在 (げんざい, present) and 現象 (げんしょう, phenomenon). Together: じつげん = 'making substance appear' = realization. Note: じつ + げん → 実現 (じつげん). Some learners guess じっげん (with a doubled consonant), but the geminate does not apply here because 実 (じつ) precedes げ, not a voiceless stop.
✗ じっげん incorrectly applies gemination to 実. The geminate っ before consonants applies predictably for certain prefixes like 一 (いっ) or 実 when followed by か/さ/た row sounds. じつ + げ does not trigger gemination — the reading is じつげん, not じっげん.
✗ みげん applies a non-standard み reading to 実. 実 does not have mi as a standard reading; its on-yomi is じつ and its kun-yomi is み (fruit of a tree), but み is not used in this compound.
✗ みっげん applies a kun-yomi fragment み and then over-geminates it. Neither み nor the geminate applies to 実 in the compound 実現.
例: 長年 (ながねん) の夢 (ゆめ) をついに実現 (じつげん) することができた。 — I was finally able to make my long-held dream come true.

question: 夢を（＿＿＿）するために努力します。
explanation:
夢を（ ）するために努力します — 実現 (じつげん) is the correct choice because it means 'realizing' a dream.
実現 (じつげん) means 'to realize,' 'to make real,' or 'to bring something into being from a dream or plan.' 実 (じつ) means 'reality' or 'substance,' and 現 (げん) means 'to appear' or 'to manifest.' Together: じつげん = 'making something manifest as reality.' The sentence says 'I make effort in order to （ ）my dream.' 夢を実現する (ゆめをじつげんする) = 'to make a dream come true' is a fixed, natural phrase in Japanese. The other 実〜 compounds do not fit the collocation 夢を〜する in the same way.
✗ 実施 (じっし) means 'to implement' or 'to put into practice' — used for plans, policies, and programs, not for dreams. 「計画を実施する」(implement a plan) is natural; 「夢を実施する」is unnatural.
✗ 実績 (じっせき) means 'actual results' or 'track record' — what you have already accomplished. You cannot '実績する' a dream; 実績 is a noun describing past outcomes, not a goal-oriented verb.
✗ 実行 (じっこう) means 'to carry out' or 'to execute' — used for plans and actions, not dreams. 「計画を実行する」(execute a plan) is correct; 「夢を実行する」sounds awkward because dreams are realized, not executed.
例: 長年 (ながねん) の夢 (ゆめ) をついに実現 (じつげん) することができた。 — I was finally able to make my long-held dream come true.

question: 「傾向」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
傾向 is read けいこう and means 'tendency' or 'trend' — a pattern in which things lean in a particular direction.
傾向 (けいこう) means a tendency, inclination, or trend — a pattern by which things regularly lean in a particular direction. 傾 (けい) has the on-yomi けい and means 'to lean' or 'to incline'; its kun-yomi かたむ appears in 傾く (かたむく, to tilt/lean). 向 (こう) has the on-yomi こう and means 'direction' or 'tendency'; it appears in 方向 (ほうこう, direction) and 向上 (こうじょう, improvement). Together: けいこう = 'leaning in a direction' = tendency or trend. Common uses: 増加傾向 (ぞうかけいこう, upward trend), 〜する傾向がある (〜するけいこうがある, to tend to do ~). Both kanji use their on-yomi.
✗ けいむく gets the first character right (けい) but reads 向 as the kun-yomi むく (from 向く, むく, to face/turn toward). The compound uses the on-yomi こう for 向.
✗ かたむく is the verb 傾く (to lean/tilt) written in its conjugated form — but this is the kun-yomi reading of 傾 alone, not a reading of the compound 傾向.
✗ かたこう applies the kun-yomi かた (from 傾く) to 傾 and the on-yomi こう to 向. The compound uses the on-yomi けい for 傾.
例: 近年 (きんねん)、若者 (わかもの) の活字離 (かつじばな) れの傾向 (けいこう) が強 (つよ) まっている。 — In recent years, the trend of young people moving away from reading printed material has been growing stronger.

question: 「現象」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
現象 is read げんしょう and means 'phenomenon / observable occurrence.'
現象 (げんしょう) is a noun meaning 'phenomenon' — something that occurs and can be observed or studied. 現 (げん) means 'to appear / to become visible,' and 象 (しょう) means 'form / image / likeness.' Together they describe something that 'appears in visible form' — a measurable, observable event in the world. 自然現象 (しぜんげんしょう, natural phenomenon), 社会現象 (しゃかいげんしょう, social phenomenon), 異常気象 (いじょうきしょう, abnormal weather — a related word). 現象 is widely used in science, social commentary, and academic writing. The reading uses on-yomi for both: 現 (げん) and 象 (しょう).
✗ げんぞう is the reading for 現像 (げんぞう, photographic development) or 幻像 (げんぞう, phantom image) — different words. 象 reads しょう here, not ぞう.
✗ あらぞう uses a kun-yomi guess for 現 (あら, from 現れる, あらわれる) and the wrong on-yomi ぞう for 象. Compound nouns like 現象 use on-yomi for both characters.
✗ あらしょう applies the kun-yomi あら for 現 and the correct on-yomi しょう for 象. The compound still needs on-yomi げん for the first character.
例: オーロラは美 (うつく) しい自然現象 (しぜんげんしょう) のひとつだ。 — The aurora is one of nature's beautiful phenomena.

question: 「現在」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
現在 is read げんざい and means 'the present' or 'currently' — this moment in time.
現在 (げんざい) means 'the present,' 'currently,' or 'at this time.' 現 (げん) has the on-yomi げん and means 'to appear' or 'current/present'; it appears in 現実 (げんじつ, reality), 現象 (げんしょう, phenomenon), and 表現 (ひょうげん, expression). 在 (ざい) has the on-yomi ざい and means 'to exist' or 'to be located'; it appears in 存在 (そんざい, existence) and 所在 (しょざい, location/whereabouts). Together: げんざい = 'existing at this moment' = the present. Common uses: 現在の状況 (げんざいのじょうきょう, the current situation), 現在地 (げんざいち, current location). Both kanji use their on-yomi.
✗ あらいま applies the kun-yomi あら of 現 (from 現れる, あらわれる, to appear) and the kun-yomi いま of 在 (meaning 'now'). While both are real kun-yomi, the compound 現在 uses on-yomi throughout.
✗ あらざい applies the kun-yomi あら to 現 and the correct on-yomi ざい to 在. The compound uses the on-yomi げん for 現.
✗ げんいま gets the first character right (げん) but reads 在 as the kun-yomi いま (now). The compound uses the on-yomi ざい for 在.
例: 現在 (げんざい) の状況 (じょうきょう) を踏 (ふ) まえて、今後 (こんご) の対策 (たいさく) を考 (かんが) えましょう。 — Based on the current situation, let us think about future measures.

question: 「過去」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
過去 is read かこ and means 'the past' — events that have already happened.
過去 (かこ) is a noun meaning 'the past' — all events that have already occurred. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 過 (か) and 去 (こ). 過 (す/か) means 'to pass' or 'to exceed' — as in 通過 (つうか, passing through) and 過程 (かてい, process). 去 (さ/きょ/こ) means 'to leave' or 'to depart' — as in 去年 (きょねん, last year). Together, 過去 literally means 'passed and departed.' Used in temporal expressions (過去に, かこに, in the past), grammatical categories (過去形, かこけい, past tense), and reflective writing.
✗ かきょ gets 過 correct (か) but misreads 去 as きょ. While 去 does have the reading きょ (去年 きょねん), in the word 過去 the reading is こ, not きょ.
✗ すぎきょ uses the kun-yomi すぎ for 過 (from 過ぎる すぎる) and きょ for 去. Both errors: on-yomi か and on-yomi こ are needed.
✗ すぎこ uses the kun-yomi すぎ for 過 with こ for 去. The correct reading uses the on-yomi か for 過, not the kun-yomi すぎ.
例: 過去 (かこ) のことは変 (か) えられない。 — You cannot change what happened in the past.

question: 「未来」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
未来 is read みらい and means 'the future.'
未来 (みらい) is a common compound meaning 'the future.' 未 (み) means 'not yet / still to come,' and 来 (らい) means 'to come / coming.' Together they describe the time that has not yet arrived. みらい is the standard on-yomi reading. 未 (み) appears widely in words meaning 'not yet': 未定 (みてい, undecided), 未来 (みらい, future), 未成年 (みせいねん, minor/under-age). 来 (らい) appears in 来年 (らいねん, next year), 来週 (らいしゅう, next week), and 将来 (しょうらい, future/prospects). Note that 未来 and 将来 (しょうらい) both translate as 'future,' but 未来 often feels more distant and abstract (the far future of humanity), while 将来 is more personal (your future career, your future plans).
✗ ひき assigns ひ to 未 and き to 来. 未 reads み (on-yomi) or いまだ (adverb meaning 'not yet'). ひ is the on-yomi for characters like 日 (ひ, sun/day) or 比 (ひ, compare). 来 reads らい, ら, or くる — not き.
✗ ひらい correctly reads 来 as らい but assigns ひ to 未 instead of the correct み. The on-yomi of 未 is み in all standard compounds.
✗ みき reads 未 correctly as み, but 来 becomes き — which is not a standard reading for 来. 来 reads らい (on-yomi) or くる (kun-yomi). き belongs to characters like 木 (き, tree) or 気 (き, spirit).
例: 未来 (みらい) の技術 (ぎじゅつ) がどんなものになるか、誰 (だれ) にも分 (わ) からない。 — No one knows what technology will look like in the future.

question: 「過去」「現在」「未来」を時間順に並べてください。
explanation:
過去→現在→未来 is the correct chronological order — past, present, future.
The three time words are: 過去 (かこ, the past), 現在 (げんざい, the present), and 未来 (みらい, the future). In chronological order: 過去→現在→未来. These are essential N3 vocabulary items used in formal writing, news, and academic texts. 過去 uses 過 (か, to pass) and 去 (きょ, to leave) — something that has passed and gone. 現在 uses 現 (げん, to appear/present) and 在 (ざい, to exist). 未来 uses 未 (み, not yet) and 来 (らい, to come) — what has not yet arrived.
✗ 現在→過去→未来 puts the present before the past, reversing their order. The past always precedes the present.
✗ 未来→現在→過去 is fully reversed — the reverse chronological order, not standard time sequence.
✗ 過去→未来→現在 skips the present and places it last. 現在 always lies between past and future; it must come second.
例: 過去 (かこ) の経験 (けいけん) が現在 (げんざい) の自分 (じぶん) を作 (つく) っている。 — Past experiences shape who I am today.

question: 「構造」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
構造 is read こうぞう and means 'structure / construction / framework.'
構造 (こうぞう) is a noun meaning 'structure,' 'construction,' or 'framework.' 構 (こう) means 'to build / to set up,' and 造 (ぞう) means 'to make / to construct.' Together they describe how something is built or organized — the internal arrangement of its parts. This word appears in many domains: 建物 (たてもの) の構造 (structure of a building), 社会構造 (しゃかいこうぞう, social structure), 文章構造 (ぶんしょうこうぞう, structure of a text), DNA の構造 (structure of DNA). Note the voiced second character: 造 reads ぞう (voiced) after 構 (こう) due to sequential voicing rules, a common pattern in two-kanji compounds.
✗ かまぞう uses the kun-yomi of 構 (かま, as in 構える, to set up) and the correct on-yomi for 造 (ぞう). However, the compound noun 構造 uses on-yomi こう, not kun-yomi かま.
✗ かまつく uses kun-yomi for 構 (かま) and a fabricated reading for 造 (つく, likely from 作る). 造 reads ぞう in this compound, not つく.
✗ こうつく uses the correct on-yomi for 構 (こう) but applies the kun-yomi for 造 (つく). The compound needs on-yomi for both: こう + ぞう.
例: この建物 (たてもの) の構造 (こうぞう) は非常 (ひじょう) に複雑 (ふくざつ) だ。 — The structure of this building is extremely complex.

question: 「段階」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
段階 is read だんかい and means 'stage' or 'phase' — one level in a sequence of steps or development.
段階 (だんかい) means a stage, phase, or step in a process or sequence. 段 (だん) has the on-yomi だん and means 'step,' 'level,' or 'stage'; it appears in 階段 (かいだん, staircase) and 手段 (しゅだん, means/method). 階 (かい) has the on-yomi かい and means 'floor,' 'level,' or 'stage'; it appears in 段階, 二階 (にかい, second floor), and 階層 (かいそう, hierarchy/layer). Together: だんかい = 'one step-level in a sequence' = stage or phase. Common uses: 第一段階 (だいいちだんかい, the first stage), 発達段階 (はったつだんかい, developmental stage), 段階的に (だんかいてきに, step by step/gradually).
✗ だんがい applies the on-yomi だん to 段 and reads 階 as がい — a voiced version of the correct reading かい. The on-yomi of 階 is かい (voiceless), not がい (voiced).
✗ たんがい reads 段 as たん (mixing it with 単 (たん) or 端 (たん)) and 階 as がい. 段 uses its on-yomi だん (voiced), not たん.
✗ たんかい reads 段 as たん and 階 correctly as かい. The first character 段 reads だん, not たん.
例: プロジェクトは現在 (げんざい) 第二段階 (だいにだんかい) に入 (はい) っており、順調 (じゅんちょう) に進 (すす) んでいる。 — The project has now entered its second stage and is progressing smoothly.

question: 「基本」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
基本 is read きほん and means 'basics' or 'fundamentals' — the essential foundation of something.
基本 (きほん) is an on-yomi compound. 基 (き) means 'base / foundation,' and 本 (ほん) means 'root / origin / main.' Together they describe the foundational principles or essential starting points of any activity, field, or skill. 基本を守る (きほんをまもる) = to observe the basics; 基本的な考え方 (きほんてきなかんがえかた) = a fundamental way of thinking. This word appears constantly in education, instruction manuals, and introductory courses. 基本的に (きほんてきに) is the adverb meaning 'basically / fundamentally,' used both in analysis ('fundamentally, the plan is flawed') and in polite hedging ('basically, yes'). 基 (き) appears in 基礎 (きそ, foundation/base), 基準 (きじゅん, standard/criterion), and 基地 (きち, base/station). 本 (ほん) appears in 本来 (ほんらい, originally), 本質 (ほんしつ, essence), and 本末転倒 (ほんまつてんとう, putting things in the wrong priority order). The reading きほん is entirely on-yomi and straightforward.
✗ もとほん applies the kun-yomi もと from 基 (基になる, もとになる, to form a basis) and then ほん for 本. Compounds use on-yomi; もと is not used in the two-kanji compound 基本.
✗ きぼん reads 基 correctly as き but uses ぼん (voiced) for 本 instead of the correct ほん (unvoiced). 本 reads ほん in this compound, not ぼん.
✗ もとぼん applies kun-yomi もと for 基 (incorrect) and voiced ぼん for 本 (also incorrect). Both halves are wrong.
例: 料理 (りょうり) の基本 (きほん) をしっかり覚 (おぼ) えることが大切 (たいせつ) です。 — It is important to thoroughly learn the basics of cooking.

question: 「基準」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
基準 is read きじゅん and means 'standard' or 'criterion' — a reference point used to measure or judge.
基準 (きじゅん) is the word for a standard, benchmark, or criterion used to evaluate or measure something. 基 (き) has the on-yomi き and means 'base' or 'foundation'; it appears in 基本 (きほん, basics), 基礎 (きそ, foundation), and 基地 (きち, base). 準 (じゅん) has the on-yomi じゅん and means 'level' or 'standard'; it appears in 水準 (すいじゅん, level/standard) and 標準 (ひょうじゅん, norm). Together: きじゅん = 'a foundational reference level' = standard or criterion. Common collocations: 基準を満たす (きじゅんをみたす, to meet a standard), 判断基準 (はんだんきじゅん, criteria for judgment), 安全基準 (あんぜんきじゅん, safety standards). Both kanji use their on-yomi.
✗ もとじゅん applies the kun-yomi もと for 基 and the correct on-yomi じゅん for 準. 基 uses its on-yomi き in academic compounds, not もと.
✗ もとすい takes the kun-yomi もと for 基 and reads 準 as すい instead of じゅん. すい is not a standard reading of 準.
✗ きすい gets the first character right (き) but reads 準 as すい. The on-yomi of 準 is じゅん, not すい.
例: この製品 (せいひん) は国際 (こくさい) 基準 (きじゅん) を満 (み) たしている。 — This product meets international standards.

question: 「根拠」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
根拠 is read こんきょ and means 'basis' or 'grounds' — the evidence or reason supporting a claim.
根拠 (こんきょ) is an on-yomi compound meaning 'basis,' 'grounds,' or 'rationale.' 根 (こん) means 'root,' and 拠 (きょ) means 'to rely on / base / foundation.' Together they describe the underlying support or evidence that a claim or argument rests on. 根拠のある主張 (こんきょのあるしゅちょう) = a well-grounded argument; 根拠がない (こんきょがない) = without basis / groundless. It is used in academic, legal, and formal contexts. 根 (こん) as on-yomi appears in 根本 (こんぽん, root/fundamental) and 根性 (こんじょう, guts/determination). 拠 (きょ) appears in 証拠 (しょうこ, evidence) and 依拠 (いきょ, to be based on). Notice that 根 reads こん in compounds but its kun-yomi is ね (root of a tree).
✗ こんこ assigns こ to 拠, but 拠 reads きょ (on-yomi). こ is not a standard on-yomi for this character.
✗ ねきょ uses the kun-yomi ね for 根 (from 根っこ, ねっこ, root) and the on-yomi きょ for 拠. 拠 is correct, but 根 uses its on-yomi こん in this compound.
✗ ねこ applies kun-yomi ね to 根 (same issue as above) and then こ to 拠 (wrong). Both halves are incorrect in their compound reading context.
例: その発言 (はつげん) には根拠 (こんきょ) がない。 — That statement has no basis.

question: その意見の（＿＿＿）は何ですか。
explanation:
根拠 (こんきょ) fits because the sentence asks for the basis or evidence behind an opinion.
根拠 (こんきょ) means 'basis,' 'grounds,' or 'evidence for a claim.' 根 (こん) means 'root,' and 拠 (きょ) means 'to be based on / a foothold.' Together they describe the root that a claim rests on — its supporting evidence or reasoning. The sentence says: 「その意見の（ ）は何ですか」 — 'What is the ( ) of that opinion?' This calls for a word meaning 'basis' or 'evidence.' 根拠 is the exact fit: 根拠のある意見 (a well-grounded opinion), 根拠を示す (to show evidence), 根拠がない (baseless/unsubstantiated).
✗ 基準 (きじゅん) means 'standard / criterion' — a rule used to judge or measure. A standard tells you what counts as acceptable; 根拠 tells you why a specific claim is valid.
✗ 基本 (きほん) means 'fundamental / basic principle.' It describes foundational concepts, not the evidence behind a specific opinion. 基本がわかる (to understand the basics) is quite different from 根拠を示す (to present grounds).
✗ すべて可能 ('all possible') does not apply because 基準 (standard) and 基本 (fundamental) do not naturally fill 「その意見の（ ）は何ですか」 — you would not ask 'What is the standard of that opinion?' or 'What is the fundamental of that opinion?' in natural Japanese.
例: その主張 (しゅちょう) には根拠 (こんきょ) がないと批判 (ひはん) された。 — The claim was criticized as lacking any basis.

question: 「分析」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
分析 is read ぶんせき and means 'analysis' — breaking something down to understand it.
分析 (ぶんせき) is a noun and verb (分析する) meaning 'analysis' or 'to analyze.' 分 (ぶん) means 'to divide / to separate,' and 析 (せき) means 'to split apart / to examine.' Together they describe breaking something complex into parts to understand how it works. This word is widely used in science, business, and academic Japanese: データ分析 (データぶんせき, data analysis), 市場分析 (しじょうぶんせき, market analysis), 原因分析 (げんいんぶんせき, cause analysis). 分析する is a suru-verb. The reading ぶんせき uses on-yomi for both characters: 分 (ぶん) and 析 (せき).
✗ ぶんかい is the reading for 分解 (ぶんかい, decomposition / disassembly) — physically taking something apart. 分析 (analysis) is conceptual; 分解 is mechanical or chemical.
✗ わけせき guesses a kun-yomi for 分 (わけ, as in 分ける, to divide) and on-yomi for 析. This mixed reading is not standard for the compound 分析.
✗ わけかい uses kun-yomi for 分 (わけ) and a misread かい for 析. 析 does not read かい — that would be 解 (かい, as in 理解).
例: データを分析 (ぶんせき) して問題点 (もんだいてん) を明 (あき) らかにした。 — We analyzed the data and clarified the issues.

question: 「評価」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
評価 is read ひょうか and means 'evaluation' or 'assessment' — judging the value or quality of something.
評価 (ひょうか) is an on-yomi compound. 評 (ひょう) means 'to comment on / to judge,' and 価 (か) means 'price / value.' Together they describe the act of assessing worth — whether of a person's performance, a product, or an academic result. 評価する means 'to evaluate / to assess / to appreciate.' 高い評価を受ける (たかいひょうかをうける) = to receive a high evaluation; 適切な評価 (てきせつなひょうか) = an appropriate assessment. This word is essential in academic, workplace, and business contexts. 評 (ひょう) also appears in 批評 (ひひょう, critique) and 評判 (ひょうばん, reputation). 価 (か) appears in 価格 (かかく, price) and 物価 (ぶっか, prices/cost of living).
✗ へいけ assigns へい to 評 and け to 価. 評 reads ひょう, not へい. The character for へい includes 平 (へい, flat/peace) or 閉 (へい, to close), neither of which is 評.
✗ ひょうけ reads 評 correctly as ひょう but assigns け to 価. The on-yomi of 価 is か, not け. か and け are different sounds.
✗ へいか reads 評 as へい (incorrect) and 価 as か (correct). Because the first half is wrong, the whole reading is wrong.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) は上司 (じょうし) から高 (たか) い評価 (ひょうか) を得 (え) た。 — She received a high evaluation from her supervisor.

question: 「批判」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
批判 is read ひはん and means 'criticism' or 'critical evaluation.'
批判 (ひはん) is an on-yomi compound. 批 (ひ) means 'to comment on / to annotate,' and 判 (はん) means 'to judge / to decide.' Together they describe the act of analyzing something and pointing out its faults or weaknesses — whether a policy, a person's actions, or a piece of writing. 批判する means 'to criticize.' You will see it in news, academic writing, and debates: 政府 (せいふ) への批判 (criticism of the government), 厳しい批判 (きびしいひはん, harsh criticism). 批 (ひ) is a less common character, but its on-yomi ひ is used in 批准 (ひじゅん, ratification) and 批評 (ひひょう, critique/review). 判 (はん) is very common: 判断 (はんだん, judgment), 判決 (はんけつ, court verdict).
✗ ひだん applies だん to the second character 判, but the on-yomi of 判 is はん, not だん. The character that reads だん includes 断 (だん, to cut/decide) or 段 (だん, step/level), neither of which is 判.
✗ ひばん uses ばん for 判, but ばん is the reading for characters like 晩 (ばん, evening) or 番 (ばん, number/turn). 判 reads はん, not ばん — a voicing slip that changes the word entirely.
✗ ひぱん applies half-voiced ぱん to 判, which is not a standard reading for this character in any context. Half-voicing (p-sounds) in Japanese compounds typically comes from rendaku rules, and 判 does not undergo this change here.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) の発言 (はつげん) は多くの人から批判 (ひはん) を受 (う) けた。 — Her remarks drew criticism from many people.

question: 「主張」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
主張 is read しゅちょう and means 'assertion' or 'claim' — stating one's position firmly.
主張 (しゅちょう) is an on-yomi compound meaning 'assertion,' 'claim,' or 'argument' — actively and firmly stating one's opinion or position. 主 (しゅ) means 'main / principal / lord,' and 張 (ちょう) means 'to stretch / to assert forcefully.' Together they describe the act of putting forward one's position as the central point. 主張する means 'to assert / to insist / to argue.' 自分の主張を曲げない (じぶんのしゅちょうをまげない) = to not bend one's position; 強い主張 (つよいしゅちょう) = a strong assertion. At N3, 主張 appears in discussions, essays, and debates. It differs from 意見 (いけん, opinion), which is softer and more tentative. 主張 implies force and insistence; 意見 is a milder, more tentative stated view.
✗ ぬしちょう uses the kun-yomi ぬし (owner/master, as in 持ち主) for 主. In two-kanji compounds, 主 reads しゅ (on-yomi), not ぬし.
✗ ぬしばり uses ぬし for 主 (incorrect, same issue) and ばり for 張. 張 reads ちょう (on-yomi) or はる (kun-yomi). ばり is not a standard reading for 張.
✗ しゅばり correctly reads 主 as しゅ but assigns ばり to 張. The on-yomi of 張 is ちょう, not ばり. ばり does not correspond to any standard reading of 張.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) は自分 (じぶん) の主張 (しゅちょう) を最後 (さいご) まで曲 (ま) げなかった。 — She did not abandon her claim until the very end.

question: 自分の意見を（＿＿＿）しました。
explanation:
主張 (しゅちょう) fits because the sentence is about asserting one's own opinion.
主張 (しゅちょう) means 'to assert / to claim / to advocate.' 主 (しゅ) means 'main / principal,' and 張 (ちょう) means 'to stretch out / to insist.' Together the word describes actively pushing forward your own view. The sentence says: 「自分の意見を（ ）しました」 — 'I ( ) my own opinion.' Asserting, claiming, and standing by one's view is exactly what 主張する expresses. 自分の意見を主張する is a set phrase. Notice that 主張 implies pushing your view out to others, not just holding it internally.
✗ 評価 (ひょうか) means 'to evaluate / to assess.' You evaluate someone else's opinion or work; you do not evaluate your own opinion in the sense of asserting it.
✗ 批判 (ひはん) means 'to criticize.' Criticizing your own opinion would be unusual and contradictory in this context. The sentence implies sharing/defending one's view, not attacking it.
✗ すべて可能 ('all possible') does not apply here because 批判する (criticize one's own opinion) would be self-contradictory, and 評価する does not carry the 'asserting' nuance the sentence requires.
例: 会議 (かいぎ) で自分 (じぶん) の意見 (いけん) をはっきり主張 (しゅちょう) した。 — I clearly asserted my opinion at the meeting.

question: 「矛盾」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
矛盾 is read むじゅん and means 'contradiction' — two claims that cannot both be true simultaneously.
矛盾 (むじゅん) means contradiction — two statements or facts that logically cannot coexist. The word comes from a Chinese fable: a merchant sold a 矛 (ほこ, spear) that could pierce anything, and a 盾 (たて, shield) that nothing could pierce. A bystander asked what happens when the spear meets the shield — and this logical impossibility became the word for contradiction. 矛 (む) has the on-yomi む; 盾 (じゅん) has the on-yomi じゅん. Together: むじゅん = contradiction. In modern Japanese: 「矛盾 (むじゅん) している」= 'It is self-contradictory.' This is a very common word in everyday arguments, essays, and logical reasoning.
✗ むとん takes the correct on-yomi む for 矛 but reads 盾 as とん instead of じゅん. とん is not a standard reading of 盾.
✗ ほことん applies the kun-yomi ほこ of 矛 (a spear) and reads 盾 as とん. Both readings are wrong; the compound uses on-yomi throughout.
✗ ほこじゅん takes the kun-yomi ほこ for 矛 and the correct on-yomi じゅん for 盾. Half right — but 矛 uses the on-yomi む, not the kun-yomi ほこ, in the compound.
例: 彼 (かれ) の発言 (はつげん) には矛盾 (むじゅん) が多 (おお) く、誰 (だれ) も信 (しん) じなかった。 — His statements were full of contradictions, and nobody believed him.

question: 「偏見」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
偏見 is read へんけん and means 'prejudice' or 'bias' — a one-sided, unfair view.
偏見 (へんけん) means prejudice or bias — a preconceived, one-sided view that is not based on fair evaluation. 偏 (へん) has the on-yomi へん and means 'one-sided' or 'biased'; it appears in 偏る (かたよる, to be biased/unbalanced) and 偏食 (へんしょく, unbalanced diet). 見 (けん) has the on-yomi けん and means 'view' or 'opinion'; it appears in 意見 (いけん, opinion) and 先入見 (せんにゅうけん, preconception). Together: へんけん = 'a one-sided view' = prejudice. Common uses: 偏見をなくす (へんけんをなくす, to eliminate prejudice), 偏見を持つ (へんけんをもつ, to hold prejudice).
✗ へんげん reads 偏 correctly as へん but reads 見 as げん instead of けん. The on-yomi of 見 in this compound is けん.
✗ かたけん applies the kun-yomi かた of 偏 (from 偏る, かたよる) and the correct on-yomi けん for 見. The compound uses the on-yomi へん for 偏.
✗ かたげん applies the kun-yomi かた to 偏 and reads 見 as げん — both readings are wrong for this compound.
例: 偏見 (へんけん) を持 (も) たずに相手 (あいて) の話 (はなし) を聞 (き) くことが大切 (たいせつ) だ。 — It is important to listen to the other person without prejudice.

question: 「公平」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
公平 is read こうへい and means 'fairness / impartiality.'
公平 (こうへい) is a na-adjective and noun meaning 'fair,' 'impartial,' or 'equitable.' 公 (こう) means 'public / open / official,' and 平 (へい) means 'flat / equal / calm.' Together they describe a state where everyone stands on even, flat ground — no one has an unfair advantage. Common patterns: 公平な判断 (こうへいなはんだん, a fair judgment), 公平に扱う (こうへいにあつかう, to treat fairly), 公平性 (こうへいせい, fairness as a principle). This word appears often in ethical, legal, and workplace contexts. The on-yomi for 公 is こう, seen in 公務員 (こうむいん, civil servant) and 公式 (こうしき, official/formal). The on-yomi for 平 is へい, seen in 平和 (へいわ, peace) and 平均 (へいきん, average).
✗ こうびょう confuses the reading of 平. 平 reads へい in こうへい, not びょう. びょう is the on-yomi for 病 (illness) or a different reading context entirely.
✗ おおびょう attempts a kun-yomi for 公 (おお is the kun-yomi of 大, not 公) and again misreads 平 as びょう. Two errors in one option.
✗ おおだいら uses the kun-yomi of 大 (おお) instead of 公's on-yomi こう, and reads 平 as だいら — a valid kun-yomi (平ら, たいら/だいら, 'flat surface') but not the reading used in this compound.
例: 採用 (さいよう) は公平 (こうへい) に行 (おこな) われなければならない。 — Hiring must be carried out fairly.

question: 「公平」の反対の意味の言葉はなんですか。
explanation:
不公平 (ふこうへい) is the direct opposite of 公平 (こうへい, fair).
公平 (こうへい) means 'fair / impartial.' Its direct antonym is 不公平 (ふこうへい), formed by adding the negation prefix 不 (ふ). The question asks for the single best opposite of 公平, and 不公平 is the precise mirror image — the exact same concept negated. While 差別 (さべつ, discrimination) and 偏見 (へんけん, prejudice) are related to unfairness, they describe specific forms of biased behavior. 不公平 is the broad, direct negation of 公平 on the same abstract level.
✗ 差別 (さべつ) means 'discrimination' — treating someone differently based on group membership. It is a form of unfairness, but it is more specific than the direct opposite of 公平.
✗ すべて関連 ('all are related') does not apply here because the question asks for the opposite (反対), not related words. 差別 and 偏見 are related to unfairness but are not direct antonyms of 公平 at the same level.
✗ 偏見 (へんけん) means 'prejudice / bias' — a preconceived negative attitude. It relates to unfairness but describes a mental state, not the direct negation of 公平 as a principle.
例: 扱 (あつか) いが不公平 (ふこうへい) だと感 (かん) じて、上司 (じょうし) に相談 (そうだん) した。 — I felt the treatment was unfair and consulted my supervisor.

question: 「抽象」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
抽象 is read ちゅうしょう and means 'abstraction / abstract (concept).'
抽象 (ちゅうしょう) is a noun and na-adjective meaning 'abstraction' or 'abstract.' 抽 (ちゅう) means 'to extract / to draw out,' and 象 (しょう) means 'form / image.' Together they describe drawing out the essential image or concept from specific instances — moving from concrete details to a general idea. 抽象的 (ちゅうしょうてき) is the na-adjective form: 抽象的な考え (an abstract idea), 抽象的すぎてわかりにくい (too abstract to understand). 抽象 contrasts with 具体的 (ぐたいてき, concrete / specific). The reading uses on-yomi for both: 抽 (ちゅう) and 象 (しょう).
✗ ぬきじょう guesses a kun-yomi for 抽 (ぬき, from 抜く / 抽く) and invents じょう for 象. 象 reads しょう in this compound, not じょう.
✗ ちゅうじょう uses the correct on-yomi ちゅう for 抽 but misreads 象 as じょう. 象 reads しょう — not じょう.
✗ ぬきぞう guesses kun-yomi ぬき for 抽 and applies the voiced ぞう reading of 象. 象 reads しょう (unvoiced) in 抽象; ぞう is a separate on-yomi of 象 (as in 象, elephant or 想像 ぞう... no, 想像 reads そうぞう). The unvoiced しょう is correct here.
例: この説明 (せつめい) は抽象的 (ちゅうしょうてき) すぎて理解 (りかい) しにくい。 — This explanation is too abstract and difficult to understand.

question: 「具体」の反対の意味の言葉はなんですか。
explanation:
具体 (ぐたい, concrete) is the opposite of 抽象 (ちゅうしょう, abstract).
具体 (ぐたい) means 'concrete' or 'specific' — relating to things you can see, touch, or describe in detail. Its direct antonym is 抽象 (ちゅうしょう), meaning 'abstract' — relating to ideas that lack a specific physical form. The pair 具体的 (ぐたいてき) vs. 抽象的 (ちゅうしょうてき) is a foundational contrast in academic Japanese. When someone says 「具体的に言うと」 (to put it concretely), they want details and examples. When something is 抽象的, it is theoretical and hard to picture. This antonym pair appears in both N3 vocabulary sections and reading passages.
✗ 一般 (いっぱん) means 'general' or 'common,' contrasting with 特定 (とくてい, specific) — not with 具体.
✗ 簡単 (かんたん) means 'easy' or 'simple.' Difficulty has no relation to concreteness — a problem can be simple yet abstract, or complex yet concrete.
✗ 普通 (ふつう) means 'ordinary' or 'normal,' contrasting with 特別 (とくべつ, special). Ordinariness is about frequency, not tangibility.
例: 抽象 (ちゅうしょう) な考 (かんが) え方 (かた) を具体 (ぐたい) 的 (てき) に説明 (せつめい) してください。 — Please explain that abstract idea in concrete terms.

question: 「促進」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
促進 is read そくしん and means 'promotion' or 'acceleration' — actively pushing something forward.
促進 (そくしん) means the act of promoting, accelerating, or facilitating something. 促 (そく) has the on-yomi そく and means 'to urge' or 'to prompt'; its kun-yomi うなが appears in 促す (うながす, to urge/prompt). 進 (しん) has the on-yomi しん and means 'to advance'; it appears in 進歩 (しんぽ, progress) and 進化 (しんか, evolution). Together: そくしん = 'urging forward' = promotion or acceleration. Common phrases: 経済成長を促進する (to promote economic growth), 健康促進 (けんこうそくしん, health promotion). The causative feel of 促進 is important — it implies an active agent making something happen faster.
✗ うなしん applies the kun-yomi うな of 促 (from 促す) and on-yomi しん for 進. The compound uses on-yomi throughout: そく + しん.
✗ うなすす applies kun-yomi to both: うな for 促 and すす for 進 (from 進む). The compound uses on-yomi for both characters.
✗ そくすす gets the first character right (そく) but applies the kun-yomi すす to 進 instead of the on-yomi しん.
例: 政府 (せいふ) は再生可能 (さいせいかのう) エネルギーの普及 (ふきゅう) を促進 (そくしん) する政策 (せいさく) を発表 (はっぴょう) した。 — The government announced a policy to promote the spread of renewable energy.

question: 「抑制」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
抑制 is read よくせい and means 'suppression / restraint.'
抑制 (よくせい) is a two-kanji noun meaning 'suppression,' 'restraint,' or 'inhibition.' 抑 (よく) means 'to hold down or press' and 制 (せい) means 'to control or regulate.' Together they describe actively suppressing something — holding it back from its natural tendency to grow or act. Common uses: 感情 (かんじょう) を抑制する (suppress emotions), 欲求 (よっきゅう) の抑制 (restraint of desires), インフレの抑制 (inflation control). In biology and medicine, 抑制 appears in contexts like 'immune suppression' (免疫抑制, めんえきよくせい). The reading よくせい uses the on-yomi for both kanji: 抑 (よく) and 制 (せい). Notice that 制 appears in many other control-related words: 制度 (せいど, system), 制限 (せいげん, limit), 規制 (きせい, regulation).
✗ よくせつ does not exist. The second character 制 reads せい, not せつ. Mixing up せい and せつ is a common phonetic trap because both end in similar sounds.
✗ おさせい reverses the kanji order and uses a kun-yomi guess for 抑. The kun-yomi 抑える is おさえる, but it does not apply to the compound 抑制. Compound nouns like 抑制 almost always use on-yomi.
✗ おさせつ is fabricated. Neither character produces this reading sequence. It combines the kun-yomi error from option 1 with the せつ error from option 0.
例: 感情 (かんじょう) を抑制 (よくせい) することが大切 (たいせつ) だ。 — It is important to suppress one's emotions.

question: 「促進」の反対の意味の言葉はなんですか。
explanation:
抑制 (よくせい) is the antonym of 促進 (そくしん) because it means 'to suppress or restrain' rather than 'to promote.'
促進 (そくしん) means 'promotion' or 'acceleration' — pushing something forward. The question asks for its opposite, so you need a word meaning 'to hold back.' 抑制 (よくせい) fits precisely. 抑 (よく) means 'to press down / restrain,' and 制 (せい) means 'to control or regulate.' Together they describe deliberately slowing, limiting, or suppressing something. You will see 抑制 in formal and academic contexts: 物価 (ぶっか) の抑制 (controlling prices), 感情 (かんじょう) を抑制する (to suppress emotions). It functions as a noun and a する-verb. The opposite relationship 促進 ↔ 抑制 is a common test pair because both words appear frequently in economics, science, and policy writing. When you see 促す (うながす, to urge/prompt), think 促進. When you see 押さえる (おさえる, to hold down), think 抑制.
✗ 発展 (はってん) means 'development' or 'expansion' — a positive growth, not a suppression. It is in the same direction as 促進, not opposite to it.
✗ 推進 (すいしん) means 'propulsion' or 'driving forward.' It is a near-synonym of 促進, not its antonym. Using 推進 as the answer would be choosing another word that means essentially the same thing as the question word.
✗ 加速 (かそく) means 'acceleration' — making something go faster. This is the opposite of what is needed. If 促進 already implies moving forward, 加速 intensifies that movement further, making it even further from the antonym.
例: 政府 (せいふ) はインフレを抑制 (よくせい) するための政策 (せいさく) を発表 (はっぴょう) した。 — The government announced policies to suppress inflation.

question: 「貢献」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
貢献 is read こうけん and means 'contribution' to a cause or group.
貢献 (こうけん) is an on-yomi compound. 貢 (こう) means 'to offer tribute / to contribute,' and 献 (けん) means 'to present / to dedicate.' Together they describe actively giving effort, resources, or talent for the benefit of something larger — society, a team, science. 貢献する means 'to contribute.' You will see it in formal contexts: 社会 (しゃかい) への貢献 (contribution to society), 貢献度 (こうけんど, degree of contribution). The reading こうけん uses on-yomi for both characters. 貢 (こう) also appears in 貢ぎ物 (みつぎもの, tribute offerings). 献 (けん) appears in 献血 (けんけつ, blood donation) and 献身 (けんしん, devotion) — all carrying the sense of giving selflessly.
✗ みつこん assigns みつ to 貢 (a kun-yomi fragment) and こん to 献. The on-yomi of 貢 is こう, not みつ. The kun-yomi is みつぐ (to pay tribute), but that form is only used in isolation, not in two-kanji compounds.
✗ こうこん replaces けん with こん. While こん is the on-yomi for characters like 根 (こん, root) or 困 (こん, trouble), 献 reads けん, not こん.
✗ みつけん applies the kun-yomi root みつ for 貢 and then けん for 献. The second character is correctly identified (けん), but the first remains wrong. In standard compound vocabulary, 貢 reads こう.
例: 彼女 (かのじょ) は長年 (ながねん) にわたって地域社会 (ちいきしゃかい) に貢献 (こうけん) してきた。 — She has contributed to the local community for many years.

question: 社会に（＿＿＿）したいです。
explanation:
社会に貢献 (こうけん)・参加 (さんか)・奉仕 (ほうし) する — all three work in this sentence.
The sentence says: 「社会に（ ）したいです」 — 'I want to ( ) society.' The question is which verb(s) fit the blank. All three options work: 貢献する (こうけんする) = 'to contribute to' — making a positive difference to society. 参加する (さんかする) = 'to participate in' — joining activities within society. 奉仕する (ほうしする) = 'to serve / to volunteer' — dedicating effort to society. All three can follow 社会に and express positive engagement with society. Because all three are grammatically and semantically valid, すべて可能 ('all possible') is the correct answer. This question type tests whether you can distinguish words that fit a frame from words that do not.
✗ 貢献 alone is valid, but selecting only one misses that 参加 and 奉仕 are equally correct completions of the same sentence.
✗ 参加 alone is valid, but the same reasoning applies — all three options produce a natural, meaningful sentence.
✗ 奉仕 alone is valid, but excluding the other two misses the full picture that the question is testing.
例: 地域 (ちいき) 社会 (しゃかい) に貢献 (こうけん) するためにボランティア活動 (かつどう) を始 (はじ) めた。 — I started volunteer activities to contribute to the local community.

question: 「独立」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
独立 is read どくりつ and means 'independence' — standing on one's own without relying on others.
独立 (どくりつ) means independence — whether of a nation, a person, or a business entity. 独 (どく) has the on-yomi どく and means 'alone' or 'single'; it appears in 独自 (どくじ, unique/original) and 独占 (どくせん, monopoly). 立 (りつ) has the on-yomi りつ and means 'to stand'; it appears in 自立 (じりつ, self-reliance) and 確立 (かくりつ, establishment). Together: どくりつ = 'standing alone' = independence. Common uses: 国家独立 (こっかどくりつ, national independence), 精神的独立 (せいしんてきどくりつ, psychological independence), 独立する (to become independent/set up one's own business).
✗ どくたつ gets the first character right (どく) but reads 立 as たつ — a kun-yomi of 立 (from 立つ, たつ). In the compound 独立, 立 uses its on-yomi りつ.
✗ ひとりつ applies the kun-yomi ひとり of 独 (as in 一人, alone) and the on-yomi りつ of 立. The compound uses the on-yomi どく for 独.
✗ ひとたつ applies the kun-yomi ひとり to 独 and the kun-yomi たつ to 立. Both readings are wrong for this compound.
例: 大学 (だいがく) を卒業 (そつぎょう) 後 (ご) 、親 (おや) から独立 (どくりつ) して一人暮 (ひとりぐ) らしを始 (はじ) めた。 — After graduating from university, I became independent from my parents and started living alone.

question: 「依存」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
依存 is read いぞん (also acceptable: いそん) and means 'dependence' — relying on something or someone.
依存 (いぞん) means dependence or reliance on something or someone. 依 (い) has the on-yomi い and means 'to rely on' or 'to depend'; it appears in 依頼 (いらい, request/reliance). 存 (ぞん/そん) has the on-yomi ぞん (or そん) and means 'to exist' or 'to be present'; it appears in 存在 (そんざい, existence) and 存続 (そんぞく, continuation). Together: いぞん = 'existing in reliance on something' = dependence. Note that both いぞん and いそん are accepted readings; the dictionary lists both, but いぞん is more common in contemporary Japanese. Common uses: インターネット依存 (internet dependence), 薬物依存 (やくぶついぞん, drug dependence).
✗ いそん is the older/alternate reading of 依存 — it is technically also correct in modern usage. However, the question lists いぞん (option 3) as the marked correct answer, reflecting the more contemporary pronunciation. When both appear as options, いぞん is the preferred modern form.
✗ よりぞん applies the kun-yomi より of 依 (from 依る, よる, to depend on) and the on-yomi ぞん of 存. The compound uses on-yomi for both: い + ぞん.
✗ よりそん applies kun-yomi より to 依 and the alternate on-yomi そん to 存. The compound uses the on-yomi い for 依.
例: スマートフォンへの依存 (いぞん) が高 (たか) まり、社会問題 (しゃかいもんだい) になっている。 — Dependence on smartphones is increasing and has become a social issue.

question: 「独立」の反対の意味の言葉はなんですか。
explanation:
独立の反対は 依存と従属両方 — both 依存 (dependence) and 従属 (subordination) are antonyms of 独立 (independence).
独立 (どくりつ) means 'independence' — standing on one's own without relying on or being controlled by others. 独 (どく) means 'alone / by oneself,' and 立 (りつ) means 'to stand.' The antonyms must express the opposite. 依存 (いぞん) means 'dependence' — relying on something or someone else to exist or function: 薬物依存 (やくぶついぞん, drug dependence), 親への依存 (おやへのいぞん, dependence on parents). 従属 (じゅうぞく) means 'subordination' — being under the control or authority of another entity: 従属国 (じゅうぞくこく, subordinate/vassal state). Both express different facets of the opposite of independence. 依存 focuses on needing something outside yourself to function; 従属 focuses on being ranked beneath and controlled by a higher power. Because both describe ways of not being independent, the question correctly identifies both as antonyms of 独立. This is one of the more nuanced antonym questions at N3, requiring you to recognize that a single word can have more than one valid antonym depending on the dimension being contrasted.
✗ 依存 (いぞん) alone is a valid antonym of 独立, but 従属 is also correct. Choosing only 依存 ignores the equally valid second antonym.
✗ 従属 (じゅうぞく) alone is also a valid antonym, but 依存 is equally valid. Choosing only 従属 ignores 依存.
✗ 協力 (きょうりょく) means 'cooperation' — working together. This is not an antonym of 独立. You can cooperate while remaining independent. 協力 describes a relationship between equals, not dependence or subordination.
例: 経済的 (けいざいてき) に独立 (どくりつ) するために、親 (おや) への依存 (いぞん) をなくす努力 (どりょく) をした。 — I made efforts to eliminate dependence on my parents in order to become financially independent.

question: 「膨大」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
膨大 is read ぼうだい and means 'enormous' or 'vast' — a quantity or scale that is staggeringly large.
膨大 (ぼうだい) is a な-adjective or noun-modifier meaning 'enormous,' 'vast,' or 'immense.' It typically describes quantities, amounts, or scales that are overwhelming in size: 「膨大 (ぼうだい) なデータ」= 'a vast amount of data,' 「膨大 (ぼうだい) な費用 (ひよう)」= 'an enormous cost.' 膨 (ぼう) has the on-yomi ぼう and means 'to swell' or 'to expand'; its kun-yomi ふく appears in 膨らむ (ふくらむ, to swell/expand). 大 (だい) has the on-yomi だい and means 'large'; it appears in 大学 (だいがく), 大量 (たいりょう), and 巨大 (きょだい). Together: ぼうだい = 'swelling large' = enormously large.
✗ ぼうおお applies the correct on-yomi ぼう to 膨 and the kun-yomi おお to 大 (as in 大きい). In the compound 膨大, 大 uses its on-yomi だい.
✗ ふくおお applies the kun-yomi ふく of 膨 (from 膨らむ) and the kun-yomi おお of 大. Both are real kun-yomi, but the compound uses on-yomi throughout.
✗ ふくだい applies the kun-yomi ふく to 膨 and the on-yomi だい to 大. Half right, but 膨 uses its on-yomi ぼう in this compound.
例: このプロジェクトには膨大 (ぼうだい) な時間 (じかん) と費用 (ひよう) がかかる。 — This project will require an enormous amount of time and money.

question: 「微妙」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
微妙 is read びみょう and means 'subtle / delicate / hard to define.'
微妙 (びみょう) is a na-adjective meaning 'subtle,' 'delicate,' or 'nuanced.' 微 (び) means 'minute / tiny,' and 妙 (みょう) means 'exquisite / mysterious / hard to pin down.' Together they describe something at the fine edge of perception — a subtle difference, a delicate taste, a nuanced emotion. 微妙な差 (びみょうなさ, a subtle difference), 微妙な表情 (びみょうなひょうじょう, a nuanced expression), 微妙な関係 (びみょうなかんけい, a delicate relationship). In casual modern Japanese, びみょう is also used to mean 'so-so / not quite right' — a young-person usage that can signal mild disapproval.
✗ かすみょ is not a real reading. It misreads 微 as かす (a kun-yomi fragment from 霞む, to haze/blur) and drops the long vowel for 妙.
✗ びみょ drops the long vowel. 妙 reads みょう (with a long vowel). びみょ is not a standard word — the っ-elongation びみょう is required.
✗ かすみょう combines the incorrect かす reading for 微 with the correct みょう for 妙. One character is right, one is wrong.
例: 二人 (ふたり) の間 (あいだ) には微妙 (びみょう) な空気 (くうき) が流 (なが) れた。 — A subtle tension passed between the two of them.

question: 「曖昧」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
曖昧 is read あいまい and means 'vague / ambiguous / unclear.'
曖昧 (あいまい) is a na-adjective meaning 'vague,' 'ambiguous,' or 'unclear.' Both 曖 (あい) and 昧 (まい) independently carry meanings related to darkness and obscurity. Together they reinforce each other to describe something that lacks clear definition — an answer that is neither yes nor no, a boundary that is hard to draw, a promise that is not firm. 曖昧な答え (あいまいなこたえ, a vague answer), 曖昧な表現 (あいまいなひょうげん, an ambiguous expression), 曖昧にする (to make something vague on purpose). Japanese culture is often described as tolerating ambiguity more than some other cultures — 曖昧 can describe both a problematic lack of clarity and a deliberate, face-saving indirectness.
✗ あいばい replaces まい with ばい. 昧 reads まい in this compound — ばい is not a standard on-yomi for 昧.
✗ わくまい invents the reading わく for 曖. 曖 reads あい — no standard reading produces わく.
✗ わくばい compounds both errors: わく for 曖 and ばい for 昧. Neither reading is correct.
例: 彼 (かれ) の返事 (へんじ) は曖昧 (あいまい) で、賛成 (さんせい) なのか反対 (はんたい) なのかわからなかった。 — His answer was so vague that I could not tell whether he agreed or disagreed.

question: 彼の説明は（＿＿＿）でよくわかりませんでした。
explanation:
曖昧 (あいまい) fits because the sentence says his explanation was hard to understand.
曖昧 (あいまい) means 'vague / ambiguous.' The sentence says: 「彼の説明は（ ）でよくわかりませんでした」 — 'His explanation was ( ) and I could not understand it well.' The blank needs a word that describes a failure of clarity — something that made the explanation hard to follow. 曖昧な説明 (a vague explanation) fits: when an explanation is vague or ambiguous, the listener cannot grasp what is being said. The result よくわかりませんでした (I could not understand well) confirms that the explanation lacked clarity — not that it was too detailed, too precise, or too accurate.
✗ 正確 (せいかく) means 'accurate / precise.' A precise explanation would be easy to understand, not difficult. 正確 would contradict よくわかりませんでした.
✗ 明確 (めいかく) means 'clear / definite.' A clear explanation makes understanding easy, not hard. Like 正確, it contradicts the sentence's stated result.
✗ 詳細 (しょうさい) means 'detailed.' Detailed explanations can be hard to follow if they are too long or complex, but 詳細 is not the natural fit here — the sentence suggests a problem of clarity, not of quantity. 曖昧 targets the core issue more precisely.
例: 上司 (じょうし) の指示 (しじ) が曖昧 (あいまい) で、何 (なに) をすればいいかわからなかった。 — My supervisor's instructions were so vague that I did not know what to do.

question: 「明確」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
明確 is read めいかく and means 'clear' or 'definite' — without ambiguity.
明確 (めいかく) is a な-adjective meaning 'clear,' 'definite,' 'explicit,' or 'unambiguous.' Both kanji use their on-yomi: 明 (めい) and 確 (かく). 明 means 'bright' or 'clear' — as in 明るい (あかるい, bright), 説明 (せつめい, explanation), and 透明 (とうめい, transparent). 確 means 'certain,' 'definite,' or 'to confirm' — as in 確認 (かくにん, confirmation), 確実 (かくじつ, certain), and 正確 (せいかく, accurate). Together, 明確 describes something clear and certain — no room for doubt. Common: 明確な指示 (めいかくなしじ, clear instructions), 目的を明確にする (もくてきをめいかくにする, clarify the objective).
✗ みょうかく misreads 明 as みょう. みょう is a valid on-yomi for 明 in certain words — most notably 明日 (みょうにち, tomorrow in formal register) and 明後日 (みょうごにち). However, in 明確, the reading is めい.
✗ あかかく uses the kun-yomi of 明 (あか from 明るい, bright) with the on-yomi of 確 (かく). Compound nouns use consistent on-yomi: めい＋かく.
✗ あきかく applies another kun-yomi of 明 (あき from 明ける, to open/become light). This kun-yomi does not belong in this formal compound.
例: 目標 (もくひょう) を明確 (めいかく) にしてから始 (はじ) めましょう。 — Let's clarify our goal before we begin.

question: 「曖昧」の反対の意味の言葉はなんですか。
explanation:
明確 (めいかく) is the antonym of 曖昧 (あいまい) because it means 'clear and definite' while 曖昧 means 'vague and ambiguous.'
曖昧 (あいまい) means 'vague,' 'ambiguous,' or 'unclear' — something that can be interpreted in more than one way. Its antonym must mean 'clear and definite.' 明確 (めいかく) fits exactly. 明 (めい) means 'bright / clear,' and 確 (かく) means 'definite / certain.' Together they describe something unambiguous, with no room for misinterpretation. 明確にする means 'to clarify / to make clear.' You will see it in contracts, instructions, and academic writing: 明確な基準 (きじゅん, clear criteria), 明確な回答 (かいとう, a definitive answer). The direct opposition 曖昧 ↔ 明確 is one of the important antonym pairs at N3 level, often tested together. 明確 functions as a な-adjective: 明確な指示 (めいかくなしじ, clear instructions), and as an adverb: 明確に述べる (めいかくにのべる, to state clearly). When a superior asks for 明確な返事 (めいかくなへんじ), they want a definite yes or no — not an ambiguous 曖昧な答え (あいまいなこたえ).
✗ すべて関連 means 'all are related' — a meta-answer about relationships among choices, not an antonym of 曖昧. This option is a distractor that does not function as a vocabulary word at all.
✗ 詳細 (しょうさい) means 'details' or 'detailed information.' While a detailed explanation might reduce ambiguity, 詳細 describes the quantity of information provided, not its clarity. Something can be detailed yet still ambiguous.
✗ 正確 (せいかく) means 'accurate' or 'precise' — free from errors. While 正確 and 明確 are close, 正確 is about factual correctness, whereas 明確 is about being unambiguous and clear in meaning. The direct opposite of 曖昧 is 明確.
例: 契約 (けいやく) の内容 (ないよう) を明確 (めいかく) にしておく必要 (ひつよう) があります。 — It is necessary to make the terms of the contract clear.

question: 「適切」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
適切 is read てきせつ and means 'appropriate' or 'suitable.'
適切 (てきせつ) is an on-yomi compound. 適 (てき) means 'to fit / to be suitable,' and 切 (せつ) means 'to cut to the right size / precise.' Together they describe something that fits a situation precisely — the right word, the right response, the right level of force. 適切な対応 (てきせつなたいおう) = an appropriate response; 適切に処理する (しょりする) = to handle appropriately. This is a key adjective at N3 that appears in reports, guidelines, and feedback. The reading てきせつ uses on-yomi for both characters: 適 (てき) as in 適合 (てきごう, conformity), 切 (せつ) as in 親切 (しんせつ, kindness) and 大切 (たいせつ, important).
✗ てきせち assigns せち to 切. The on-yomi of 切 is せつ or さい; せち is not a standard on-yomi for 切.
✗ てきぎ applies ぎ to 切. ぎ is the on-yomi for characters like 義 (ぎ, justice/duty) or 技 (ぎ, skill). 切 does not have a standard on-yomi reading of ぎ.
✗ てきき reads 切 as き — the kun-yomi (as in 切る, きる, to cut). In compound nouns, both characters use on-yomi. 切 reads せつ in this compound, not き.
例: 医師 (いし) は患者 (かんじゃ) に対 (たい) して適切 (てきせつ) な処置 (しょち) を取 (と) った。 — The doctor took appropriate measures for the patient.

question: 「妥当」の読み方はなんですか。
explanation:
妥当 is read だとう and means 'appropriate / reasonable / valid.'
妥当 (だとう) is a na-adjective meaning 'appropriate,' 'reasonable,' 'valid,' or 'sound.' 妥 (だ) means 'to settle / to be appropriate,' and 当 (とう) means 'to be fitting / to correspond.' Together they describe a judgment, action, or decision that fits the situation and cannot reasonably be faulted. 妥当な判断 (だとうなはんだん, a reasonable judgment), 妥当な理由 (だとうなりゆう, a valid reason), 妥当性 (だとうせい, validity/appropriateness). In legal and business contexts, 妥当 often appears in evaluating whether a decision or procedure was sound. The on-yomi reading: 妥 (だ) and 当 (とう).
✗ たとう is close but wrong — 妥 reads だ (voiced), not た (unvoiced). The distinction between voiced だ and unvoiced た is phonologically significant in Japanese.
✗ たさ invents a one-syllable reading for a two-character compound. No standard Japanese word is formed by reading 妥当 as たさ.
✗ ださ takes the correct voiced だ for 妥 but drops the second character 当 entirely, reading only one character. 当 reads とう in this compound and must not be dropped.
例: その提案 (ていあん) は妥当 (だとう) だと委員会 (いいんかい) が認 (みと) めた。 — The committee recognized the proposal as reasonable.

question: 「途方に暮れる」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
途方に暮れる (とほうにくれる) means 'to be at a loss' — not knowing what to do next.
途方に暮れる (とほうにくれる) is a set phrase meaning 'to be at a complete loss,' 'to not know which way to turn,' or 'to be utterly bewildered.' 途方 (とほう) originally meant 'a direction to take / a method,' and 暮れる (くれる) means 'to grow dark / to come to an end.' The combination evokes the feeling of darkness falling just as you realize you have no path forward — no idea what to do. This phrase is typically used when someone faces an unexpected, overwhelming problem and feels paralyzed. 彼女は仕事を失 (うしな) い、途方に暮れた (she lost her job and was at a complete loss). It carries a heavier emotional weight than 困る (こまる, to be troubled), which only means 'to be in a difficult spot.'
✗ 'to be happy' is the opposite emotional tone from 途方に暮れる. The word for being happy is 嬉しい (うれしい) or 幸せ (しあわせ). 途方に暮れる always describes distress or helplessness.
✗ 'to be angry' translates to 怒る (おこる) or 腹を立てる (はらをたてる). Anger involves a clear emotional target; 途方に暮れる describes helplessness rather than directed anger.
✗ 'to be sleepy' translates to 眠い (ねむい) or 眠たい. There is no semantic connection between sleepiness and being at a loss. The confusion would only arise if a learner did not know the phrase at all.
例: 突然 (とつぜん) 仕事 (しごと) を失 (うしな) い、彼女 (かのじょ) は途方 (とほう) に暮 (く) れた。 — She was at a complete loss after suddenly losing her job.

question: 「手に入れる」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
手に入れる (てにいれる) means 'to obtain / get' — to successfully acquire something you wanted.
手に入れる (てにいれる) is a verb phrase literally meaning 'to put into one's hand' — that is, to acquire or obtain something. 手 (て) is 'hand' and 入れる (いれる) is 'to put in / to insert.' Together they create the vivid image of bringing something into your grasp. The phrase is used for both physical objects and abstract goals: チケットを手に入れる (to get a ticket), 情報 (じょうほう) を手に入れる (to obtain information), 夢 (ゆめ) を手に入れる (to achieve one's dream). It implies active effort — you did not just find it, you went after it. 手に入る (てにはいる) is the intransitive form meaning 'to become obtainable / to come into one's hands,' whereas 手に入れる is the transitive, deliberate version.
✗ 'to lose' is the opposite. The Japanese for losing something is 失う (うしなう) or なくす. 手に入れる is about gaining, not losing.
✗ 'to throw away' translates to 捨てる (すてる) or 手放す (てばなす). 手放す is the near-antonym — releasing from the hand — while 手に入れる is the opposite, bringing into the hand.
✗ 'to return' translates to 返す (かえす) or 返却する (へんきゃくする). Returning something involves giving back what you already have — not acquiring something new as 手に入れる describes.
例: 彼 (かれ) はずっと欲 (ほ) しかった本 (ほん) をついに手 (て) に入 (い) れた。 — He finally got the book he had always wanted.

question: 「目を通す」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
目を通す (めをとおす) means 'to look through' or 'to read over' — giving something a quick read or scan.
目を通す (めをとおす) is an idiomatic expression meaning 'to go through' or 'to read over' — giving a document, report, or text a scan or quick read, not necessarily reading every word with full attention. 目 (め) = eyes; 通す (とおす) = to pass through/to run through. Together: 'to pass one's eyes over' = to scan or read through. It implies something less thorough than じっくり読む (to read carefully) but more engaged than glancing: 「メールに目 (め) を通 (とお) す」= 'to go through emails'; 「会議前 (かいぎまえ) に資料 (しりょう) に目 (め) を通 (とお) した」= 'I read over the materials before the meeting.' This expression is common in business Japanese.
✗ to open one's eyes means waking up or becoming aware — 目を開ける (めをあける) or 気 (き) づく. 目を通す is about reading/scanning, not about opening eyes.
✗ to blink is 目をパチパチさせる or まばたきする — an involuntary eye movement. 目を通す is a deliberate act of reading/reviewing, unrelated to blinking.
✗ to close one's eyes is 目を閉じる (めをとじる) — the opposite physical action. 目を通す means directing one's eyes at text, not closing them.
例: 会議 (かいぎ) の前 (まえ) に、配布 (はいふ) された資料 (しりょう) に目 (め) を通 (とお) してください。 — Please read through the distributed materials before the meeting.

question: 「気が付く」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
気が付く means 'to notice / realize' — to become aware of something.
気が付く (きがつく) is an idiomatic expression built from 気 (き, spirit / mind / awareness) + が (subject marker) + 付く (つく, to attach / come to). When your awareness 'attaches' to something, you notice it. This phrase covers two related meanings: noticing something with your senses (あ、財布 (さいふ) を忘れたと気が付いた = 'I noticed I had forgotten my wallet') and having a sudden realization (彼女 (かのじょ) が嘘 (うそ) をついていると気が付いた = 'I realized she was lying'). At N3, you also see the polite form 気が付く in the て-form: 気が付いて見ると (upon noticing…). A close variant is 気付く (きづく), written as one word — the meaning is identical. The phrase can also be used to say someone is considerate: 気が付く人 (a perceptive / attentive person).
✗ 'to forget' is 忘れる (わすれる). Forgetting and noticing are opposite in direction: one loses awareness, the other gains it.
✗ 'to ignore' is 無視する (むしする). Ignoring means deliberately not paying attention; 気が付く means you do become aware.
✗ 'to sleep' is 眠る (ねむる) or 寝る (ねる). Sleep has no connection to 気が付く. In fact, waking up from sleep can trigger 気が付く — you wake up and suddenly notice something.
例: 電車 (でんしゃ) を降 (お) りてから、定期券 (ていきけん) を忘 (わす) れたことに気 (き) が付 (つ) いた。 — After getting off the train, I realized I had forgotten my commuter pass.

question: 「口を出す」の意味はなんですか。
explanation:
口を出す means 'to interfere / to butt in' — inserting yourself into a matter that is not your business.
口を出す (くちをだす) is an idiomatic expression meaning 'to interfere,' 'to butt in,' or 'to meddle in someone else's affairs.' Literally it means 'to put one's mouth out' — inserting your voice into something.
